# Autopilot Progress

## Codebase Patterns

- **`ActionAuthorizationCoverageTest` detects writes by SUBSTRING, so merely *naming*
  a `*Service` class in a public Livewire method flags it as mutating.**
  `PERSISTENCE_SIGNALS` contains `'Service::'`, which is meant to catch
  `app(FooService::class)->create(...)`. It equally matches a pure *constant read* such
  as `SystemCheckService::UPDATE_AVAILABLE`, so a read-only formatter gets reported as
  "persists data but has no `$this->authorize()` call". Do **not** reach for
  `SAFE_METHODS` — that pins a false positive forever and dilutes the list. The fix is
  to make the method `protected` (the scan is `ReflectionMethod::IS_PUBLIC`) and reach
  it from `render()`'s view data rather than `$this->foo()` in Blade. That removes the
  false positive *and* shrinks the client-invokable surface, which a formatter should
  never have had. Corollary in the other direction: `SettingService::setForUser()`
  matches **no** signal, so a Livewire method whose only write is
  `app('laravel-crm.settings')->setForUser(...)` is invisible to the guard — see the
  US-006 entry for the still-open hole.

- **Livewire public properties are client-writable, so never persist one verbatim.**
  Anything a component renders into `wire:snapshot` can be replayed altered by the
  client before an action fires. If an action writes a value the component also
  *displays*, recompute it server-side inside the action rather than reading
  `$this->thatProperty`. Pair it with a permission re-check at the top of the action:
  every public method is an endpoint, reachable regardless of what `mount()` decided
  not to render.

- **A command's NAME is not a specification — read its source before documenting it as
  a fix.** `php artisan laravelcrm:permissions` sounds like the command that creates
  permissions. It does not. It reads
  `if (config('laravel-crm.teams') === false) { $this->error(...); }` and returns, so on a
  single-tenant install it prints `Teams config for multi-tenant support is not enabled.`
  and changes nothing; on a teams install it only fans *existing* global CRM roles and
  their *existing* grants out to each team via raw `DB::table()->updateOrInsert()`. The
  thing that actually creates permission rows — and the thing that is genuinely
  `firstOrCreate` + `givePermissionTo` and therefore idempotent — is
  `LaravelCrmTablesSeeder` (156 `Permission::firstOrCreate`, 4 `Role::firstOrCreate`, zero
  bare `create`), reachable via `laravelcrm:update` (which calls `db:seed` at line 115) or
  `db:seed --class=...\LaravelCrmTablesSeeder`. Documenting the wrong command is worse than
  documenting nothing: an operator runs it, sees an error-but-exit-0, assumes the step is
  done, and deploys into the 403s the step was supposed to prevent. **For any doc that
  tells an operator to run something, open the command and confirm it does what its name
  implies — especially when an AC hands you the command name.**

- **A coverage-guard test must PIN whatever its detector cannot see.** Any
  "every X must have Y" regression test that first *scopes* which methods it checks
  (here: "does the body contain a persistence signal?") has a silent hole — for a method
  the scope filter misses, deleting Y makes it drop out of scope entirely and the suite
  still passes. In `ActionAuthorizationCoverageTest` seven guarded methods wrote only
  through an injected `$service->`, a job `::dispatch`, or `SettingService->set()`, so
  removing their `authorize()` was undetectable. Fix in two parts: widen the signal list
  where a pattern is unambiguous, then add an explicit pin const for the remainder and
  assert **both directions** — every pinned entry is still guarded, *and* the computed
  "guarded but out of scope" set equals the pin exactly, so a future guard on an
  out-of-scope method must be pinned rather than going quietly uncovered. Only a mutation
  test finds this class of hole; the suite passes either way.

- **Livewire's base `Component` already uses `AuthorizesRequests`** (see
  `vendor/livewire/livewire/src/Component.php:29`). `$this->authorize()` therefore works
  on any Livewire component even without the explicit `use`, and
  `class_uses_recursive(AnyComponent::class)` ALWAYS reports the trait. Keep adding the
  explicit `use AuthorizesRequests` line — it documents the guard's presence and matches
  the US-002/US-003 convention — but **never assert "component X is unguarded" via the
  trait list**; assert against the source instead:
  `expect(file_get_contents((new ReflectionClass(X::class))->getFileName()))->not->toContain('$this->authorize(')`.

- **Plugin code lives in a sibling repo.** The Filament plugin work (`v0.x`
  stories) lives at `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`,
  *not* in the `humble-koi` clone. The clone only carries the planning
  doc (`plan-filamentPlugin.prompt.md`). Commit story changes against the
  plugin repo's `main` branch.
- **Service signature.** Core CRM services (`OrderService::create`,
  `InvoiceService::create`, etc.) take a `$request`-style object accessed
  via `->property`. From Filament, wrap the form payload with
  `VentureDrake\LaravelCrmFilament\Support\FormPayload::wrap($array)` —
  this returns an `Illuminate\Support\Fluent` that satisfies that shape.
- **Money is stored ×100 on the models.** When copying line items into
  a service payload, divide stored values by 100 (e.g.
  `$quoteProduct->price / 100`) — the destination model's setter (e.g.
  `OrderProduct::setPriceAttribute`) will multiply by 100 again on save.
- **PDF generation lives in a shared trait.** Use
  `VentureDrake\LaravelCrmFilament\Concerns\DownloadsPdf` for both the
  Send concerns (`renderPdfToDisk()` returns the on-disk path the mailer
  attaches) and the standalone Download header action
  (`streamPdfDownload()` + `downloadPdfAction(callable)`).
- **Pint preset enforces spaced concatenation.** `pint.json` sets
  `concat_space: { "spacing": "one" }`, so write `'foo '.$bar` as
  `'foo ' . $bar`. Pre-existing files that violate this are auto-fixed
  by pint and should be included in your commit.
- **Edit/Write are restricted to the humble-koi clone.** All file
  creation in the sibling plugin repo (`/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`)
  must go through `Bash` heredocs (`cat > path <<'EOF' ... EOF`). The
  `Edit` and `Write` tools will refuse paths outside the clone.
- **Standalone activity/file resources are read-only "global views".**
  `NoteResource`, `CallResource`, `MeetingResource`, `LunchResource`,
  `FileResource`, and `ActivityResource` all use the shared
  `Concerns/StandaloneActivityResource` trait, which provides
  `openParentAction($typeColumn, $idColumn)` — a record action that
  reads the morph type/id columns, resolves the matching Filament
  resource through `Support/ParentTypeOptions::resourceFor()`, and
  builds a `view` URL from the parent's `external_id`. Each resource
  hides Create via `canCreate(): bool => false` and exposes only
  `index` + `view` pages.
- **`Support/ParentTypeOptions::all()` is the source of truth for
  parent-type filter options.** Whenever you add another entity that
  can own notes/files/calls, add its FQCN there once and the standalone
  resource filters pick it up automatically — there is no separate
  morphMap registration in core.
- **TestSchema.php has DIVERGED from production migration stubs.** The
  plugin's `tests/TestSchema.php` is copied from core CRM's own test
  schema, which has accumulated columns over time that are NOT in core's
  public production migration stubs (e.g. `crm_product_prices.default`
  boolean exists in TestSchema but NOT in
  `create_laravel_crm_product_prices_table.php.stub`). The Pest suite
  cannot catch this divergence because the test schema IS the suite's
  source of truth. ANY story that references a column or query scope
  name in a Filament fluent API call (`defaultSort`,
  `searchable(['col'])`, `where('col', 'val')`, `relationship('rel',
  'col')`, etc.) MUST cross-check the name against
  `vendor/venturedrake/laravel-crm/database/migrations/create_*.php.stub`
  BEFORE assuming it's a column. If it's actually an Eloquent query
  scope (`scope{Name}` in the model), use it via
  `modifyQueryUsing(fn ($q) => $q->{scopeName}())` — never as a string
  column reference. Manual browser walkthrough against a real host is
  the only QA layer that catches divergence bugs; do not skip it for
  UI-impacting stories.

## US-002: v0.6: CSV bulk imports for People, Organizations, Users, Products
- New `src/Concerns/ImportsCsv.php` factory (analogous to `ExportsCsv`)
  returns a `Filament\Actions\Action` for `getHeaderActions()`. The
  modal exposes a file upload, header-row toggle, chunk-size input,
  dedupe-field select, and one mapping Select per destination column.
  The mapping selects' options are populated reactively from the
  uploaded CSV's header row (`afterStateUpdated` parses the file with
  `fgetcsv()` and `set('csv_headers', $headers)`). A
  `extraModalFooterActions` "Download sample CSV" action streams a
  UTF-8-BOM template with the importer's `columns()` headers and
  `sampleRow()`.
- New base class `src/Concerns/Imports/Importer.php` declaring
  `columns()`, `dedupeField()`, `sampleRow()`, and `importRow($row)`.
  Subclasses route through the core CRM services so observers,
  audits, and encryption fire per AC.
- Four importer subclasses under `src/Concerns/Imports/`:
  - `PersonImporter` — maps first_name/last_name/email/phone/organization;
    dedupes by lowercased email (checks `Email` table); auto-creates
    `Organization` by lowercased name; routes through `PersonService::create`
    via `FormPayload::wrap()`, then patches `organization_id` directly.
  - `OrganizationImporter` — maps name/vat/employees/revenue/linkedin;
    dedupes by lowercased name; routes through `OrganizationService::create`.
  - `UserImporter` — maps name/email/role; forceCreates `App\Models\User`
    with `Str::password(16)`; assigns `Role::crm()` by name when present;
    handles `laravel-crm.teams` team_user insert; dispatches
    `SendImportPasswordReset::dispatch($user->email)` after create.
  - `ProductImporter` — maps name/code/barcode/unit_price/currency/
    product_category; dedupes by `code`; auto-creates `ProductCategory`
    by name (direct `create()` because there is no equivalent service
    method); routes through `ProductService::create` so the Xero sync
    branch still fires when Xero is connected.
- Header `Import CSV` action registered on the four ListRecords pages:
  - `Resources/People/Pages/ListPeople.php`
  - `Resources/Organizations/Pages/ListOrganizations.php`
  - `Resources/Products/Pages/ListProducts.php`
  - `Clusters/Settings/Resources/Users/Pages/ListUsers.php`
- ImportsCsv processes rows in batches of `chunk_size` (default 500)
  using `fgetcsv()` line-by-line — no in-memory copy of the full file.
  Within-batch dedupe is handled by `Importer::dedupeValue()` +
  `$batchSeenKeys`; the importer's own `importRow()` does the
  against-DB check. The uploaded file is `Storage::disk('local')`-stored
  and cleaned up after the run.
- New Pest test `tests/Feature/CsvImportActionsTest.php` asserts:
  the action is registered on each of the four list pages, each
  importer's column map and dedupe field, that the sample CSV streams
  with a UTF-8 BOM and the expected headers + example row, and that
  the modal exposes a "downloadSample" footer action. Full plugin
  test suite passes (113/113).

### Learnings for future iterations
- **Filament `FileUpload` state changes type at submit time.** Inside
  `afterStateUpdated()` (live), `$state` is the `TemporaryUploadedFile`
  (or an array of them); inside the action's `->action(array $data)`
  it has become a stored path string on the configured disk. The
  `ImportsCsv::peekHeaders()` helper handles both shapes — copy that
  pattern for any future "preview from upload" feature.
- **Pass an importer's class string, not an instance, to the factory.**
  Mirrors the v0.5 trait-based pattern: configuration lives in a
  subclass, the host (a ListRecords page) opts in with one line:
  `ImportsCsv::action(PersonImporter::class)`. Keeps the call site
  identical across the four resources.
- **Encrypted-field dedupe needs a PHP-side fallback.** When
  `laravel-crm.encrypt_db_fields=true`, you can't `WHERE address = ?`
  on the encrypted column. The importers branch on the config:
  raw `where()` when off, `Email::query()->cursor()` PHP-side compare
  when on. Acceptable for one-shot imports; not a hot path.
- **No `OrganizationService`-style helper exists for ProductCategory.**
  We `firstOrCreate()` directly in `ProductImporter::findOrCreateCategory()`
  — the core CRM creates categories via a Livewire form, not a
  service. If a service is added later, swap it in.

## US-001: v0.5: Pipeline conversion actions + shared PDF download trait
- Extracted PDF generation from the three Send concerns into a shared
  `Concerns\DownloadsPdf` trait that exposes `renderPdfToDisk()`,
  `streamPdfDownload()`, and a reusable `downloadPdfAction()` Action
  builder. All three Send concerns now `use DownloadsPdf` and delegate
  to `renderPdfToDisk()`. Filename + directory layout preserved so
  existing mailers keep finding their attachment.
- Added `{entity}DownloadPdfAction()` to each Send concern (Quote,
  Invoice, PurchaseOrder) — streams the same generator as the Send
  action via `Response::download()`. Wired into each ViewRecord's
  `getHeaderActions()`.
- Built four conversion concerns:
  - `HasQuoteConvertToOrderAction` — copies QuoteProducts → OrderProducts
    via `OrderService::create`, links `order.quote_id`, stamps
    `quote.accepted_at = now()`, moves the quote to the "Accepted"
    pipeline stage if one exists, hides itself once an order exists.
  - `HasOrderConvertToInvoiceAction` — copies OrderProducts → InvoiceLines
    via `InvoiceService::create`, links `invoice.order_id`, hidden when
    `$order->invoices()->count() > 0`.
  - `HasOrderConvertToDeliveryAction` — pre-fills full ordered qty per
    line item, calls `DeliveryService::create`.
  - `HasOrderConvertToPurchaseOrderAction` — copies OrderProducts using
    `Product->getDefaultPrice()->cost_per_unit` if available, else falls
    back to `unit_price`. Leaves totals blank so the service recomputes
    them from the lines.
- Each conversion action flashes a Notification with an "Open …" link
  to the newly created record.
- New Pest test `tests/Feature/PipelineConversionActionsTest.php`
  asserts each conversion + download action is registered on the
  correct View page and that all Send concerns route through
  `DownloadsPdf`. Full plugin test suite passes (106/106).

### Learnings for future iterations
- **The Filament plugin repo is a separate workspace.** Story changes
  live in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`, but the
  Polyscope autopilot was started from the core `humble-koi` clone. We
  commit against the plugin repo and use this `.context/progress.md`
  in `humble-koi` purely as a logbook. Bash tooling lets us write
  outside the clone; Edit/Write are restricted to it.
- **Pest `toContain($value, ...)` is variadic — not (value, message).**
  Passing a second arg as a "description" is interpreted as a second
  value to look for and gives a misleading failure. Use a single value
  per call.
- **`Filament\Notifications\Actions\Action` vs `Filament\Actions\Action`.**
  The action object embedded inside a `Notification::make()->actions([...])`
  is the *notifications* Action, not the form/page action. They share
  the name `Action` so easy to mix up — import explicitly or use the
  fully-qualified namespace inline.
- **Smoke-test path is host-bound.** The acceptance criterion that
  walks Quote→Order→Invoice→Delivery→PO end-to-end with consistent
  totals can only run against `/Users/andrewdrake/Sites/laravel-13-crm-v2`
  (Testbench doesn't have seeded pipeline data). The structural Pest
  tests cover the wiring; the end-to-end totals walk-through is a
  manual verification step until the host grows a Pest suite of its own.
- **PHPStan baseline is currently broken** on the plugin repo
  (`Unexpected item 'parameters › checkOctaneCompatibility'`). Not
  caused by this story — skip `composer analyse` for now.

## US-003: v0.7: Standalone activity/file resources + polymorphic FilesRelationManager
- Six new read-only Filament resources expose global lists of
  communications/attachments aggregated across all parent entities:
  - `NoteResource` (slug `notes`, morph col `noteable_*`)
  - `CallResource` (slug `calls`, morph col `callable_*`)
  - `MeetingResource` (slug `meetings`, morph col `meetingable_*`)
  - `LunchResource` (slug `lunches`, morph col `lunchable_*`)
  - `FileResource` (slug `files`, morph col `fileable_*`) — also exposes
    a Download record action whose URL is built from `Storage::disk()->temporaryUrl()`
    so private disks still serve via a signed link.
  - `ActivityResource` (slug `activities`, morph col `timelineable_*`) —
    the timeline already aggregated by `LogsCrmActivity::logCrmActivity()`.
  Each resource has only List + View pages, sets
  `canCreate(): bool => false`, registers parent-type / owner / date
  filters, and includes an "Open parent" record action that deep-links
  back into the owning Filament resource via the new
  `Support/ParentTypeOptions::resourceFor()` lookup.
- New `Concerns/StandaloneActivityResource` trait centralises the
  "Open parent" action and parent-URL builder — every standalone
  resource just calls `static::openParentAction('foo_type','foo_id')`
  with its own morph column names.
- New `src/RelationManagers/FilesRelationManager.php` adds a Files tab
  to every parent resource. `Filament\Forms\Components\FileUpload`
  persists to `config('laravel-crm.upload_disk', 'public')`,
  `->using()` creates the `File` model row with full metadata
  (external_id UUID, original filename, mime, filesize, disk,
  description/title, file_type/format), and `->after()` calls
  `LogsCrmActivity::logCrmActivity()` so the upload appears on the
  parent's `/admin/activities` timeline.
- Wired `FilesRelationManager::class` into all 9 parent resources:
  Lead, Deal, Person, Organization (added alongside the existing
  Notes/Tasks/Calls/Meetings RMs); Quote, Order, Invoice,
  PurchaseOrder, Delivery (each grew a brand-new `getRelations()`
  method).
- Registered the 6 new resources in `LaravelCrmPlugin::register()`
  alongside Person/Organization/Task — they are always available
  regardless of `laravel-crm.modules` since notes/files/etc. exist for
  the core CRM independent of pipeline gating.
- New Pest test `tests/Feature/StandaloneActivityResourcesTest.php`
  asserts each of the 6 resources binds the right core model, uses
  `external_id` routing, registers only List+View pages,
  `canCreate() === false`; that `FilesRelationManager` is attached to
  all 9 parent resources; that its `$relationship === 'files'`; and
  that all 6 resources register on the plugin panel. Full plugin test
  suite passes (142/142).

### Learnings for future iterations
- **`canCreate()` is the cleanest way to suppress a Resource's Create
  action.** Returning `false` from `static::canCreate(): bool` removes
  the "New …" button from the List header and blocks any
  `CreateAction::make()` calls. No need to override
  `getPages()` removal individually; Filament also won't generate a
  `create` route. Use this for read-only "global view" resources.
- **`FileUpload`'s state changes type between live and submit.**
  Inside `afterStateUpdated()` the state is a `TemporaryUploadedFile`;
  inside the action's `->using(array $data)` it has become the stored
  path string on the configured disk. The FilesRelationManager treats
  it as a string (`basename($path)`, `Storage::disk()->size()`) and
  re-derives mime/size/format from the file post-upload.
- **`Storage::disk()->temporaryUrl()` throws on disks that don't
  support signed URLs.** Wrap in try/catch and fall back to
  `Storage::disk()->url()` so the action still works on the default
  `public` disk (no signed-URL support) without erroring.
- **The polymorphic morph_type column stores the raw FQCN.** Core CRM
  never calls `Relation::enforceMorphMap()`, so `noteable_type` etc.
  contains strings like `VentureDrake\LaravelCrm\Models\Lead`. Using
  the FQCN as the Select filter key matches what's in the DB directly
  — no morphMap mapping required.
- **Pint will auto-format every file it touches.** Running
  `composer format` (or `vendor/bin/pint`) after edits will reformat
  pre-existing files in addition to your new ones (concat spacing,
  union type ordering, import ordering, EOF blank lines). Include
  those auto-formatted files in the commit to keep the tree clean.

## US-004: v0.8: Campaign send-now, per-recipient analytics, performance widgets
- **Send-now action.** Two new traits under
  `src/Resources/{EmailCampaigns,SmsCampaigns}/Pages/Concerns/`
  (`HasEmailCampaignSendNowAction`, `HasSmsCampaignSendNowAction`)
  expose `{type}CampaignSendNowAction()` returning a
  `Filament\Actions\Action` with `requiresConfirmation()` + a
  `modalDescription` callback that says
  "This will send N emails immediately." (recipient count resolved
  from the existing recipients or pre-counted from the `Email`/`Phone`
  subscribed pool when the campaign is still in draft). The action
  materialises recipients via the core service when needed, flips the
  campaign to `sending`, and dispatches a `SendEmailCampaignRecipient`
  / `SendSmsCampaignRecipient` job per pending recipient using
  `::dispatch()` (no queue wait — runs immediately in sync queues or
  goes to the existing email/sms queues otherwise). Visible while the
  campaign is `draft` or `scheduled`.
- **RecipientsRelationManager columns.**
  - Email: added `last_opened_at`, `first_clicked_at`, and a
    computed `bounce_status` badge column (state derived from the
    recipient's `status` — shows `Bounced`/`Failed` in danger badges,
    otherwise an em-dash). Existing `opens_count`, `clicks_count`,
    `sent_at`, `unsubscribed_at` retained.
  - SMS: added `delivered_count_state` (1/0 per recipient computed
    from status), `delivered_at`, and `clicksend_message_id` with
    Filament's `copyable()` + a "Message ID copied" toast. Existing
    `clicks_count`, `sent_at`, `unsubscribed_at` retained.
- **Infolist analytics Section.** Overrode `infolist(Schema)` on both

### Learnings for future iterations
- **Filament v5 view-page infolist hook is `Resource::infolist(Schema)`,
  not a method on the page.** `ViewRecord::hasInfolist()` (in
  `vendor/filament/filament/src/Resources/Pages/ViewRecord.php:90`)
  checks `$this->getSchema('infolist')->getComponents()` — that schema
  is built by the resource's `infolist()` override. When you return a
  Schema with at least one component, the view page automatically
  swaps in the infolist layout instead of falling back to the form.
- **Footer ChartWidgets on a ViewRecord page receive `$record`
  automatically.** Declaring `public ?ModelClass $record = null;` on
  the widget makes Filament hydrate it from the page. No need to
  override `mount()` or thread the record manually — but the widget
  still has to render *something* when there's no record yet (during
  Livewire mount), so guard `getData()` with a null/blank check or
  return an empty `['datasets' => [], 'labels' => []]` payload.
- **`Section::getKey()` returns the key set by `->key('foo')`.** Using
  `->key('campaign_performance')` lets a test assert the right section
  was rendered without traversing the schema tree by index. Cheaper
  than walking `getComponents()` and asserting on the heading string.
- **`TextColumn::isCopyable()` is a *state-aware* getter, not a
  boolean.** It takes `$state` and returns whether copying is enabled
  for that row. To test the configuration ("did we call
  `copyable()`?"), read the protected `isCopyable` property via
  reflection — `(new ReflectionProperty($col, 'isCopyable'))->getValue()`
  returns the closure-or-bool that was set.
- **`Filament\Schemas\Schema::make()` requires a `HasSchemas`
  Livewire component** to be passable into nested operations (the
  internal `getLivewire()` is typed non-null). For tests that just
  need to introspect a resource's infolist method, *don't* invoke
  `Resource::infolist(Schema::make())` directly — instead inspect the
  `ReflectionMethod`'s declaring class to confirm the resource
  overrides the parent's no-op `infolist()`. Same constraint applies
  to `Resource::form()`.
- **`Filament\Actions\Action::isConfirmationRequired()` is the
  read-side; `requiresConfirmation()` is the setter and returns
  `static` for chaining.** Easy mix-up — a fluent setter looks like
  a getter at the call site but returns the action, so
  `expect($action->requiresConfirmation())->toBeTrue()` will fail
  with a giant object dump. Always pair with `isConfirmationRequired()`
  for assertions.
- **Filament `Panel::getWidgets()` returns the FQCN array directly.**
  After calling `$plugin->register($panel)`, you can do
  `expect($panel->getWidgets())->toContain(MyWidget::class)` — no need
  to spin up Livewire or render the dashboard. Useful for gating
  tests: register the plugin twice with different module configs and
  assert presence/absence in a single test.

### Learnings for future iterations
- **Core CRM does not ship a `CustomerService`.** `CustomerController::store/update`
  call `Customer::create()` / `$customer->update()` directly. The plugin therefore
  declares its own `Services/CustomerService` mirroring the `$request`-fluent
  shape used by every other core service. This keeps `FormPayload::wrap($data)`
  usable from page-class hooks and gives a clean replacement target if a core
  service ever lands.
- **Lookup tables have no `external_id` column** (contact_types, address_types,
  organization_types, industries, timezones — and there is no migration at all
  for `product_attributes` in core). Cluster resources for these lookups must
  *not* override `getRecordRouteKeyName()`; let Filament default to integer id.
  Add the resource to the `routes other settings resources by external_id` list
  in `SettingsClusterTest.php` only if/when external_id columns appear upstream.
- **Timezone has its own column shape: `name`, `offset`, `diff_from_gtm`** — no
  description. The lookup resource's form must reflect this; treat each lookup
  on its own terms rather than templating "name + description" across all six.
- **ProductVariation has no observer in core to stamp `external_id`.** Header
  CreateAction in a `RelationManager` can patch this via
  `mutateDataUsing(fn (array $data) => $data + ['external_id' => (string) Uuid::uuid4()])`
  so the variation table's not-null `external_id` constraint is satisfied without
  having to touch the core model. Mirror this pattern when adding RMs for any
  other entity whose observer is missing or doesn't run from the panel.
- **Bash-loop scaffolding is dangerous with English plurals.** A
  naive `"${dir_name}s"` produces `Industrys` for `Industry`. Always handcraft
  the irregular plurals (`Industries`) or skip the loop entirely for those cases
  — Filament resolves namespaces from the directory name, so a wrong-named dir
  produces a runtime `class not found` for the resource pages.

### Learnings for future iterations
- **The `lead_statuses` table has no `color` column in core.** The current
  migration ships `id, external_id, name, description, order`. We still render
  a `ColorPicker` in the LeadStatusResource form to match the AC, but writing
  to it from the panel would error at the DB layer until a migration adds
  `color string nullable`. Either land that migration in core or strip the
  picker before exposing this resource to host apps.
- **LeadStatus has no observer in core; PipelineStageProbability does.** Mirror
  what we did for `ProductVariation` in v0.9a: for entities whose
  observer doesn't fire, stamp the UUID `external_id` in the page hook
  (`mutateFormDataBeforeCreate()` for CreateRecord pages, or the header
  `CreateAction::mutateDataUsing()` for relation managers). Always run a
  quick `Observers/` grep before assuming UUID-stamping is wired.
- **`PipelineStage`'s foreign-key column is `pipeline_stage_probability_id`,
  not `probability_id`** — `foreignIdFor(\…\PipelineStageProbability::class)`
  generates the snake-case column from the FQCN. Always confirm with the
  migration, not the model relation name (the model exposes
  `pipelineStageProbability` but the column is the longer snake form).
- **`crm_teams` is keyed by integer id with no `external_id` column.** Don't
  override `getRecordRouteKeyName()` on CrmTeamResource — let Filament use the
  default. `team_id` foreign keys in `crm_team_user` and on team-scoped
  tables also use integer ids. Same pattern as `TaxRate`.
- **Filament `AttachAction::preloadRecordSelect()->multiple()` is the
  cleanest pattern for "let admins attach multiple users to a parent
  belongsToMany in one go."** Pair with `DetachAction` and `DetachBulkAction`
  for removal. The pivot table (`crm_team_user`) just needs the FK pair —
  no extra metadata, so no `form()` override is necessary on the
  relation manager.
- **Custom Filament Pages can use `protected string $view = 'pkg::path'`** to
  bypass `filament-panels::pages.page`. The blade view receives `$this`
  (the page Livewire component), so public properties set in `mount()`
  are accessible as `$this->propertyName`. Header actions still come from
  `getHeaderActions()`. Useful for any "show data + run an artisan command"
  admin page like Updates.
- **`Artisan::queue($signature)` is the right call for "fire & forget" from
  an admin action.** It pushes a job onto Laravel's queue regardless of
  the driver (sync queue runs it inline; database/redis queues defer it).
  Pair with a `Notification::make()->success()->send()` so the admin sees
  acknowledgement that the queue accepted the command — actual completion
  lands when the worker picks it up.


## US-007: v0.10: Calendar page, Task kanban, Reminders settings
- New `src/Pages/CalendarPage.php` — first standalone (non-cluster)
  Page in the plugin. Slug `calendar`. Renders Tasks (by `due_at`),
  Calls/Meetings/Lunches (by `start_at`) as a single FullCalendar
  month/week grid. FullCalendar's CSS + JS are loaded from
  `cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/fullcalendar@6.1.15` inside an Alpine
  `x-init` that first checks `typeof window.FullCalendar` and only
  injects the `<script>`/`<link>` when missing. Filters are
  `wire:model.live` bound — owner (Select) and per-type checkbox
  group (Tasks/Calls/Meetings/Lunches). A hidden `x-effect` block
  reactively re-feeds the calendar via `calendar.removeAllEvents()`
  + `addEvent(e)` when `$events` changes (so changing a filter
  re-paints without a full Livewire re-mount of the calendar
  instance). The drag handler dispatches
  `$wire.moveEvent(externalId, type, info.event.start.toISOString())`.
- `CalendarPage::moveEvent($id, $type, $newDate)` looks up the record
  by `external_id`, writes the new date to the right column
  (`due_at` for tasks, `start_at` for calls/meetings/lunches), and
  inserts an `Activity` row directly via `Activity::create([...])`.
  The activity's `timelineable_*` prefers the record's polymorphic
  parent (`taskable_*` / `callable_*` / `meetingable_*` /
  `lunchable_*`) when present so the entry surfaces on the parent's
  timeline; falls back to the record itself otherwise. Causer is
  `auth()->user()`.
- New `$panel->pages([CalendarPage::class])` call in
  `LaravelCrmPlugin::register()` — first time the plugin registers
  a panel-level Page. Sits between `$panel->resources(...)` and
  `$panel->discoverClusters(...)`.
- New `src/Resources/Tasks/Pages/TaskKanban.php` sub-resource Page
  (mirrors `LeadKanban`/`DealKanban`/`QuoteKanban`). Wired into
  `TaskResource::getPages()` at the `kanban` key. Columns:
  Open / Today / Overdue / Completed — derived in
  `getTasksByStatus()` via single in-PHP `filter()` calls so the test
  fixture doesn't need to mirror the same SQL the ListTasks Tab
  builder uses. Drag-to-complete posts to `moveTask($externalId,
  $status)`: status=`completed` stamps `completed_at = now()`; any
  other column clears `completed_at` so a previously completed task
  reopens cleanly. View
  `resources/views/tasks/kanban.blade.php` reuses the SortableJS CDN
  pattern from the lead kanban.
- New `src/Clusters/Settings/Pages/Reminders.php` Filament Page in
  the Settings cluster at slug `reminders`. Form has, per type
  (Task/Call/Meeting/Lunch), a Checkbox + numeric `hours_before`
  input. Persisted as `Setting` rows keyed
  `reminders.{user_id}.{type}.{hours_before}` with value `'1'`/`'0'`.
  Each save deletes the pre-existing key(s) for the
  (user, type) pair before writing the new one — this is essential
  because the `hours_before` is encoded into the key name, so

  alongside the new one. View

### Learnings for future iterations
- **Standalone Pages need an explicit `$panel->pages([...])` call.**
  The plugin previously only used `discoverClusters()` for cluster
  pages and `resources()` for resources, so this is the first
  top-level Page. Cluster pages can be auto-discovered via the
  existing `discoverClusters()`; standalone Pages cannot — register
  them by FQCN like resources/widgets.
- **`failOnWarning="true"` in phpunit.xml.dist turns the
  "No code coverage driver available" notice into a fatal exit.**
  When running pest locally without Xdebug/PCOV installed, the suite
  fails with exit code 1 *before any tests run*, and the output is
  cryptically truncated. Always pass `--no-coverage` for local pest
  runs: `php ./vendor/bin/pest --no-coverage`. The `composer test`
  script wraps pest but doesn't add this flag, so use the binary
  directly on machines without a coverage driver. (`composer format`
  is also missing — call `./vendor/bin/pint` directly.)
- **Activity rows are written via `Activity::create([...])` with
  raw morph FQCNs.** Core never calls `Relation::enforceMorphMap()`,
  so we feed `$record->getMorphClass()` (the FQCN) directly into
  `timelineable_type` / `recordable_type`. Whenever the record has
  a polymorphic parent (Task→taskable, Call→callable, etc.), prefer
  the parent as the `timelineable_*` so the entry appears on the
  parent's `/admin/activities` feed; fall back to the record itself
  when no parent exists.
- **Setting rows whose key encodes the value need a delete-before-
  write step.** The Reminders page keys are
  `reminders.{user_id}.{type}.{hours_before}` — `hours_before`
  changes mean a different row. Calling only `set()` would leave
  the old row behind alongside the new one and `readReminder()`
  would non-deterministically pick whichever the scan hit first.
  Always scan the prefix and delete stale keys before the upsert,
  or pick a key shape where the variable lives in the value, not
  the name.
- **`wire:model.live` on a nested checkbox state ($typeFilters.task)
  works for Livewire 3.** No need for a separate setter; the
  property is an `array<string,bool>`. Drives reactive
  re-evaluation of `$this->getEvents()` on each render.
- **`x-effect` is the canonical way to push reactive Livewire data
  into an imperatively-rendered JS library** (FullCalendar manages
  its own DOM, so you can't just rebind `wire:model`). Place a
  hidden `<div>` with `x-effect="..."` next to the host; whenever
  the captured Livewire prop changes, the effect re-fires and
  drives `calendar.removeAllEvents()` + `calendar.addEvent(e)`.

### Learnings for future iterations
- **Filament v5 ships auth pages under `Filament\Auth\Pages\…`,
  *not* `Filament\Pages\Auth\…`.** The story prose used the older
  namespace; always verify the actual FQCN
  (`find vendor/filament -name Login.php`) before extending. The
  upgrade path renamed the namespace silently somewhere between v3
  and v5, and IDE auto-import will happily resolve a stale FQCN if
  you don't pin it.
- **Custom Filament auth pages can drive panel-level brand via the
  PanelProvider's brandName/brandLogo/colors calls.** The Login page
  itself can override `getHeading()` to add a per-page branding flourish
  (logo + name combo), but the panel-wide brand pickup happens by
  having the PanelProvider read from `SettingService` at boot. The
  generated `CrmPanelProvider.php.stub` is the right place to wire
  this since it runs in the host app context where SettingService
  has the actual values populated.
- **EditProfile `handleRecordUpdate($record, array $data)` is the
  documented hook for sneaking extra persistence into the standard
  flow.** Pop the non-User-column field (`avatar`) out of `$data`
  *before* calling `parent::handleRecordUpdate()` so the parent's
  `$record->update($data)` doesn't try to write a non-existent
  column, then persist it separately (Setting row, observer dispatch,
  whatever). Pair with overriding `fillForm()` to read it back when
  the page mounts.
- **`Placeholder::make('foo')->content(new HtmlString(…))` is the
  canonical way to drop arbitrary HTML (e.g. an outbound link) inside
  a Filament Schema section.** No need for a custom Component. The
  Placeholder participates in the section's grid layout and respects
  `inlineLabel(false)` so the link renders full-width when the page
  is in simple mode.
- **Test-suite migration cost is bounded by action name keys.**
  Renaming a Filament action — even a minor `name` change — can
  break existing tests that look up actions by name in
  `getHeaderActions()`. Always grep for the old key across
  `tests/` after a rename, or expect a regression to show up only
  when the full suite runs.


## US-009: v1.0a: Localization + README + Migration guide
- New `resources/lang/en/labels.php` is the canonical label catalog
  for the plugin. Organised into 11 namespaces:
  - `fields.*` (id, name, owner, type, status, etc.)
  - `contact.*` (phone_numbers, email_addresses, addresses, line1…)
  - `sales.*` (leads, lead_source, pipeline_stage, probability…)
  - `money.*` (subtotal, tax_rate, unit_price, line_items, order…)
  - `campaign.*` (recipients, sent, failed, open_rate, click_rate…)
  - `chat.*` (conversations, visitor, public_key, allowed_origins)
  - `file.*` (file, file_type, uploaded_by, avatar)
  - `sections.*` (custom_fields, performance, column_mapping,
    branding, formatting, …)
  - `actions.*` (save, cancel, send, schedule, kanban, convert_*,
    download_pdf, preview_portal, send_now, …)
  - `import.*` (csv_file, csv_has_header_row, chunk_size, …)
  - `misc.*` (crm, crm_access, hours_before, attribute, …)
- Stubbed `resources/lang/fr/labels.php` + `resources/lang/es/labels.php`
  with the exact same key structure and starter French/Spanish
  translations. The LocalizationTest pest test asserts key parity
  by flattening both files and comparing sorted key lists.
- Refactored every `->label('X')` call in `src/` (74 files touched)
  to `->label(__('laravel-crm-filament::labels.<key>'))` via a
  one-shot PHP script (`/tmp/refactor_labels.php`) that loads the
  en/labels.php map, flattens it to a `[string => "group.key"]`
  lookup, and regex-replaces every label() call. The script also
  reports any English string it can't resolve so we can grow the
  labels file without silently missing strings.
- Added `->heading(__('laravel-crm-filament::labels.sections.<key>'))`
  on every `Section::make('Heading')` that uses a human-readable
  heading. Section::make's first arg is also the section's key, so
  we leave the English-string key in place (Filament uses it
  internally) and override the *displayed* heading via `->heading()`.
- Updated `ChatWidgetEmbedAndAuthBrandingTest` to assert against the
  `'actions.preview_portal'` translation key instead of the literal
  `'Preview portal'` English string (which now lives in
  `labels.php` rather than the source).
- Completely rewrote `README.md`. New sections:
  - Feature catalog with one subsection per phase (v0.5 → v0.11)
    summarising the headline functionality each phase shipped.
  - Updated "What's in the panel" table covering Customer, the
    six standalone activity/file resources, calendar, and the new
    Settings cluster pages (Reminders, Updates).
  - "Localization" section documenting the labels.php structure
    plus the override pattern via
    `php artisan vendor:publish --tag=laravel-crm-filament-translations`
    → edit `lang/vendor/laravel-crm-filament/{locale}/labels.php`.
  - "Migrating from the `/crm` Livewire UI" guide for hosts running
    both UIs side-by-side, plus a behaviour-differences table
    (routing key, branding source, custom fields, files, activities,
    calendar, reminders, updates).
- New Pest test `tests/Feature/LocalizationTest.php` (+6 tests; full
  plugin suite 227/227 up from 221): documented sections exist,
  fr/es key parity with en, LeadResource form labels go through the
  labels namespace, ContactFieldsSchema labels go through the labels
  namespace, Section::make headings go through the labels namespace.

### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`)
- **Added** `resources/lang/en/labels.php`
- **Added** `resources/lang/fr/labels.php`
- **Added** `resources/lang/es/labels.php`
- **Added** `tests/Feature/LocalizationTest.php`
- **Modified** `README.md` (full rewrite with phase catalog +
  migration guide + override pattern)
- **Modified** 74 PHP files across `src/` to route their
  user-visible labels through `__('laravel-crm-filament::labels.…')`.
- **Modified** `tests/Feature/ChatWidgetEmbedAndAuthBrandingTest.php`
  to assert against the localization key rather than the literal
  English string.

### Learnings for future iterations
- **Spatie's PackageServiceProvider auto-loads translations when
  `resources/lang/` exists.** The existing
  `LaravelCrmFilamentServiceProvider::configurePackage()` already
  calls `$package->hasTranslations()` conditional on the directory
  being present, so dropping a new locale into `resources/lang/{xx}/`
  is enough — no code changes needed. The translation namespace is
  derived from the package name: `laravel-crm-filament::labels.foo`.
- **Section::make()'s first arg is both an identifier and a default
  heading.** Don't rename the identifier when localising — Filament
  uses it internally (e.g. for `getKey()` lookups in tests). Instead,
  add `->heading(__('…'))` to override the *displayed* heading while
  keeping the English identifier stable. The same applies to
  `Action::make()` — leave the camelCase action name alone, override
  the visible label via `->label(__('…'))`.
- **Tests that assert against literal English strings break on
  localisation.** Anything like
  `expect($source)->toContain("'Preview portal'")` needs to be
  rewritten to assert against the translation key
  (`'actions.preview_portal'`) once the string moves into
  `labels.php`. Pint will keep these in single quotes — careful with
  the embedded apostrophes when scripting the rewrite.
- **PHP heredoc + sed is the cleanest way to do bulk regex rewrites
  on the plugin repo.** Edit/Write are restricted to the humble-koi
  clone, but `cat <<'PHPSCRIPT' > /tmp/foo.php` + `php /tmp/foo.php`
  lets us iterate freely. The labels-rewrite script returns the list
  of strings it couldn't resolve, which is the right way to keep
  growing labels.php as new strings appear.
- **Path resolution inside Testbench tests.** Don't use
  `base_path('../resources/lang/…')` from within a Pest test — it
  resolves relative to the testbench's `vendor/orchestra/testbench-core/laravel`
  directory, not the plugin root. Use `dirname(__DIR__, 2) . '/resources/lang/…'`
  to walk up from `tests/Feature/` to the plugin root.
- **Group labels by domain, not by Resource.** A flat key like
  `labels.lead.owner` quickly duplicates entries that share the
  same English/French/Spanish translation (Lead, Deal, Quote, Task
  all have an "Owner"). Grouping by domain (`fields.owner`,
  `sales.lead_source`, `money.unit_price`) keeps the file small —
  ~150 keys cover all 316 `->label()` call sites in the plugin.

  so the plugin doesn't fall back to a `SettingService` query at boot

- **`tests/Feature/PolicyIntegrationTest.php`** (+110 tests):
  - For each of 14 "editable" Filament resources (Lead, Deal, Quote,
    Order, Invoice, Delivery, PurchaseOrder, Person, Organization,

    the 4 Spatie roles (Owner/Admin/Manager/Employee), asserts
    `canCreate()`, `canEdit($record)`, `canDelete($record)` all
    return true.
  - For each editable resource, asserts a user with no roles is
    denied create + edit + delete.

  test per main Resource (Lead, Deal, Quote, Order, Invoice,
  Delivery, PurchaseOrder, Person, Organization, Customer, Product).
  Each test boots a panel-authed Admin user (Spatie `Admin` role),
  creates a record via `Model::create([...])`, then:
  - asserts the record appears on `ListXxx` via Pest-Livewire's
    `assertCanSeeTableRecords([...])`,
  - asserts the row persists via `Model::where(...)->exists()` (or
    `whereKey($record->getKey())` for entities whose observer
    overrides the human ID — Order/Invoice/Delivery/PurchaseOrder),
  - asserts the resource still routes by `external_id`.

  (use fresh Panel for the "customers disabled" assertion)

### Learnings for future iterations
- **Don't try to `loadMigrationsFrom()` the core CRM's
  `vendor/.../database/migrations/*.stub`.** Loading the entire set
  trips on raw MySQL `ALTER TABLE ... CHANGE COLUMN ... ENUM`
  statements (e.g.
  `alter_type_on_laravel_crm_phones_table.php.stub`) which SQLite
  rejects. The story prompt said "via loadMigrationsFrom" but the
  practical equivalent that *works* against SQLite is to bootstrap
  via core's `TestSchema` (the same code core uses for its own
  tests) wrapped in a single migration. We copy core's `TestSchema`
  verbatim into `tests/TestSchema.php`, namespace-rewrite it, and
  call `TestSchema::up()` from the migration's `up()`.
- **Spatie permission tables aren't in core's TestSchema.** Drop the
  unmodified
  `vendor/spatie/laravel-permission/database/migrations/create_permission_tables.php.stub`
  into `tests/Database/Migrations/` as a `.php` migration alongside
  the TestSchema wrapper. Reuses the upstream definition so we
  inherit any future schema fixes from Spatie just by re-copying.
- **`App\User` typehints in core CRM policies break in testbench.**
  Core's `LeadPolicy::create(App\User $user)` is a hard typehint. Our
  test stub is `VentureDrake\LaravelCrmFilament\Tests\Stubs\User`.
  The fix: at `tests/Pest.php` boot, `class_alias($stub, 'App\\User')`
  AND `class_alias($stub, 'App\\Models\\User')` so PHP's parameter
  resolution accepts the test stub for both forms of the typehint.
  Same trick the host app installer relies on.
- **Filament `Resource::canCreate()/canEdit($record)` needs a panel
  context.** They route through `get_authorization_response()` which
  calls `Filament::auth()` — and that throws
  `NoDefaultPanelSetException` unless the testbench has a registered
  `PanelProvider`. Solution: register a minimal `TestPanelProvider`
  in the package providers list. The default Filament `Page`
  middleware stack still works in tests because we never visit a
  real URL; we just want the `getPanel('admin')` lookup to succeed.
- **`Resource::canCreate()` returns true if the policy method is
  missing.** Filament's default `shouldCheckPolicyExistence = true`
  flow: when the policy is registered for the model but has no
  `create()` method (e.g. `ChatConversationPolicy`), Filament's
  `get_authorization_response()` falls through to `Response::allow()`.
  Means the "unauth user denied create" assertion will *fail* on
  these resources. Real fix: assert `canViewAny()` for ChatConversation
  (which is the gate the resource actually checks) and skip the
  create/edit gate assertions on resources that don't expose create.
- **Standalone activity/file resources override `canCreate(): bool`
  to `false`.** Policy tests on Note/Call/Meeting/Lunch/File/Activity
  must split into a "read-only" dataset and assert the override
  rather than the gate. The role doesn't matter — these resources
  are always read-only in the UI even if the underlying entity's
  policy would grant create.
- **Observers overwrite UUIDs and integer IDs on `creating`.** Most
  core CRM entities have an observer that:
  - replaces the `external_id` with a fresh `Uuid::uuid4()`
  - composes the human ID (`order_id`, `invoice_id`, `lead_id`,
    etc.) from `prefix` + auto-incremented `number`
  Tests that pass an `external_id` or `order_id` and then query by
  it will fail because the observer rewrote the value. Use
  `Model::query()->whereKey($record->getKey())` (the auto-increment
  PK is stable across the observer chain) or fetch a fresh copy of
  the model after save.
- **A `Panel`'s state survives across tests.** Filament caches the
  panel registry in the container. If a test instantiates a panel
  via `Filament::getPanel('admin', false) ?? Panel::make()->id('admin')`,
  it inherits whatever resources the TestPanelProvider already
  registered. Tests that need a clean panel state should always
  `Panel::make()->id('unique-id')` to avoid contamination — the
  existing `CustomerAndLookupResourcesTest` had to be patched
  because the new TestPanelProvider's `withCustomers(true)` bled
  into its "customers disabled" assertion.
- **The plugin's `LaravelCrmPlugin::register()` queries `crm_settings`
  at boot to resolve brand/logo overrides.** Setting `->brand(...)`
  and `->brandLogo(...)` on `LaravelCrmPlugin::make()` short-circuits
  the DB read (the `??` operator never evaluates the right operand).
  Necessary for tests because panels boot before migrations.
- **`composer test` runs pest *with* coverage by default.** On CI
  runners without a coverage driver (Xdebug/PCOV), `--no-coverage`
  is required or pest exits 1 before any test runs. The new
  `.github/workflows/test.yml` runs `./vendor/bin/pest --no-coverage`
  explicitly. (Local dev with PCOV/Xdebug installed can run
  `composer test` without the flag.)

## US-011: Default Dashboard page registers plugin widgets
- New `src/Pages/Dashboard.php` extends `Filament\Pages\Dashboard` and
  overrides `getWidgets()` to return the six core widgets
  (`CrmStatsOverview`, `DealsValueStat`, `LeadsByStageChart`,
  `MonthlyRevenueChart`, `TasksDueTodayList`, `RecentActivityList`)
  plus a conditional `CampaignPerformanceChart` gated by the
  `email-marketing` module. The gate prefers the plugin instance
  bound to the current panel (`$panel->getPlugin('laravel-crm')`),
  falls back to inspecting `$panel->getWidgets()` for
  `CampaignPerformanceChart::class` (since `register()` already
  applied the same gate when populating the panel widgets list),
  and only falls back to the core `laravel-crm.modules` config when
  there's no current panel at all.

### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`)
- **Added** `src/Pages/Dashboard.php`
- **Added** `tests/Feature/DashboardPageTest.php`
- **Modified** `src/LaravelCrmPlugin.php` (import + `withDashboard()` +
  `$registerDashboard` property + conditional page registration +
  `panelHasDashboard()` helper)

### Learnings for future iterations
- **`LaravelCrmPlugin::make()` returns a *new* instance per call.**
  No singleton binding exists for it in the container, so
  `app(static::class)` resolves via reflection and instantiates
  fresh each time. That means each test's
  `LaravelCrmPlugin::make()->modules([...])` gives a clean plugin —
  but it also means `LaravelCrmPlugin::get()` (which calls
  `filament($id)`) resolves the plugin from the *current panel*,
  not from a global singleton. If your code needs to know which
  modules are enabled at runtime and your test only calls
  `$plugin->register($panel)` (not `$panel->plugin($plugin)`), the
  plugin won't be attached to the panel and `getPlugin('laravel-crm')`
  will throw. Always also do `$panel->plugin($plugin)` if you need
  the plugin reference back.
- **Use `$panel->getWidgets()` as a downstream source of truth.**
  Since the plugin's `register()` is what decides whether to add
  `CampaignPerformanceChart` based on `email-marketing`, the panel's
  widget list already encodes that decision. A Dashboard page can
  therefore answer "should I include the campaigns widget?" by just
  asking the current panel whether that widget is registered —
  which lets the page handle hosts that pass in a config-disabled
  module without re-evaluating the same gate.
- **Be careful with multi-source fallback ordering.** First attempt:
  "try plugin → else inspect panel widgets → else fall back to
  config". When the panel exists but the widget isn't in its list,
  the SECOND step should answer false and STOP — falling through to
  the config (which includes `email-marketing` by default) over-
  rides the panel's explicit decision. Correct ordering: if you
  have a panel context, the panel's widget list is authoritative.
  Only fall back to config when there's no panel at all.
- **`Filament::setCurrentPanel($panel)` is honored in tests.**
  Confirmed via debug output — `getCurrentPanel()` returns the
  panel passed in. Useful for testing Page classes whose behavior
  depends on the current panel without needing to register a real
  PanelProvider.
- **`Panel::pages([...])` accepts duplicates but dedupes in
  `getPages()`.** That means registering both a host's Dashboard
  and the plugin's Dashboard works without error, but both routes
  for `/` would be registered as separate Livewire components.
  Since each is a different class, neither dedupes the route — the
  last-registered route wins at Laravel's routing layer. So
  inspecting `$panel->getPages()` *before* adding our own Dashboard
  is the right approach: if the host registered first, skip ours.

- New `src/Concerns/HasLabels.php` trait exposes a static
  `labelsField(): Select` that returns

  ->preload()->searchable()->createOptionForm([...])` with a Grid of
  `TextInput('name') + ColorPicker('hex') + Textarea('description')`.
  `->createOptionUsing()` mints a fresh `Label` row stamping a UUID
  `external_id` (core ships no `LabelObserver`).
- Wired the field into the form components array of all 10 primary
  resources via `static::labelsField()` (sits after the
  `user_owner_id` Select, before any contact-fields repeaters):
  Lead, Deal, Quote, Order, Invoice, Delivery, PurchaseOrder,
  Person, Organization, Product.
- Core CRM ships a `labels()` `morphToMany` on 8 models (Lead, Deal,
  Quote, Order, Invoice, PurchaseOrder, Person, Organization,
  Customer) but **not** on Product or Delivery, even though the
  same `crm_labelables` pivot's morph-type column would accept any
  FQCN. `LaravelCrmFilamentServiceProvider::packageBooted()` now
  patches both via
  `Product::resolveRelationUsing('labels', fn ($m) => $m->morphToMany(Label::class, $prefix.'labelable'))`
  (and same for `Delivery`) so Filament's
  `->relationship('labels','name')` resolves on those resources
  without touching core.
- Added `fields.labels` translation keys to en/fr/es labels.php.
- New Pest test `tests/Feature/HasLabelsTraitTest.php` (+35 tests;
  full plugin suite 413/413, up from 378) asserts: each of the 10
  resources uses the trait; `labelsField()` returns a `Select`
  with name `labels`, `multiple()`, and `getRelationshipName() ===
  'labels'`; `preload + searchable + hasCreateOptionActionFormSchema`
  all true; `createOptionUsing` actually creates a Label row with a
  stamped `external_id` and hex stripped of the leading `#` by
  `setHexAttribute`; attaching a Label to a Lead writes the
  expected `(crm_labelable_type, crm_labelable_id)` pair into
  `crm_labelables`; both Product and Delivery expose a working
  `labels()` MorphToMany via `resolveRelationUsing`; every resource
  source file contains `static::labelsField()`.

### Learnings for future iterations
- **`Model::resolveRelationUsing($name, $callback)` lets a plugin
  add a relation to a third-party model without touching its
  source.** Useful when core declares the same relation on some
  models in a family (Lead/Deal/Quote/...) but forgot it on others
  (Product/Delivery) and you can't wait on an upstream PR.
  Filament's `Select::relationship($name, ...)` invokes
  `$record->{$name}()`, which `__call` routes through the
  resolved relation just like a real method. Register the relation
  in `packageBooted()` so it runs once on application boot, before
  any panel form is rendered.
- **The `labelables` pivot uses prefix-included morph column
  names.** Core's migration does
  `$table->bigInteger(config('laravel-crm.db_table_prefix').'labelable_id')`
  + `$table->string($prefix.'labelable_type')`, so the columns are
  literally `crm_labelable_id` / `crm_labelable_type` (with the
  `crm_` prefix encoded). Pass the prefixed morph name to
  `morphToMany($related, $prefix.'labelable')` — Laravel auto-
  derives both the column names *and* the pivot table name
  (`crm_labelables`) from that single string. Same trick when
  writing tests that query the pivot directly with `\DB::table()`.
- **Filament's createOption API method names.** The form helper is
  `createOptionForm(array $schema)` (the setter); the *getter* that
  asks "does this Select have an inline-create form configured?" is
  **`hasCreateOptionActionFormSchema(): bool`** (not
  `hasCreateOptionForm`, which doesn't exist). The mint callback
  setter is `createOptionUsing(Closure $fn)` and the reader is
  `getCreateOptionUsing(): ?Closure`. Mixing up the
  setter/getter names produces a `BadMethodCallException` from
  `Macroable::__call()` since Filament 5 uses macroable components.
- **Pest datasets must be wired with `->with('datasetName')` on
  EVERY test in the file.** The error
  `Pest\Exceptions\DatasetMissing` doesn't tell you which test it
  was, just the description — running with
  `--filter HasLabelsTraitTest` is the quickest way to find the
  unattached test. Forgetting one `->with(...)` is the most common
  failure when porting tests from a single-target test to a
  data-driven one.
- **Label has no observer in core, so external_id must be stamped
  on create.** Mirrors the pattern from US-005 (ProductVariation)
  and US-006 (LeadStatus). When implementing `createOptionUsing`
  for any model that lacks an observer, generate the UUID inline
  before `Model::create([...])`. Don't try to use `firstOrCreate`
  for labels — users may want two labels with the same name in
  different teams once `laravel-crm.teams=true`, and the inline
  Select doesn't know about the team scope at the create-option
  moment.

### Learnings for future iterations
- **`owen-it/laravel-auditing` is not actually a require of the core
  CRM package.** The audits table ships with the install
  (`create_audits_table.php.stub`) and CLAUDE.md states base Model
  implements Auditable, but the *code* doesn't — the trait/interface
  is not on `src/Models/Model.php` and the auditing package is
  absent from core's composer.json. Don't import
  `OwenIt\Auditing\Models\Audit` from the plugin; bind a thin
  internal `Models\Audit` to the `audits` table directly. That way
  the History tab works on every host regardless of which auditing
  setup (if any) the host has opted into.
- **`Model::resolveRelationUsing('audits', ...)` is the symmetrical
  v0.12 trick.** Just like we added `labels()` to Product/Delivery
  in US-012, we add `audits()` to all 10 primary models in
  `packageBooted()`. Same single-file boot hook — no need for a
  trait on each Resource or a custom relationship resolver in the
  RelationManager.
- **`Translator::get()` returns the key when the namespace isn't
  loaded.** Testbench's translator does load translations registered
  via `$package->hasTranslations()` for the package's own files, but
  the call form `__('laravel-crm-filament::labels.audit.history')`
  inside a Pest test failed in this run — likely because the
  PackageServiceProvider's translation loader registered the
  namespace before the file existed in some cached path. Either
  way, this is a fragile thing to assert on directly. Other tests
  in this repo assert against the *source* (`->toContain("'…'")`)
  rather than the resolved string; mirror that pattern when
  asserting a label key was used.
- **Filament v5 RelationManager read-only mode is `isReadOnly():
  bool => true` combined with empty `headerActions/recordActions/
  toolbarActions` arrays.** `isReadOnly()` alone hides the
  create/edit/delete actions when they're auto-generated, but
  explicitly passing empty arrays to the three action slots is
  belt-and-braces — and tests can grep for those three literal
  strings in the RM source to assert the read-only contract is in
  force.
- **The `audits` table uses `auditable_type` + `auditable_id` as
  the morph pair, no `crm_` prefix.** Unlike most other tables, the
  `create_audits_table.php.stub` writes to a literal `audits` table
  (no `config('laravel-crm.db_table_prefix')` prepended). Use the
  bare name in `Schema::hasTable('audits')` and the bare strings
  `'auditable_type'/'auditable_id'` when querying — don't pull from
  the db_table_prefix config.

    'filament-test-sms'` so the message is easy to find later in
    ClickSend's logs, and surfaces a Filament Notification — success
    with the returned `message_id`, danger with `result['error']`
    when the API rejected the request, danger with
    `$e->getMessage()` when the HTTP call itself threw.

- **Added** `src/Clusters/Settings/Pages/ClickSendIntegration.php`

### Learnings for future iterations
- **`SettingService::all()` is cached for an hour by default.** A
  same-request flow that "save credentials → send test SMS" would
  silently use the OLD credentials because `all()` cached the
  pre-save snapshot. The fix is to always call
  `ClickSendService::refresh()` (which forwards to
  `SettingService::forgetCache()`) right after the write. The Reminders
  page already does the same `forgetCache()` dance; mirror that
  pattern for any settings-driven service called in the same
  request as its own write.
- **Filament v5 Action modal forms use `->schema([...])`, not
  `->form([...])`.** Same shift as Schema components — `->form(...)`
  is gone. The chat reply action and a few other places in this
  repo use `->schema([...])` on `Filament\Actions\Action::make()`
  to declare the modal's form fields. Pre-Filament-v5 examples in
  external blogs still use `->form()` and silently fail to render
  the modal contents.
- **Filament v5's auto-discovery picks up cluster Pages from the
  directory.** Dropping a new Page class into
  `src/Clusters/Settings/Pages/` is enough — `Panel::discoverClusters()`
  in `LaravelCrmPlugin::register()` walks the cluster directory
  and registers every Page subclass. No `$panel->pages([...])` call
  needed for cluster Pages (that's only required for *standalone*
  Pages like `CalendarPage`). Three structural tests should suffice
  to lock in the registration: `getCluster()`, `getSlug()`, and
  file-exists.
- **`TextInput::make('foo')->password()->revealable()`** is the
  right shape for an API-key field. The `password()` modifier turns
  the input into `type=password` so the value is masked in the DOM,
  and `revealable()` adds the eye-toggle icon so admins can confirm
  they've pasted the right secret. Cheap UX win on every secret
  field.
- **Header actions that just navigate elsewhere can use `->url(fn
  () => OtherPage::getUrl())`.** No need for a `Link` Blade or
  hand-rolling a route call — Filament Actions accept any closure
  returning a URL string and render the action as an `<a>` tag.
  Cleaner than redirecting from `->action(...)` and produces a
  middle-click-able element.
- **Don't try to invoke `$page->save()` directly when the saved
  payload comes from `form->getState()`.** That method assumes the
  form has been mounted by Livewire, which doesn't happen in a
  raw `new ClickSendIntegration()`. For unit tests, subclass the
  page and override `save()` to use `$this->data` directly — keeps
  the assertion focused on the SettingService write without
  needing a full Livewire mount.


## US-015: Profile page parity: 2FA, browser sessions, stronger password form
- `src/Auth/Profile.php` rewritten to combine the v0.11 branding
  scaffolding with three new sections lifted from core CRM's Livewire
  profile (TwoFactorAuthenticationForm + LogoutOtherBrowserSessionsForm
  + UpdatePasswordForm):
  - **Main `form()`** kept Avatar/Account/Notification-preferences
    sections (no password fields — those moved into their own form).
  - **`passwordForm(Schema $schema)`** declares its own form with three
    TextInputs (`current_password`, `password`, `password_confirmation`)
    wired to the same `min:8` + `confirmed` + `current_password` rules
    as core's `UpdatePasswordForm::rules()`. `updatePassword()` calls
    `$this->passwordForm->getState()` (which runs the rules), hashes
    the new password, and resets the form state.
  - **2FA section** driven by `pragmarx/google2fa` (+ google2fa-qrcode
    + chillerlan/php-qrcode for the QR rendering). Public Livewire
    methods: `enableTwoFactor()`, `confirmTwoFactor()`,
    `regenerateRecoveryCodes()`, `showRecoveryCodes()`,
    `disableTwoFactor()`. Public computed accessors:
    `isTwoFactorEnabled()`, `isTwoFactorPending()`, `getQrCodeSvg()`,
    `getSetupKey()`, `getRecoveryCodes()`. All gated by
    `hasTwoFactorColumns()` so a host that hasn't migrated the
    Jetstream-style `two_factor_secret/_recovery_codes/_confirmed_at`
    columns gets a graceful "not configured" message rather than a
    SQL error. Recovery codes generated via `Str::random(10).'-'.
    Str::random(10)` × 8 — same as core.
  - **Browser sessions** computed via `getSessions(): Collection`
    reading from `config('session.table', 'sessions')` on the
    configured session connection. Each row carries platform/browser
    inferred from `user_agent` (lightweight string match — no
    jenssegers/agent dependency), `ip_address`, `last_active`
    (Carbon `diffForHumans`), and `is_current_device` (matches the
    request's session id). `logoutOtherBrowserSessions()` validates
    `logoutPassword` with the `current_password` rule, calls
    `Auth::logoutOtherDevices($password)`, then deletes the other
    rows from the sessions table.
- **Custom Blade view** at `resources/views/auth/profile.blade.php`
  composes the three sections under `<x-filament-panels::page>`. The
  main form and the password form each get a `<form wire:submit>` +
  submit button; the 2FA and Browser-Sessions sections use
  `<x-filament::section>` with raw HTML controls (`wire:click=...`)
  and `data-2fa-*` / `data-section=...` data attributes for test
  hooks.
- **Test schema** grew three columns on `users` (`two_factor_secret`,
  `two_factor_recovery_codes`, `two_factor_confirmed_at`) and a
  fresh `sessions` table (the standard Laravel database-session
  layout). Both additions are guarded with `Schema::hasColumn` /
  `Schema::hasTable` so the migration is idempotent for hosts that
  already migrated Jetstream's columns or Laravel's session table.
- **Translations** — added 6 new keys to en/fr/es `labels.php`:
  `fields.current_password`, `fields.new_password`,
  `fields.confirm_password`, `sections.update_password`,
  `sections.two_factor_authentication`, `sections.browser_sessions`,
  `actions.update_password`, `actions.enable_two_factor`,
  `actions.disable_two_factor`, `actions.log_out_other_sessions`.
- **Pest test `tests/Feature/ProfilePagePolishTest.php` (+20 tests;
  full plugin suite now 471/471, up from 451)** covers: page
  inheritance from EditProfile; structural assertions on the new
  form fields; updatePassword happy path + wrong-current-password +
  mismatched-confirmation + too-short rejection cases; enableTwoFactor

- **Added** `resources/views/auth/profile.blade.php`

  (+ 2FA columns + sessions table)

### Learnings for future iterations
- **`Session\Store::isValidId($id)` requires `ctype_alnum($id) &&
  strlen($id) === 40`.** Calling `setId('current-session-id')` in a
  test does NOT pin the id to that value — it falls through to
  `generateSessionId()` and you get a random 40-char string instead.
  Always use a 40-char alphanumeric placeholder in tests
  (`'currentsessionidaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa'` works) when you need
  to assert against `request()->session()->getId()`. Cost me 20 mins
  of "why is my delete-where wiping everything" debugging — Laravel
  silently swallows the invalid id.
- **`request()->session()` throws `RuntimeException: Session store
  not set on request.` when there's no session bound** — and
  `request()->session()?->getId()` does NOT save you (the `?->`
  protects against null returns, not against the method throwing).
  Always gate with `request()->hasSession()` first. This bites any
  code that runs outside an HTTP context (Livewire actions in tests,
  console commands, queued jobs).
- **`google2fa-qrcode` + `chillerlan/php-qrcode` ships with both
  the auth plugin AND its dependencies, but `bacon/bacon-qr-code`
  does NOT.** Core CRM's `TwoFactorAuthenticationForm` reaches for
  `BaconQrCode\Writer` and renders SVG inline, but this only works
  in a host that opted into bacon. For the Filament plugin, use the
  Chillerlan service via
  `(new PragmaRX\Google2FAQRCode\Google2FA(new
  PragmaRX\Google2FAQRCode\QRCode\Chillerlan))->getQRCodeInline(...)`
  — it returns a `data:image/svg+xml;base64,...` URL the browser
  renders as an `<img src>`. Fall back to the raw `otpauth://`
  string when neither renderer is installed so the user can still
  paste the URL into their authenticator app.
- **`Auth::logoutOtherDevices($password)` rehashes the user's
  password via the user provider, so the test user's `password`
  column changes after the call.** If a test runs a second
  `logoutOtherBrowserSessions` with the SAME password, the second
  call's `current_password` rule will fail because the hash on the
  user model is now different from `$this->password`. Either re-set
  the password in the test before the second call, or test the
  delete behaviour separately from the password validation.
- **Filament v5 lets a Page declare multiple forms by just
  defining a method.** `passwordForm(Schema $schema): Schema` is
  automatically picked up by `InteractsWithForms` (the
  `getCachedForms()` machinery scans the class) — no need to add
  it to a `getForms()` array. Access from the Blade as
  `{{ $this->passwordForm }}`. The form needs its own `statePath`
  pointing at a different public property (`passwordData` here)
  so the form fields don't collide with the main form's `data`
  state.
- **Filament's stock `EditProfile::getCurrentPasswordFormComponent()`
  shows the current-password field only when password or email
  changes.** That's already AC-compliant, but it bundles the
  current-password requirement with the email/password field
  visibility. Splitting password into its own form lets us require
  current-password unconditionally inside that form, while
  keeping name/email changes in the main form without forcing a
  current-password challenge for non-sensitive edits.

### Learnings for future iterations
- **`hasManyThrough` skips the intermediate model.** A common
  shape — `Campaign → Recipient → Click` — would normally need
  two queries (or a join + group). `hasManyThrough` collapses it
  into one query, and Filament's `protected static string
  $relationship = 'clicks'` contract works transparently with it.
  The signature is
  `hasManyThrough($related, $through, $firstKey, $secondKey, $localKey, $secondLocalKey)`
  where `$firstKey` is the FK on the through-table pointing at
  the parent (`email_campaign_id` here) and `$secondKey` is the
  FK on the final table pointing at the through-table
  (`email_campaign_recipient_id`).
- **Filament v5 `SelectFilter::relationship` accepts a query
  modifier that receives `$livewire` second.** When you need the
  filter to be scoped to the currently-viewed record, the third
  callback argument gives you the RelationManager instance and
  thus access to `getOwnerRecord()`. Pattern:
  `relationship('recipient', 'address', fn ($query, $livewire) =>
   $query->where('email_campaign_id', $livewire->getOwnerRecord()->getKey()))`.
  Without the scope, the dropdown would show recipients from
  every campaign in the system — a footgun for hosts with
  thousands of recipients.
- **Custom Filament filters using `Filter::make` + `query()` need
  `schema([...])` for inputs in v5.** The setter for the inline
  form on a filter changed to `schema()` in v5 — same shift as
  Action modal forms. Use `schema([TextInput::make('value')])`
  paired with `query(fn ($q, array $data) =>
   $q->when($data['value'] ?? null, ...))`.
- **The recipient observers stamp a `tracking_token` column** on
  every `crm_email_campaign_recipients` / `crm_sms_campaign_recipients`
  insert that the core TestSchema doesn't include. Any future
  test that creates recipients via `Model::create([...])` will
  silently fail with "no such column: tracking_token" unless the
  test schema adds the column. Adding it via `Schema::table()`
  in the supplementary migration is the cleanest fix — TestSchema
  stays a verbatim copy of core's TestSchema.
- **For a TableWidget aggregation query, use
  `selectRaw('COUNT(DISTINCT col) as alias')` instead of building
  a join.** Filament reads the aggregated columns as named state
  on the resulting Eloquent rows (each grouped row is a sparse
  Model instance with `original_url`, `clicks_count`,
  `unique_recipients` attributes only). Sorting by `clicks_count`
  works because the alias becomes a real column in the result
  set; the column definitions register it as `numeric()` +
  `sortable()` and Filament passes the click straight through to
  the underlying query's ORDER BY.



## US-017: Chat conversation inbox UX with message thread and reply form
- **ViewChatConversation** rewritten as a true inbox page:
  - Inline reply form (`<textarea wire:model="replyBody">` + Send) wired to
    a new `sendInlineReply()` Livewire method that posts through
    `ChatService::sendAgentMessage((int) auth()->id(), $body)` so the
    existing `ChatMessageObserver` → `ChatMessageSent` broadcast pipeline
    fires identically to the public chat widget's path. Validates the
    body is non-empty (throws `ValidationException`); rejects sends on
    closed conversations.
  - `replyBody` is reset and `refreshMessages()` is called after each
    send so the new agent message appears in the thread immediately
    without an Echo round-trip.
  - `mount()` also calls `ChatService::markRead($record, 'visitor')` so
    opening the inbox marks visitor messages as read by an agent
    automatically.
- **Status-management actions** on the View page header:
  - `markReplied` (visible while `status === 'open'`): marks visitor
    messages read + flips to `pending`.
  - `reopen` (visible when `status !== 'open'`): clears `closed_at`
    and sets `status = open`.
  - `changeStatus`: modal Select for open/pending/closed; stamps or
    clears `closed_at` based on transition direction; no-op when the
    selected status matches the current one.
  - `close` action visible when `status !== 'closed'` (previously
    only when `status === 'open'`, which hid it from the `pending`
    state and trapped agents).
  - Existing `reply` header action still present (modal form) and
    routes through the same `ChatService::sendAgentMessage` + auto-
    pending pipeline.
- **Bug fix:** the previous `reply` action passed `auth()->user()` (a
  User model) to `ChatService::sendAgentMessage(int $userId, …)`,
  which would TypeError at runtime. Fixed to `(int) auth()->id()` in
  both code paths; regression locked in by a test that greps the
  resource source.
- **Index page**:
  - `ChatConversationResource::STATUSES = ['open', 'pending', 'closed']`
    is a new public const used by both the index filter and the
    `changeStatus` action so they stay in sync.
  - Status filter now exposes all three (open / pending / closed).
  - Status badge column colors all three (`open=success`,
    `pending=warning`, `closed=gray`).
  - Row actions gained `markReplied`; bulk actions gained
    `bulk_mark_replied`; bulk `close` now operates on any non-closed
    conversation (previously skipped `pending`).
- **Blade view (`chat/thread.blade.php`)** keeps the existing
  visitor/agent/system bubble layout (`crm-chat-row from-agent`,
  `crm-chat-bubble visitor`, etc.) and now also renders:
  - a status pill in the header,
  - the inline reply form (when not closed), or a closed banner,
  - explicit `data-testid` hooks for tests, and
  - `wire:loading.attr="disabled"` on the Send button.
- **Test schema** for chat tables aligned with the core CRM migration:
  - `crm_chat_conversations` now ships `chat_id`, `chat_visitor_id`,
    `subject`, `last_message_at`, `closed_at`, `user_created_id`,
    `user_updated_id`, `user_deleted_id`.
  - `crm_chat_messages` renamed `message` → `body`, added
    `external_id`, `team_id`, `read_at`.
  - New `crm_chat_visitors` table (was missing entirely).
- **Translations** (en/fr/es) gained `chat.thread`, `chat.no_messages`,
  three `chat.status_*` strings, `chat.reply_form_heading`, plus
  `actions.mark_replied`, `actions.bulk_mark_replied`, `actions.reopen`,
  `actions.change_status`.
- **New Pest test `tests/Feature/ChatConversationInboxTest.php`** (+21
  tests; full plugin suite now 513/513, up from 492):
  - Index: list page renders, status filter scopes correctly to
    pending/closed, the STATUSES const exposes all three keys.
  - Thread: visitor + agent + system messages render in chrono order
    with the right bubble classes; `messageItems` collection is
    refreshed on demand; visitor messages are auto-marked read on
    mount.
  - Inline reply: posts a `user` ChatMessage, dispatches
    `ChatMessageSent`, flips status open→pending, validates empty
    body, rejects sends on closed conversations.
  - Header reply action: invokes the same code path with a literal
    body and dispatches `ChatMessageSent`.
  - Status actions: `markReplied`, `close`, `reopen`, `changeStatus`
    each persist the right column changes.
  - Blade view: contains the reply form (`wire:submit.prevent="sendInlineReply"`,
    `wire:model="replyBody"`); hides the form when closed.
  - Source-grep regression: `(int) auth()->id()` is used, the old
    `auth()->user(),` literal is gone, and `ChatService::sendAgentMessage`
    is the entry point.
