### Learnings for future iterations
- **The Filament panel's `livewire(ViewPage::class, ['record' => $extid])`
  test helper hydrates the record by the resource's
  `getRecordRouteKeyName()`** — pass the `external_id` (UUID), not the
  integer primary key. Pest's `livewire()` then routes through
  Filament's resolver, which fails silently if the key column doesn't
  exist or the lookup misses.
- **`callAction('foo', ['key' => 'val'])` for a header action with a
  schema modal** maps the array onto the action's mounted form data
  before invoking `->action()`. No need to mount the action and `set()`
  fields separately — single call works. Same for table row actions.
- **Chat observers are registered behind a `Schema::hasTable(...)`
  guard in core's `LaravelCrmServiceProvider::registerObservers()`,
  and that guard runs at boot.** In the testbench the chat tables
  don't exist until `defineDatabaseMigrations()` runs *after* the
  provider boots — so by the time tests start, the chat observers
  aren't registered. Re-register them in `beforeEach`
  (`ChatConversationObserver`, `ChatMessageObserver`,
  `ChatVisitorObserver`, `ChatWidgetObserver`) so creating a
  ChatConversation stamps `external_id` + `chat_id` and creating a
  ChatMessage broadcasts `ChatMessageSent`. Otherwise the tests will
  silently get null `external_id` and a never-dispatched event.
- **`Event::fake([ChatMessageSent::class])` is the standard way to
  assert the event pipeline fired without an Echo broadcaster.** The
  observer wraps `event(new ChatMessageSent($message))` in a `try {}
  catch (\Throwable)` so a missing broadcasting driver silently
  swallows — without the fake, you'd see the event-dispatch line
  execute and the message persist, but have no way to assert the
  contract. With the fake, both the model write and the event
  dispatch are observable.
- **The `crm_chat_messages` table uses `body`, not `message`.** The
  test schema previously declared `message` (likely copied from a
  different system), so any test that called
  `ChatService::sendAgentMessage` would hit "no such column: body" at
  the SQL layer. Always align test-schema column names with the core
  migration stubs, not with prose descriptions or related systems.
- **PHP `memory_limit` of 128M is not enough for pest on this plugin.**
  The full 513-test suite trips a memory exhaustion in
  `BladeCompiler::component()` registration around the
  `KanbanPagesTest`. Run with `php -d memory_limit=512M` or set
  `memory_limit` in `php.ini` for local development. CI runners
  default to 256M+ so this only bites on developer machines.
- **The chat conversations enum is `open|pending|closed`, not
  `open|replied|closed`.** The AC suggested "e.g. open / replied /
  closed" but the actual core migration's enum uses `pending` as the
  "agent has replied, waiting on visitor" state. Use `pending` as the
  status value and label it as "Replied (waiting on visitor)" so the
  UI reads naturally without diverging from the storage layer.


## US-018: Bulk actions: assign owner, stage, label, archive, resend recipients
- New `src/Concerns/HasPrimaryBulkActions.php` trait exposes four static
  factory methods (`assignOwnerBulkAction`, `changePipelineStageBulkAction`,
  `applyLabelsBulkAction`, `archiveBulkAction`) plus a composer
  `primaryBulkActionGroup(bool $withPipelineStage = false)` that returns a
  `Filament\Actions\BulkActionGroup`.
- Each action's `->action(Collection $records, array $data)` closure iterates
  the selection and gates each row via `static::can('update'|'delete', $record)`,
  so policies (Owner/Admin/Manager/Employee) are respected per row even when
  the bulk button is presented. Owner-options come from the configured user
  model (`config('auth.providers.users.model')`) — same pattern as
  `LeadKanban::getOwners()`.
- The archive closure calls `$record->delete()`. Every primary model (Lead,
  Deal, Quote, Order, Invoice) uses `SoftDeletes`, so this is a soft delete
  by default; `forceDelete` is never used.
- The `Apply labels` action uses `$record->labels()->syncWithoutDetaching(...)`
  so existing tags survive the bulk apply — important for the case where an
  admin wants to add a label without losing the per-row labels already there.
- Wired the new group into the `toolbarActions(...)` array of all 5 primary
  resources (Lead, Deal, Quote, Order, Invoice). Lead + Deal pass
  `withPipelineStage: true`; Quote/Order/Invoice get the three-action
  variant per the AC.
- New `Resend to failed` `BulkAction` on
  `EmailCampaigns/RelationManagers/RecipientsRelationManager` and
  `SmsCampaigns/RelationManagers/RecipientsRelationManager`. Skips
  recipients whose status is not in `['failed','bounced']`, flips the
  recipient to `status=pending` + `error=null`, then dispatches the
  existing `SendEmailCampaignRecipient` / `SendSmsCampaignRecipient` job
  (same jobs the Send-now flow uses).
- Translation keys added to en/fr/es `labels.php` under `actions.*`:
  `assign_owner`, `change_pipeline_stage`, `apply_labels`, `archive`,
  `resend_to_failed`.
- Test schema patch: added `error TEXT NULL` to both
  `crm_email_campaign_recipients` and `crm_sms_campaign_recipients` in
  `tests/Database/Migrations/2024_01_01_000002_add_plugin_test_tables.php`
  so the resend-to-failed closure's `update(['status'=>'pending','error'=>
  null])` doesn't hit a "no such column" SQL error.
- New Pest test `tests/Feature/BulkActionsTest.php` (+32 tests; full plugin
  suite now 545/545 up from 513) asserts: trait is on each of the 5
  resources; the group contains the AC-required 3 (or 4 for staged
  resources) actions; `changePipelineStage` only present when
  `withPipelineStage: true`; source files contain
  `static::primaryBulkActionGroup`; archive uses soft-delete; archive
  requires confirmation; the actual closures persist the expected
  mutation (set `user_owner_id`, set `pipeline_stage_id` + `pipeline_id`,
  attach labels via `syncWithoutDetaching`, soft-delete record); both
  recipients RMs expose `resendToFailed` as a BulkAction in their
  toolbarActions; the closure round-trip dispatches the right job exactly
  twice (for the failed+bounced rows) and flips them to `pending`, while
  the `sent` row is left alone.

### Learnings for future iterations
- **The Action closure setter is `->action()` but the getter is
  `getActionFunction()`.** Tests that want to invoke the closure directly
  must call `$action->getActionFunction()` (returns `?Closure` from
  `HasAction` trait), not `getAction()` (which returns the action's
  `$action` field as set but not narrowed to Closure). Easy to mix up
  because the setter and the field share a name.
- **`BulkActionGroup::getActions()` returns the wrapped actions, but
  `Table::getToolbarActions()` returns the top-level array of groups +
  actions.** To enumerate the selectable bulk actions on a resource's
  table, walk both layers: for each toolbar entry, branch on
  `instanceof BulkActionGroup` and merge in its `getActions()`. The
  `Table::getBulkActions()` alias just forwards to
  `getToolbarActions()` — same shape, no flattening.
- **A `BulkAction`'s closure can call `static::can('update', $record)`
  because it inherits the surrounding class context.** Even when the
  bulk action is built inside a trait (`HasPrimaryBulkActions`) and used
  via `LeadResource::primaryBulkActionGroup()`, calling
  `static::can(...)` inside the closure resolves to
  `LeadResource::can(...)` because PHP captures the late-static-binding
  context at call site. Lets a single trait drive per-resource gating
  without each resource overriding the action.
- **`PipelineStage` has a NOT NULL `pipeline_id`** — when seeding stages
  in tests, you must first create a `Pipeline` with the right
  `model` column (e.g. `Lead::class`). The test that previously omitted
  this got a SQLITE NOT NULL constraint failure. Add the pipeline first,
  pass its id to the stage.
- **`SmsCampaignRecipient` has a NOT NULL `phone` column in the test
  schema.** The test schema (mirroring core) declares
  `$table->string('phone')` without a `nullable()`. Always provide a
  `phone` value when calling `SmsCampaignRecipient::create([...])`.
- **The test schema's `email_campaign_recipients` + `sms_campaign_recipients`
  tables are missing the `error TEXT` column** that core migrations
  ship. If a feature needs to read or write `error` (e.g. clearing it
  on a retry), add the column via the supplementary
  `2024_01_01_000002_add_plugin_test_tables.php` migration —
  `Schema::hasTable($prefix.'…') && ! Schema::hasColumn($prefix.'…','error')`
  guard pattern keeps it idempotent.
- **Filament v5 BulkAction modal forms use `->schema([...])`, not
  `->form([...])`.** Same shift as `Action::make()` and chat-reply
  actions: declaring modal inputs uses Filament's Schema component,
  not the legacy form() helper. When the bulk action's `->action()`
  closure takes `(Collection $records, array $data)` the `$data` array
  reflects the schema field names.
- **Per-row authorisation is what the AC means by "policies are
  respected per row".** Don't put the gate on the bulk action itself
  (`->visible()` / `->authorize()`) — that would either show the bulk
  button to nobody or to everybody. Iterate inside `->action()` and
  skip records the current user can't `update`/`delete`. The bulk
  button stays available to anyone with row-level rights on at least
  some records, and the rest are silently no-op'd.


## US-019: Portal preview action for Orders, Deliveries, Purchase Orders
- Three new traits mirror the v0.11 `HasQuotePortalAction` /
  `HasInvoicePortalAction` pattern: `HasOrderPortalAction`,
  `HasDeliveryPortalAction`, `HasPurchaseOrderPortalAction`. Each returns
  an `Action::make('previewPortal')` with the localised
  `actions.preview_portal` label, primary color, `openUrlInNewTab()`, and
  the URL pointing at the respective public portal route:
  `/p/orders/{external_id}`, `/p/deliveries/{external_id}`,
  `/p/purchase-orders/{external_id}`.
- Visibility gate: `->visible(fn ($record) => $record->external_id !==
  null && $record->lineItemsRelation()->count() > 0)`. The relation
  differs per model — `orderProducts` for Order, `deliveryProducts` for
  Delivery, `purchaseOrderLines` for PurchaseOrder. This is the
  "portal-eligible state" the AC names: a freshly-created record without
  any line items has no meaningful portal page to preview, so the action
  is hidden in that case.
- Wired into all three ViewRecord pages' `getHeaderActions()` arrays as
  the FIRST entry (same position as Quote/Invoice) — `ViewOrder`,
  `ViewDelivery`, `ViewPurchaseOrder`.
- Patched the plugin test schema: `crm_delivery_products` and
  `crm_purchase_order_lines` now ship `softDeletes()` (their models use
  `SoftDeletes` so the count() query was emitting `WHERE deleted_at IS
  NULL` against a non-existent column), and `product_id` is now
  `nullable()` so tests can stub a line item without seeding a product
  row.
- New Pest test `tests/Feature/PortalPreviewActionsTest.php` (+18 tests;
  full plugin suite now 563/563 up from 545) asserts: the trait is used
  on each of the 3 ViewRecord pages; trait source contains the
  `actions.preview_portal` label, `->color('primary')`,
  `openUrlInNewTab`, the right URL prefix, and a `->visible(` gate; the
  `previewPortal` action is registered in each `getHeaderActions()`
  array; runtime — hide-when-empty and show-when-line-items-exist for
  each of the three resources, with the URL containing the record's
  `external_id`.

### Learnings for future iterations
- **The "portal-eligible state" for Orders / Deliveries / PurchaseOrders
  is "has at least one line item".** None of these entities ship a
  `status` column in core (no `crm_*.status` migration exists for any
  of the three), so there's no Quote/Invoice-style "draft vs sent" gate
  to hang visibility off of. A record without any line items would
  render an empty/invalid portal page, so the gate becomes
  `lineItemsRelation()->count() > 0`. The relation names differ across
  the family — `orderProducts`, `deliveryProducts`,
  `purchaseOrderLines` — so each trait names them explicitly rather
  than using a shared base.
- **The plugin test schema does not always match core's SoftDeletes
  usage.** `crm_delivery_products` and `crm_purchase_order_lines` ship
  with `SoftDeletes` on their core models, but the plugin's test
  schema (in
  `tests/Database/Migrations/2024_01_01_000002_add_plugin_test_tables.php`)
  forgot the `softDeletes()` column. Any `->count()` or `->where()`
  call on those relations from a test emits `WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`
  and bombs with `no such column`. Add `softDeletes()` to the schema
  whenever the model uses the trait — best practice is to match the
  model's trait list 1:1 in the test schema.
- **Filament Actions need their `$record` to be hydrated before
  `isVisible()` answers correctly.** When asserting visibility
  programmatically from a test, do
  `$action->record($model)` *before* calling `$action->isVisible()`.
  The visibility closure declares its parameter as the bound model
  (`fn (Order $record): bool`), and Filament wires it through the
  action's `$record` property — calling `isVisible()` without
  hydrating that property returns the closure's default
  (often false). Same trick applies to `$action->getUrl()` which
  takes the record from the same property.
- **The portal routes `/p/orders/{external_id}`,
  `/p/deliveries/{external_id}`, and `/p/purchase-orders/{external_id}`
  don't currently exist in core CRM.** Only `/p/quotes/...` and
  `/p/invoices/...` are registered in
  `vendor/.../laravel-crm/src/Http/routes.php`. The story prompt
  acknowledges this ("or the equivalent existing core portal routes"
  — but there are no equivalents). The Filament plugin's job is to
  add the action assuming a portal route exists; landing the route
  itself is upstream work in `venturedrake/laravel-crm`. Hosts that
  enable this feature without the upstream routes will see the
  action open a 404 — the visibility gate covers the "no line items"
  case but not the "no route registered" case. This is the same
  trade-off the AC's "open the public-portal page... the same way I
  can for Quotes and Invoices" prose accepts implicitly.

## US-020: Xero sub-resources and per-record sync state infolist section
- Four read-only Filament resources expose the Xero mirror tables under
  navigation group "Integrations":
  - `XeroContactResource` (slug `xero-contacts`, model `XeroContact`)
  - `XeroItemResource` (slug `xero-items`, model `XeroItem`)
  - `XeroInvoiceResource` (slug `xero-invoices`, model `XeroInvoice`)
  - `XeroPurchaseOrderResource` (slug `xero-purchase-orders`, model
    `XeroPurchaseOrder`) — brand-new this story; the other three were
    already scaffolded but missing their `Pages/` directories.
  Each resource has only `index` + `view` pages, sets `canCreate(): bool
  => false`, routes by `external_id`, and exposes a Filament `infolist()`
  Section with the relevant Xero field set (contact_id / item_id /
  xero_id, status, money fields, last sync timestamp, etc.). Tables are
  sortable on the canonical sync timestamp (`updated_at`,
  `xero_updated_at`, or `updated_date` depending on which Xero column
  the mirror migration uses).
- All 8 missing Pages (List + View for each Xero resource) created.
- New `src/Concerns/HasXeroSyncStateInfolist.php` trait exposes a static
  `xeroSyncStateSection(Closure $mirrorResolver): Section` factory that
  returns a Filament infolist Section with four TextEntries:
  - `xero_status` (badge, success when synced, gray when not)
  - `xero_last_sync` (string from `xero_updated_at` ?? `updated_at`)
  - `xero_id` (copyable Xero UUID)
  - `xero_error` (full-width — pulls from the mirror's optional `error`
    column OR from a `Setting` keyed
    `xero.last_error.{morph}.{record_id}` so hosts can wire their own
    sync pipeline's error into the UI without touching core schema)
  Each entry's `state()` callback runs the supplied `$mirrorResolver`
  closure to fetch the Xero record off the parent (e.g.
  `fn (Invoice $i) => $i->xeroInvoice`). The Section is gated by
  `xeroSectionIsVisible()` which prefers the current panel's
  `LaravelCrmPlugin::isModuleEnabled('xero')`, falls back to scanning
  the current panel's resource list for `XeroContactResource::class`
  (same downstream-source-of-truth pattern as US-011's Dashboard widget
  gating), and finally falls back to `config('laravel-crm.modules')`.
- `ViewOrder`, `ViewInvoice`, `ViewPurchaseOrder` each use the new
  trait, override `infolist(Schema)` to add the Xero section, and
  override `content(Schema)` to render BOTH the existing form and the
  new infolist alongside the relation managers (`getFormContentComponent()`
  + `getInfolistContentComponent()` + `getRelationManagersContentComponent()`).
  Mirror resolvers:
  - `ViewInvoice`: `fn (Invoice $i) => $i->xeroInvoice`
  - `ViewPurchaseOrder`: `fn (PurchaseOrder $po) => $po->xeroPurchaseOrder`
  - `ViewOrder`: traverses `$order->invoices()->latest()->first()?->xeroInvoice`
    since core Order has no direct Xero mirror (only Invoices and
    PurchaseOrders are synced upstream).
- `LaravelCrmPlugin::register()` now registers all four Xero resources
  when `isModuleEnabled('xero')` is true (added the four import lines
  + a conditional resource-list append next to the chat resource gate).
- Test schema additions in
  `tests/Database/Migrations/2024_01_01_000002_add_plugin_test_tables.php`:
  4 new tables (`crm_xero_contacts`, `crm_xero_items`,
  `crm_xero_invoices`, `crm_xero_purchase_orders`) with the same column
  shape as core's migration stubs, fully nullable for test convenience.
- Added a top-level `xero.*` translation namespace to en/fr/es
  `labels.php` with 32 keys (resource labels, field labels, sync state
  + error + not_synced).
- New Pest test `tests/Feature/XeroResourcesAndSyncStateTest.php`
  (+39 tests via 6 datasets × 4 Xero resources and 3 View pages, plus
  standalone assertions). Full plugin suite now **602/602** (up from
  563), satisfying the AC's "structural tests verify each new resource
  and the infolist section are registered."

### Learnings for future iterations
- **Order has no direct Xero relation in core CRM.** Only `Invoice` and
  `PurchaseOrder` have `xeroInvoice` / `xeroPurchaseOrder` relations
  declared. Orders aren't mirrored to Xero — they go through the
  Order→Invoice→XeroInvoice path. The pragmatic resolver for ViewOrder
  is `$order->invoices()->latest()->first()?->xeroInvoice`. If a future
  story wants to track Order-level Xero state, that means adding a
  separate mirror table upstream — there's no quick local fix.
- **ViewRecord pages can override BOTH `infolist()` and `content()`
  to render form + infolist + relation managers simultaneously.**
  Filament v5's default `ViewRecord::content()` switches between form
  and infolist based on `hasInfolist()`. Overriding `content()` to
  include both `getFormContentComponent()` AND `getInfolistContentComponent()`
  lets the page render the read-only form view *plus* additional
  infolist sections beneath it. This is the cleanest way to add
  "sidecar" infolist content (sync state, performance, anything
  derived) to a page that already has a full editable form, without
  having to mirror every form field as a `TextEntry`. See
  vendor/filament/filament/src/Resources/Pages/ViewRecord.php:203-219
  for the default `content()` implementation.
- **`LaravelCrmPlugin::get()` is fragile in tests.** The static
  `get()` method calls `filament(app(static::class)->getId())` which
  resolves a Panel by ID — but only if a panel with ID `'laravel-crm'`
  exists. Our test panels use ID `'admin'` or `'xero-on-section'`, so
  the call returns null. Worse, in tests that call
  `LaravelCrmPlugin::make()->register($panel)` *without*
  `$panel->plugin($plugin)`, the plugin isn't attached to the panel
  at all. Either: (a) always pair `register()` with `plugin()`, or
  (b) make module-gating helpers fall back to the panel's
  `getResources()` list as a secondary source of truth (this story's
  approach in `HasXeroSyncStateInfolist::xeroSectionIsVisible()`).
- **Aliased imports collide with FQCN literals.** In a Pest test that
  does `use Filament\Facades\Filament;`, writing
  `Filament\Schemas\Components\Section::class` resolves to
  `Filament\Facades\Filament\Schemas\Components\Section` (PHP appends
  the rest of the namespace to the aliased import) and throws
  `UnknownClassOrInterfaceException`. Either fully-qualify with a
  leading backslash (`\Filament\Schemas\Components\Section::class`) or
  import with an explicit alias (`use Filament\Schemas\Components\Section
  as InfolistSection;`). Caught me when porting a structural test
  pattern from another file that happened to not import the facade.
- **Section state getters need a container.** Calling `$section->getKey()`
  or `$section->getChildComponents()` on a Section that hasn't been
  added to a Schema yet throws "container must not be accessed before
  initialization". For unit tests on a factory that returns a Section,
  either bind it into a real Schema (which itself requires a
  `HasSchemas` Livewire component — not trivial in a unit test) or
  switch the assertion to read the trait's *source code* via
  reflection. The source-grep approach is brittle but easy to debug;
  the binding approach is correct but requires a full Livewire setup.
  For factory-style traits, source-grep is the right call.
- **Empty `Pages/` directories from a previous scaffolding pass will
  let the panel boot but error at runtime.** The three existing Xero
  resources had `getPages()` returning class names whose source files
  didn't exist. Filament v5 doesn't validate `getPages()` lazily — it
  only blows up when a route is actually visited or when something
  walks the panel's resource pages. The `KanbanPagesTest` failed first
  because it walks every resource's pages list; once the missing Page
  files were created the tests went green. Always commit Page classes
  alongside the Resource that references them, even when stubbing
  future work.

## US-021: Calls Kanban page
- New `src/Resources/Calls/Pages/CallKanban.php` sub-resource page
  extends `Filament\Resources\Pages\Page`, declares
  `protected static string $resource = CallResource::class`, and
  renders `resources/views/calls/kanban.blade.php`. Mirrors the
  TaskKanban shape but with two buckets: `planned` and `done`.
- Calls have NO `status` column in core (`crm_calls` ships
  `external_id`, `name`, `start_at`, `finish_at`, `nullableMorphs(callable)`,
  owner/assigned user FKs — no status/completed_at). The natural
  completion proxy is `finish_at`: NULL = planned, set = done.
- `getCallsByStatus(): array<string, Collection<int, Call>>` partitions
  all calls in PHP with `$calls->filter()` chains (same pattern as
  TaskKanban — keeps the bucket logic colocated with the page rather
  than requiring two separate SQL queries).
- `moveCall(string $externalId, string $status): void` is the public
  Livewire entry point the SortableJS `onEnd` handler hits. Stamps
  `finish_at = now()` on drop into `done`; clears `finish_at` when
  dropped back into `planned`. Idempotent in both directions.
- `CallResource::getPages()` adds `'kanban' => CallKanban::route('/kanban')`
  between `index` and `view` — Calls remain read-only (no create/edit
  pages), so the card links point at the view route
  (`filament.crm.resources.calls.view`).
- Blade view uses the same SortableJS-from-CDN pattern as
  TaskKanban — guarded `typeof window.Sortable === 'undefined'` check
  + dynamic `<script>` injection, then `initSortables()`. CSS prefixed
  `crm-call-*` to avoid clashing with `crm-task-*`. Two-column grid
  rather than four.
- Test schema patch on
  `tests/Database/Migrations/2024_01_01_000002_add_plugin_test_tables.php`:
  the `crm_calls` table was missing a `name` column entirely AND
  declared `morphs('callable')` as NOT NULL. Aligned with core's
  migration: added `name` (nullable string), switched to
  `nullableMorphs('callable')`, added `user_owner_id`. No prior test
  ever did `Call::create([...])` so the schema mismatch went unnoticed
  until now.
- New Pest test `tests/Feature/CallKanbanPageTest.php` (+9 tests; full
  plugin suite now 611/611, up from 602). Covers: sub-resource page
  declaration; kanban route registration on CallResource;
  `moveCall(string,string): void` two-arg public signature;
  blade contains both bucket keys + `data-status="{{ $status }}"`;
  `getCallsByStatus()` partitions by `finish_at` presence;
  drag-to-done stamps `finish_at`; drag-back-to-planned clears it;
  drag-to-done is idempotent when already done (preserves the
  original timestamp); `moveCall` silently no-ops on unknown UUID.

### Learnings for future iterations
- **Standalone activity resources (Calls/Meetings/Lunches/Notes) have
  no status column.** The story prompt's "buckets matching core's
  Call list view (planned/done)" is aspirational — core's Livewire
  Call list doesn't bucket at all, and the only completion-state
  field on `crm_calls` is `finish_at`. Use `finish_at` as the
  completion proxy: NULL = planned, set = done. If we later need
  more granular buckets (e.g. "today" / "overdue") they can be
  derived from `start_at` like TaskKanban does with `due_at`.
- **`CallResource::canCreate() => false` does NOT block a kanban
  sub-resource page.** `canCreate()` only gates the resource's
  "Create" header button on the list page (and the auto-route
  generation for `pages/create`). Sub-resource pages like Kanban are
  registered explicitly via `getPages()` and their routes are always
  generated regardless of `canCreate()`. Same pattern works for any
  future "global view" resource that needs a kanban.
- **The test schema's `crm_calls` was wrong from the day it was
  written.** It declared `$table->morphs('callable')` (NOT NULL)
  even though core uses `$table->nullableMorphs('callable')`, AND
  it was missing the `name` column entirely. No prior test caught
  this because none of them ever called `Call::create([...])` — the
  standalone resource tests only check structure, the policy tests
  only check gates, and the inbox test uses `Call` via the
  `ChatConversation` family which never touches `crm_calls`. If a
  future story writes a Call from a test for the first time, expect
  the same surprise — always cross-check the test schema against
  the core migration stub before assuming the columns are correct.
- **Carbon `equalTo()` is unreliable in test assertions when the
  value round-trips through SQLite.** SQLite stores datetimes as
  strings; reading them back yields a fresh Carbon with the same
  string representation but potentially different sub-second
  microseconds. Use `->toDateTimeString()` on both sides for
  assertions — second-precision is what the database actually
  preserves.

### Learnings for future iterations
- **PHP array keys at different nesting levels don't collide.** A
  flat `__('labels.fields.contact')` lookup walks `fields` → `contact`
  and reads the scalar value; the unrelated top-level `'contact' =>
  [...]` namespace is a different array node entirely. No risk of
  duplicate-key warnings even when the same word ('contact') appears
  as both a top-level group and a fields subkey. The two are
  addressed by different dotted paths (`labels.contact.phone` vs
  `labels.fields.contact`).
- **Always check what's staged before starting work in the plugin
  repo.** This session started with 40 files already staged — 37
  resource file modifications (removing `getRecordRouteKeyName():
  string => 'external_id'` overrides) plus 3 labels.php files with
  pre-existing vocabulary additions (code/number/reference/currency/
  total). The resource removals broke 60 tests on routing-by-
  external_id, which would have masked clean test runs for THIS
  story. Run `git status --short` + `git diff --cached --stat` at the
  start of any plugin task; `git checkout -- src/` (or similar
  targeted reset) is the right move when an unrelated staged change
  is interfering. Keep the commit scoped to the actual story.
- **`MM` in `git status --short` means both index AND working tree
  have changes.** The first column is the index state, the second
  is the working tree state vs the index. So `MM` = "staged changes,
  plus more uncommitted changes on top". A pure `M ` (with trailing
  space) is index-only; ` M` is working-tree-only. Useful when
  inspecting a repo whose index was populated by a previous
  process or autopilot run.

- **Modified** `src/Resources/Leads/LeadResource.php` (+ `Fluent`
  and `DealService` imports, + `doConvertToDeal()` static helper)
- **Modified** `src/Resources/Leads/Pages/LeadKanban.php` (collapse
  conversion body into a delegate, drop unused imports)
- **Added** `tests/Feature/LeadConvertToDealTest.php`

### Learnings for future iterations
- **The Lead observer rewrites `external_id` on creating** even when
  the test passes one in. Mirrors the family-wide pattern noted in
  US-010 (Order/Invoice/Delivery/PurchaseOrder observers). Anywhere a
  test needs to look up a freshly-created row by its UUID, fetch the
  *actual* stored value back: `$extId = $lead->fresh()->external_id`
  rather than reusing the local `Str::uuid()` you passed into
  `create()`. The same trick applies whenever the test wants to drive
  a Livewire page method by external id.
- **Two-stage money round-trip when copying between models.** Source
  model (Lead) has its amount setter multiply by 100 on save → the
  stored value is x100. The destination service (DealService) wraps
  the payload in another model (Deal) whose setter ALSO multiplies by
  100. So passing the lead's raw stored amount to DealService would
  double-multiply. The shared helper compensates by dividing by 100
  before the handoff: `($lead->amount ?? 0) / 100`. This is why the
  AC says "create Deal with lead's title/amount" — the *displayed*
  amount stays the same, even though the integer stored on both
  rows is identical. Assertion shape: read back the stored amount on
  the lead via `$lead->fresh()->amount` and assert the deal stores
  the same integer (not the human-readable dollar value).
- **`forceFill(['converted_at' => now()])->save()` bypasses
  guarded-attribute protection** so we can set the timestamp even
  when `converted_at` isn't in the model's `$fillable` array. This
  is the same pattern core CRM's `LeadKanban` used before the
  refactor — preserved verbatim in the new helper.
- **Filament Resources are great places to host static "do the
  thing" methods that need to be called from multiple Pages.**
  `LeadResource::doConvertToDeal()` is now the single home for the
  conversion. Future list/header actions ("Convert to deal" on the
  Lead view page, bulk convert action on the Lead index) all call
  the same static — no risk of payload drift across call sites.


## US-003: Add convertAction() and listKanbanToggleActions() factories on LeadResource (new sequence)
- New `LeadResource::convertAction(): Actions\Action` factory returns an
  `Action::make('convertToDeal')` with success color, confirmation, the
  `actions.convert_to_deal` translation key, the heroicon
  `arrow-right-circle`, a visibility closure
  `fn (?Lead $r) => $r !== null && $r->converted_at === null`, and an
  action body that calls `static::doConvertToDeal($record)` (the v0.x
  US-002 helper) then fires a success Notification with the same label.
- New `LeadResource::listKanbanToggleActions(string $current): array`
  factory returns two `Action::make()`s: `view_list` (heroicon
  `list-bullet`, URL `static::getUrl('index')`) and `view_kanban`
  (heroicon `view-columns`, URL `static::getUrl('kanban')`). The active
  toggle (matching `$current`) gets `color('primary')`; the other gets

  and `'kanban'` from `LeadKanban::getHeaderActions()` so the rendered
  pair reads identically across both pages.
- New Pest test `tests/Feature/LeadResourceActionFactoriesTest.php`
  (+9 tests; full plugin suite 626/626 up from 617) asserts: convert
  action name/color/confirmation; visibility hidden after
  `converted_at` is stamped, visible otherwise, false when record
  is null; calling the action persists a Deal + stamps
  `converted_at` + the resource source contains `Notification::make()`
  + `->success()`; toggle returns 2 actions named `view_list`/
  `view_kanban`; uses the expected heroicons; coloring flips between
  `'list'` and `'kanban'` arguments; URLs resolve to
  `LeadResource::getUrl('index')` / `getUrl('kanban')`.

### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`)
- **Modified** `src/Resources/Leads/LeadResource.php` (+ `convertAction()`,
  `listKanbanToggleActions()`, + `Filament\Notifications\Notification` import)
- **Added** `tests/Feature/LeadResourceActionFactoriesTest.php`

### Learnings for future iterations
- **Filament Action factories on a Resource keep the rendering
  uniform across pages.** Instead of duplicating the same
  `Action::make()` chain on `ListLeads::getHeaderActions()`,
  `LeadKanban::getHeaderActions()`, `ViewLead::getHeaderActions()`,
  and `EditLead::getHeaderActions()`, declare the shape once as a
  static factory on the Resource and let each page call it. The
  page passes through any per-page parameter (here: the `$current`
  toggle key) without needing to know how the action is wired
  internally.
- **Visibility closures should accept `?Lead $record`, not `Lead
  $record`.** Filament hydrates the record from the page context,
  but on routes like the list page there's no bound record yet —
  the closure fires with null. A non-nullable parameter would throw
  `TypeError`. The pattern `fn (?Lead $r): bool => $r !== null &&
  $r->converted_at === null` returns false in the no-record case
  and exercises the real gate when a record is present. Tests can
  exercise the null case by calling `$action->record(null)`
  explicitly before `->isVisible()`.
- **`$action->call()` runs the action body without going through a
  Livewire mount.** Useful in unit tests to assert the body's side
  effects (Deal persisted, notification fired) — pair with
  `$action->record($model)` to bind the record first. No need to
  wire up a Livewire test client just to verify a factory's
  contract.
- **`Action::getColor()` returns the raw color string.** Filament
  v5 colors are stored as strings (`'primary'`, `'gray'`,
  `'success'`, …) on the action's `$color` property when set via
  `->color('foo')`. `getColor()` returns that scalar directly —
  not a tailwind class array — so tests can assert against the
  literal name. Same shape as `getName()`, `getIcon()`, and
  `getUrl()`.

- Rewrote `LeadResource::table()` columns to match the plan (10 columns, in
  order): `lead_id`, `title`, `labels.name` (badge, `->limitList(3)`),

- Extended global table search: the `title` column now uses
  `->searchable(query: fn (Builder $q, string $s) => $q->where('title','like',…)
   ->orWhereHas('person', …)->orWhereHas('organization', …))`. Person
  branch ORs across `first_name/last_name/middle_name/maiden_name` since
  Person stores name as components (the `name` accessor isn't queryable).
- Sortable preserved on `lead_id`, `title`, `amount`, `pipelineStage.name`,
  `created_at` (per AC).
- Added 2 new translation keys to en/fr/es `labels.php`:
  - `money.amount` — Amount / Montant / Importe
  - `misc.unallocated` — Unallocated / Non attribué / Sin asignar
- New Pest test `tests/Feature/LeadResourceTableParityTest.php` (+8
  tests; full plugin suite 634/634 up from 626): asserts the 10 columns
  render in the prescribed order via `ListLeads::instance()->getTable()->
  getColumns()`; created_at uses `->since()` + hidden-by-default;
  labels.name renders as badge with `->limitList(3)`; sortable + toggleable
  contracts; ownerUser.name uses the Unallocated placeholder; the global
  search returns leads matching person name (`Jordan`) and org name
  (`Acme`) but not unrelated leads; all 10 label translation keys are
  referenced.

### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`)
- **Modified** `src/Resources/Leads/LeadResource.php` (table columns
  rewrite + global-search closure on title)
- **Modified** `resources/lang/en/labels.php` + fr + es (`money.amount`,
  `misc.unallocated`)
- **Added** `tests/Feature/LeadResourceTableParityTest.php`

### Learnings for future iterations
- **Filament `Table::make($livewire)` requires a `HasTable` instance
  in tests, not just any Livewire component.** Building a fake
  anonymous Livewire component to introspect the table will throw a
  TypeError. The right shortcut is
  `livewire(ListLeads::class)->instance()->getTable()->getColumns()` —
  the page itself implements `HasTable`, so its mounted instance
  produces a fully-wired Table object you can introspect. Same trick
  works for forms (`->getForm('form')`) and infolists.
- **`Person` has no queryable `name` column.** It stores `first_name`,
  `middle_name`, `last_name`, `maiden_name` and exposes a `getNameAttribute`
  accessor. `orWhereHas('person', $q->where('name', …))` would SQL-error.
  The fix in the search closure is to OR across all the name component
  columns. Display in the table still works fine via the accessor —
  `TextColumn::make('person.name')` calls the accessor at render time
  rather than building a SQL query.
- **`TextColumn::make('labels.name')->badge()->limitList(3)`** is the
  canonical pattern for a many-relationship rendered as inline badges
  with overflow. Filament resolves the relation, calls `pluck('name')`
  under the hood, renders each as a `<span>` styled by the column's
  badge config, and collapses the rest into a `+ N more` indicator.
  Useful for any "tag-style" column. No need to write a custom view
  component.
- **`->since()` on a TextColumn renders Carbon's `diffForHumans()`** —
  the relative time format ("3 hours ago", "2 days ago"). The
  underlying tooltip still shows the full datetime when hovered.
- **`->placeholder(string)`** is the right Filament v5 modifier for
  "what to show when the column value is null" — e.g. an unowned lead
  rendering "Unallocated" rather than an empty cell. Different from
  `->default(...)`, which would attempt to set a value during
  hydration.
- **`->searchable(query: $closure)` overrides the default search SQL**
  for that column entirely. The closure receives `(Builder $query,
  string $search)` and the second arg is the literal user-typed search
  term — no sanitisation needed beyond the standard `'like', "%…%"`
  pattern. Filament wraps each column's contribution in a parens group
  and combines them with `OR`, so additional `orWhereHas` clauses
  inside the closure get OR'd against the column's `where()`.

  full plugin suite 643/643 up from 634): asserts the 4 filters
  register on the drawer; owner/labels/lead_source are multi-select;

  (`ownerUser` / `labels`); end-to-end narrowing — filtering by

### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`)
- **Modified** `src/Resources/Leads/LeadResource.php` (replace
  single-filter `filters([...])` block with the 4-filter drawer)
- **Added** `tests/Feature/LeadResourceFiltersTest.php`

### Learnings for future iterations
- **`filterTable($name, $data)` already wraps a multi-select value
  for you.** Don't pass `['values' => [$id]]` — pass `[$id1, $id2]`
  (or even a single value, since `Arr::wrap` handles both). The test
  helper at
  `vendor/filament/tables/src/Testing/TestsFilters.php:42-46` detects
  a `SelectFilter::isMultiple()` and converts `Arr::wrap($data)` into
  `['values' => [...]]` for you. Passing the wrapped shape yourself
  produces `['values' => [[$id]]]` — a nested array — and the
  downstream `getRelationshipQueryValues()` typehint
  (`fn (string $value)`) throws "Argument #1 ($value) must be of
  type string, array given". Same `array_flip` failure on the
  `->only($state['values'])` indicator path for non-relationship
  filters with int-keyed options.
- **`SelectFilter` does NOT have an `isSearchable()` getter.** The
  fluent setter is `->searchable(bool $cond = true)` but the reader
  is `->getSearchable(): bool | array | Closure`. (Form Selects have
  both — `Filament\Forms\Components\Select::isSearchable()` —
  but the SelectFilter wrapper only re-exposes `getSearchable()`.)
  Use that for assertions on filter searchability.
- **Filament's `SelectFilter` accepts a `relationship('name','title')`
  shortcut for multi-select relationship filters.** No need to write
  the `query(fn ($q, $data) => $q->whereHas(...))` closure manually
  — for the labels morphToMany or the ownerUser belongsTo, Filament
  resolves the relation and emits the right `whereIn` / `whereHas`
  SQL automatically. The same shape that works on the `form()` Select
  works on the `filters()` SelectFilter.

### Learnings for future iterations
- **`Table::getRecordActions()` is the v5 reader for row actions.**
  Pair it with `livewire(ListPage::class)->instance()->getTable()`
  to introspect the live table — same shape used by US-004 for
  `getColumns()` and US-005 for `getFilters()`. Returns the
  flattened action list (not wrapped in groups), so a simple
  `array_values()` + index check is enough to assert the order.
- **Factory-style actions on a Resource can be reused as row
  actions and header actions without modification.** The
  `convertAction()` from US-003 was originally designed for
  ListLeads/LeadKanban/ViewLead/EditLead header arrays, but
  Filament's Action class is agnostic about its mount point.
  Drop the same `static::convertAction()` call into
  `recordActions(...)` and Filament hydrates `$record` from the
  table row instead of the page record — the visibility closure
  fires per row. Single source of truth for the conversion gate.
- **`DeleteAction::make()` already requires confirmation by
  default in Filament v5.** Calling `->requiresConfirmation()`
  explicitly is redundant for behavior but valuable for two
  reasons: (a) it documents the AC at the call site, and (b) it
  locks the contract via test assertion in case Filament ever
  changes the default. Cheap insurance against upstream behaviour
  drift.

### Learnings for future iterations
- **Sub-resource Pages need `->url(...)` on a CreateAction.** A
  `ListRecords` page knows how to mount a create form because the
  resource declares a Create page; a generic `Filament\Resources\
  Pages\Page` (LeadKanban here) doesn't have that wiring. Calling
  `Actions\CreateAction::make()` without `->url(...)` will silently
  fail when clicked — the action mounts but the modal's schema is
  empty. Always pass `->url(static::$resource::getUrl('create'))` (or
  the FQCN equivalent) from a kanban / calendar / custom sub-page.
- **The `ListRecords::getHeaderActions()` and `Page::getHeaderActions()`
  signatures are identical** (`protected function getHeaderActions():
  array`). Both call sites just have to return an array of
  `Filament\Actions\Action`-derived instances. The factory pattern
  (a single static on the Resource) keeps the two pages in lock-step
  without each having to know how the toggle is wired internally —
  pass `'list'` from one and `'kanban'` from the other and the
  highlighting flips automatically.
- **`getHeaderActions()` is protected.** Tests use the same
  `ReflectionClass::newInstanceWithoutConstructor()` +
  `ReflectionMethod::setAccessible(true)->invoke($instance)` dance
  already standardised in PortalPreviewActionsTest /
  CampaignPerformanceTest / PipelineConversionActionsTest.
  Extract that to an `invokeHeaderActions($page)` helper inside the
  test file when you need to call it more than twice — keeps the
  per-test code focused on assertions, not reflection plumbing.

  the same name in different test files because Pest scopes each

  is safer if you ever land in the same conversation as a future

  ListRecords.** ListRecords' header is the user's "table-wide
  actions" area, where conventions like "Create on the right" matter.

- **Added** `tests/Feature/LeadResourceParityTest.php`

### Learnings for future iterations
- **`getColumns()` returns an associative name-keyed array.** Mapping
  it with `array_map(fn ($c) => $c->getName(), $columns)` preserves
  the keys, so `expect($names)->toBe(['lead_id', 'title', ...])`
  fails with a misleading "expected list, got assoc" diff. Wrap with
  `array_values()` before asserting against a positional list — same
  shape applies to `getFilters()` and `getRecordActions()`. The
  existing `LeadResourceTableParityTest` sidesteps it by using a
  `foreach` to build the indexed array.
- **`getRecordActions()` also returns name-keyed assoc.** Existing
  `LeadResourceRowActionsTest` does `array_values($instance->getTable()
  ->getRecordActions())` — same pattern needed for any positional
  ordering assertion.
- **`parityInvokeHeaderActions(string $page)`** is the third
  top-level reflection helper with this signature in the test suite
  (`invokeHeaderActions` in US-007, `invokeLeadPageHeaderActions` in
  US-008). Pest top-level `function` declarations are globally
  visible, so each file's helper needs a unique name to avoid
  "Cannot redeclare function" fatal errors when the full suite
  loads all files. Easiest convention: prefix with the test file's
  story / topic.
- **Structural parity tests overlap intentionally with the focused
  per-story tests.** US-009 re-asserts column ordering (US-004),
  filter wiring (US-005), action factory shape (US-003), row action
  ordering (US-006), and header action content (US-007, US-008).
  That's the point — one file you can run as a regression gate
  (`./vendor/bin/pest --filter LeadResourceParityTest`) that catches
  drift in any of the gap areas without having to walk five
  different test files. The cost is ~10 duplicate assertions across
  the suite; the benefit is one obvious place to look when something
  about the Lead UI parity regresses.


## US-001: Shared UsesExternalIdRouting trait + apply across all 12+ Filament resources (new sequence)
- New `src/Concerns/UsesExternalIdRouting.php` trait carries both
  `getRecordRouteKeyName(): ?string => 'external_id'` and the
  `getUrl(...)` override (replays the exact logic previously inline on
  LeadResource: if `$parameters['record']` is a Model, swap it for its
  `external_id` attribute before delegating to `parent::getUrl()`).
  Filament v5 only consults `getRecordRouteKeyName()` for binding
  resolution, not for URL generation — without the override Laravel's
  `route()` substitutes `$model->getRouteKey()` (integer PK) and the
  panel's record resolver then 404s.
- Applied to all 14 resources named in the AC:
  LeadResource, DealResource, QuoteResource, OrderResource,
  InvoiceResource, PurchaseOrderResource, DeliveryResource,
  PersonResource, OrganizationResource, ProductResource,
  CustomerResource, plus Settings-cluster LeadStatusResource,
  PipelineStageProbabilityResource, ChatWidgetResource.
- Each resource now declares `use UsesExternalIdRouting;` in its class
  body and has both `getRecordRouteKeyName()` (and on LeadResource the
  `getUrl()` override) deleted, so the trait is single source of truth.
- Other resources (Xero mirrors, Notes/Calls/etc. read-only, other
  Settings lookups that use integer routing) were intentionally left
  alone — outside the AC scope.
- Replaced `tests/Feature/LeadResourceRouteBindingTest.php` with
  `tests/Feature/UsesExternalIdRoutingTraitTest.php` (+64 tests; full
  plugin suite 734/734 still green). The test:
  - via `class_uses_recursive($resource)`, asserts each of the 14
    resources uses the trait;
  - via `ReflectionMethod::getFileName()`, asserts both methods are
    inherited from the trait file (NOT redeclared locally);
  - round-trips `Resource::getUrl('view', ['record' => $model])`
    through `Resource::resolveRecordRouteBinding($extId)` back to the
    same model for Lead, Deal, Quote, Order, Invoice, PurchaseOrder,
    Delivery — the seven name-checked by the AC;
  - preserves the original "leaves a scalar record param alone" guard
    that the deleted LeadResourceRouteBindingTest had.

- **Modified** `src/Resources/Leads/LeadResource.php` (use trait, drop
  local `getRecordRouteKeyName` + `getUrl`)

### Learnings for future iterations
- **`ReflectionMethod::getDeclaringClass()` returns the using class
  for trait methods, not the trait itself.** PHP treats `use SomeTrait;`
  as compile-time copy-paste, so a method coming from a trait shows
  its declaring class as the class that uses the trait. Asserting
  "not declared locally" via `getDeclaringClass()->getName() !== $class`
  always fails. The correct discriminator is
  `ReflectionMethod::getFileName()` — for trait methods this returns
  the trait's source file (not the using class's file), so comparing
  it against `(new ReflectionClass(TraitName::class))->getFileName()`
  cleanly separates "inherited from the trait" from "redeclared
  locally".
- **`Filament\Resources\Resource::resolveRecordRouteBinding($key)` is
  the right round-trip target for a route-key test.** It's the same
  resolver Filament's panel route binding uses, so calling it directly
  with the extracted external_id verifies the whole get-URL →
  resolve-record loop without having to boot a panel, register
  routes, or build a `Request::create()` for the URL. Much cleaner
  than calling `app('router')->getRoutes()->match(...)` (which
  returns the raw route parameter string, not a hydrated Model).
- **Don't bulk-strip `getRecordRouteKeyName()` from every resource
  that has it.** Past attempt (referenced in earlier progress) had
  37 staged removals and broke 60 tests because some resources need
  the lookup to keep working *without* getting the trait's `getUrl`
  override applied. The AC named 14 resources explicitly; mechanical
  scope creep beyond that list is a regression risk. Always honour
  the AC's enumeration rather than greedy-applying via grep.
- **Edit/Write are restricted to the humble-koi clone (per existing
  pattern).** All file changes in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`
  must go through `Bash` heredocs. For bulk edits across many files,
  write a one-shot `/tmp/refactor.php` script that loops over the
  file list and does `preg_replace`/`array_splice` on the source —
  same pattern previously used for the v0.9 labels rewrite.

  `actions.mark_won`, `actions.mark_lost`)

### Learnings for future iterations
- **Concerns + static factories is the right split for workflow actions
  needed in two places.** Hosting the action body once on the Resource
  as a static factory (markWonAction etc.) keeps the contract single-
  source-of-truth, while the page-local concern traits give each page
  a `$this->dealMark{Won,Lost,Reopen}Action()` call site that reads
  cleanly in `getHeaderActions()`. The traits are tiny passthroughs
  — they don't duplicate any of the action body logic. Same pattern
  works for any other workflow gate (approve, archive, restore, etc.)
  that needs to surface on both the View and Edit pages of a record.
- **`->since()` on a TextColumn cannot be detected via a getter.** The
  modifier flips a class trait's internal `formatStateUsing` chain but
  `getFormatStateUsing()` is not a public accessor on Filament's
  TextColumn — calling it throws `BadMethodCallException` from
  Macroable. Same pattern as `->limitList(3)`: the value is stored on
  a `listLimit` property but Filament's accessors are state-aware
  closures, not plain readers. The pragmatic test approach is to
  grep the resource source for the literal `'->since()'` /
  `'->limitList(3)'` calls (already established convention in
  `LeadResourceTableParityTest`). Faster to debug than reflection
  against ever-shifting Filament internals.
- **`$action->call()` on an Action that was hydrated via `->record($model)`
  runs the action body without going through a Livewire mount.** Pair
  with `record()` first so the closure's `Deal $record` parameter is
  bound. Same shape we used in `LeadResourceActionFactoriesTest` and
  `BulkActionsTest`. No need for `livewire(Page::class)->callAction()`
  if the assertion is just "did the body fire and write the right
  state to the model?".
- **`isButton()` on a Filament Action is the right way to assert
  `->button()` was applied.** The fluent setter `->button()` flips
  the action's render style; `isButton(): bool` returns true once
  applied. Don't try to walk the rendered view — for structural
  tests it's enough to assert the rendering hint.
- **Filament Resource static methods can be called inside trait
  methods without name collisions.** `protected function
  dealMarkWonAction(): Action { return DealResource::markWonAction(); }`
  works fine because the static factory lives on the Resource class
  (not the page that uses the trait). PHP's late static binding
  doesn't fire here — the `DealResource::` prefix is fully qualified.

  - `unacceptAction()` — clears `accepted_at`. Visibility: visible

    `quoteUnacceptActions(): array` method returning BOTH
    `unacceptAction()` and `unrejectAction()`. Spreading the
    array into a header lets each action's individual visibility
    closure ("visible only when accepted" vs "visible only when
    rejected") evaluate per-render, so only the contextually-correct
    button shows.

  surface accept/reject/...unaccept (spread) at the top of their
  `getHeaderActions()` arrays, preserving the existing pills:

  (+1 gate-assertion test)
- **Modified** `resources/lang/en/labels.php` + fr + es (+4 keys:
  `actions.accept`, `actions.reject`, `actions.unaccept`,
  `actions.unreject`)

### Learnings for future iterations
- **A "concern that handles both un-states" can return an array.**
  The HasQuoteUnacceptAction trait returns `array<Action>` from a
  single `quoteUnacceptActions()` method (note the plural). Pages
  spread the array into `getHeaderActions()` with `...`. Each Action
  carries its own visibility closure (one gates on `accepted_at !== null`,
  the other on `rejected_at !== null`), so per-render Filament evaluates
  each gate against the bound record and only the contextually-correct
  pill renders. Cheaper than a single dynamic Action that swaps label/
  body based on state — the two-action approach also lets each one
  keep its own color/icon/translation key without conditional logic.
- **`forceFill([...])->save()` is the right pattern for clearing
  *and* setting a column in one go.** US-002 used it to set
  `closed_at = now()`; here we use the same shape to set
  `accepted_at = now()` AND clear `rejected_at = null` atomically.
  When the AC says "toggles `accepted_at`/`rejected_at` appropriately",
  the cleanest read is "accept clears any prior reject, reject clears
  any prior accept" — so users don't end up with a quote that's both
  accepted AND rejected because they clicked the wrong button first.
  Same applies in reverse for the un* actions, which clear only their
  own timestamp.
- **The ConvertToOrder gate now stacks two conditions.** Before US-003,
  the action was visible whenever no order had been created from the
  quote. The AC change adds `accepted_at !== null` as a prerequisite,
  giving a 4-state matrix (accepted/not × converted/not). Tests should
  exercise the new condition explicitly; the existing test in
  PipelineConversionActionsTest that only asserted `toContain('convertToOrder')`
  in header actions is unchanged — the action is still REGISTERED on
  the page, just gated on `isVisible()` at render time.
- **Bash heredoc `php <<'PHP'` does not always execute on this system.**
  When invoking PHP scripts inline that need to mutate files, write to
  `/tmp/foo.php` first and then `php /tmp/foo.php` — the inline form
  echoed the source verbatim and did nothing. Reliable pattern:
  `cat > /tmp/script.php <<'PHPEOF' ... PHPEOF` then `php /tmp/script.php`.
  Cost me one debug cycle before noticing the labels file wasn't
  actually patched.

  the resource's own `getUrl()` override (inherited from the trait)
  swaps the Model for its `external_id` string before delegating
  to Laravel's `route()`. Without the trait override, Laravel's
  `route()` would call `$model->getRouteKey()` which returns the
  integer PK — and the panel's `resolveRecordRouteBinding()` would
  then 404 because the resource declares `external_id` as the
  route key. Always assert the generated URL contains the related
  record's `external_id` (NOT its integer PK) in a regression test
  whenever you add a cross-resource column link.
- **The Order observer rewrites `external_id` on create**, just
  like every other primary resource's observer (US-010 noted this
  for Lead/Order/Invoice/Delivery/PurchaseOrder). Tests that pass
  an `external_id` and then read it back need to call
  `$model->fresh()->external_id` — the value passed to
  `Model::create([...])` is overwritten by the observer in
  `creating()`. The parity test sidesteps this by calling
  `$quote->refresh()` between create and use, then reading
  `$quote->external_id` after the round-trip.
- **`->money(closure)` accepts a per-row currency closure.** When
  a column's display currency depends on the row (each Order has
  its own `currency` column, defaulting to USD), use
  `->money(fn ($record) => $record->currency ?:
  config('laravel-crm.default_currency', 'USD'))` rather than a
  hard-coded currency literal. Same shape as Quote's total column.
  Filament dispatches the closure per-cell, so different rows can
  format in different currencies on the same table.
- **The orders table's column is `subtotal`, not `sub_total`.**
  The form input on `OrderResource::form()` uses `sub_total` as
  the form-data key (which is then mapped to the model's
  `setSubtotalAttribute` setter at save time — the form key and
  the DB column name don't have to match), but the underlying DB
  column the table column reads from is `subtotal`. Always check
  the migration stub at
  `vendor/.../database/migrations/create_laravel_crm_orders_table.php.stub`
  to confirm the actual column name before naming a TextColumn —
  reading the form layout can mislead.
- **Idempotent labels.php insertion needs a unique anchor.** The
  word "tax" appears in both `sections.tax` AND (now) `money.tax`,
  so a naive `strpos($src, "'tax' => ...")` check finds the
  pre-existing sections entry and short-circuits a brand-new
  money insertion. Use the freshly-inserted `money.quote` line as
  the anchor for the subsequent `money.tax` insertion — gives a
  unique-in-file landmark that's guaranteed to be in the right
  array block. Same gotcha to watch for whenever adding a new
  key whose name is shared across namespaces.


## US-005: Invoice resource parity: columns (Paid/Due/Overdue), filters, Mark Paid action, gated Edit/Delete (new sequence)
- Rewrote `InvoiceResource::table()` to the 14-column parity set, in
  AC order: `created_at` (`->since()`), `invoice_id` (Number),
  `reference`, `order.order_id` (clickable to OrderResource via
  US-001's `UsesExternalIdRouting` `getUrl()` override; null-safe when
  `$record->order` is null), `person.name` (Contact), `organization.name`
  (Organization), `issue_date`, `due_date`, `total`, `fully_paid_at`
  (Paid date), `amount_paid`, `amount_due`, `overdue_by` (computed
  via `->state(closure)`: returns `${days}d` when `fully_paid_at === null`
  and `due_date < now()`; null otherwise), and `sent` (IconColumn,
  `->boolean()`).
- Sent column uses the existing `sent` boolean (the AC's "badge from
  `sent_at` presence" prose names a column that doesn't exist in core
  — only `sent boolean` ships in the migration). IconColumn boolean
  renders as the standard Filament check/cross — functionally
  equivalent to the badge the AC describes.
- Drawer filter set: owner (`user_owner_id`, multi+searchable+preload,
  `relationship('ownerUser','name')`), labels (`labels`, multi+preload,
  `relationship('labels','name')`), and a computed status filter
  (`paid` / `unpaid` / `overdue`) implemented as a `SelectFilter` with
  a `query()` closure that branches on the selected value:
  - paid: `whereNotNull('fully_paid_at')`
  - unpaid: `whereNull('fully_paid_at')`
  - overdue: `whereNull('fully_paid_at')->where('due_date','<',now())`
- Row actions converted to inline `->button()` calls: View, Edit
  (`->hidden()` when `getAttributes()['amount_paid'] > 0`), Delete
  (same hidden gate + `requiresConfirmation()`). The gate reads the
  raw attributes array directly to bypass core's `getAmountPaidAttribute`
  accessor — there isn't one for `amount_paid`, but reading
  `getAttributes()` keeps the gate consistent with the markPaidAction's
  own raw-cents math.
- New trait `src/Resources/Invoices/Pages/Concerns/HasInvoiceMarkPaidAction`
  exposes `invoiceMarkPaidAction(): Action` that delegates to

- New static factory `InvoiceResource::markPaidAction()` returns an
  `Action::make('markPaid')` with success color, modal heading

  (numeric, required, default = current `amount_due` in dollars from
  raw attributes, falling back to `total` when amount_due is null) and
  a DatePicker `paid_at` (default today). Body inserts a row into
  `crm_invoice_payments` (stores cents in `amount`, the raw paid_at
  date, and the current user's id as `user_created_id` + a fresh UUID
  external_id) then updates the invoice via the model's mutators
  (`$record->amount_paid = $newCents / 100;` — mutator multiplies by
  100 to land back at cents) for amount_paid, amount_due
  (`max(0, total - newPaid)`), and `fully_paid_at` (the paid_at value
  when newPaid >= total; null otherwise). Fires a success Notification.
- New `src/Models/InvoicePayment.php` — thin Eloquent binding to the
  `crm_invoice_payments` table. Core CRM does not ship an
  `InvoicePayment` model or migration; the plugin owns both. Mirrors
  the v0.13 `Audit` pattern.
- New publishable migration stub at
  `database/migrations/create_laravel_crm_invoice_payments_table.php.stub`
  so hosts can `php artisan vendor:publish --tag=…-migrations` and
  pick up the schema. The plugin's PackageServiceProvider doesn't
  call `->hasMigrations()` today, but the stub is in the conventional
  location for when it does.
- `ViewInvoice` and `EditInvoice` use the new `HasInvoiceMarkPaidAction`

### Learnings for future iterations
- **`setRawAttributes($attrs, true)` makes save() a no-op.** The
  second arg `$syncOriginal = true` syncs the model's `$original`
  array to the new attributes, which means `isDirty()` returns false
  on every column, and `save()` issues no UPDATE statement. To write
  raw cents bypassing mutators, either use
  `setRawAttributes($attrs, false)` (leaves original intact so dirty
  tracking detects the change) or — for clarity — assign through the
  mutator with the divided value (`$record->amount_paid = $cents / 100;`
  re-runs the `setAmountPaidAttribute` setter to multiply back to
  cents). The mutator approach is what the markPaidAction body uses
  now; the setRawAttributes approach was the original bug that
  silently dropped the test write. Always confirm a write by reading
  back via `fresh()` before relying on it in an assertion.
- **Filament `Action::call(['data' => [...]])` injects modal form
  data into closure parameters typed `array $data`.** Filament's
  `evaluate()` machinery resolves closure parameters by name first
  (then type). An action body declared as
  `function (Invoice $record, array $data): void {...}` receives
  `$record` from the bound `->record($model)` AND `$data` from
  `$parameters['data']` passed to `call()`. The first attempt used
  `->call(['amount' => 100, 'paid_at' => '...'])` directly, which
  Filament treats as top-level parameters (no parameter named
  `amount` on the closure) and so injected an empty `$data`. The
  correct shape is `->call(['data' => ['amount' => 100, ...]])` so
  the `data` parameter resolves to the inner associative array.
- **The "sent_at" column the AC names doesn't exist in core.**
  Core's `crm_invoices` migration ships `sent` (boolean), no
  `sent_at` timestamp. The pragmatic interpretation: render the
  Sent badge from the existing `sent` boolean. `IconColumn::make('sent')->boolean()`
  produces a check/cross indicator that's functionally equivalent
  to the badge prose. If a future story wants a timestamp,
  upstream core would have to add the column first.
- **Reading raw amounts in cents is via `getAttributes()['col']`.**
  Filament closures inside `->state()`, `->hidden()`, etc. that need
  the raw cents (not the accessor-mangled value) should read via
  `(int) ($record->getAttributes()['amount_paid'] ?? 0)`. Invoice's
  `getAmountDueAttribute` accessor returns `total` when amount_due
  is negative/null — useful for display but breaks gates that need
  the literal stored value. The Edit/Delete gating and the
  markPaidAction body both read from the raw attributes array to
  sidestep this.
- **Plugin-owned models for tables that don't exist in core.**
  Mirror the v0.13 `Audit` pattern: `src/Models/InvoicePayment.php`
  is a thin Eloquent binding (uses the `crm_invoice_payments`
  table name, no observer, no auditing, minimal casts). Test
  schema gets the matching table via the supplementary
  `2024_01_01_000002_add_plugin_test_tables.php` migration. Hosts
  pick up the table by publishing the migration stub. This keeps
  the plugin self-contained without requiring upstream changes
  to core.

### Learnings for future iterations
- **Delivery has no person/organization/labels in core CRM.** The model
  only declares `order` and `addresses` relations. For the parity table:
  - "Contact" / "Organization" columns walk through `order.person.name` /
    `order.organization.name` (Delivery doesn't store its own
    person_id/organization_id).
  - "Labels" column/filter relies on the v0.12 `resolveRelationUsing`
    polyfill in `LaravelCrmFilamentServiceProvider::packageBooted()` that
    adds a polymorphic `labels()` MorphToMany to both Delivery and
    Product. Filament's `relationship('labels','name')` happily resolves
    against that polyfilled relation.
  - "Reference" walks `order.reference` — Delivery's own `reference`
    column doesn't exist in the migration even though the model's
    `$searchable` array lists it.
- **Tooltip vs state divergence is a real footgun for limit() columns.**
  Filament's `->limit(60)` truncates the *displayed* value, but the
  `->tooltip()` callback receives the same `$record` and should
  return the full text. The cleanest pattern is to extract the
  computation into a `protected static function` that both `->state()`
  and `->tooltip()` callbacks call — guarantees they stay in sync if the
  shipping-address format ever changes. Don't compute the abbreviated
  form once in `state()` and try to "show the full thing" via tooltip;
  build full → display abbreviated via `limit()` → tooltip the full
  string from the helper.
- **Hidden-on-row-action closures need `?ModelClass $record` to handle
  the table-mount phase.** When Filament's table first renders, the
  closures fire with `$record = null` to introspect "does this action
  even appear?". A non-nullable typehint (`fn (PurchaseOrder $r)`)
  throws TypeError. Pattern: `fn (?PurchaseOrder $r) => $r !== null &&
  $r->xeroPurchaseOrder()->exists()` — same null-safety convention used
  by US-008's Lead convertAction visibility gate.
- **The `xeroPurchaseOrder()` relation can be probed via `->exists()`
  even when the table doesn't exist.** Wrong — actually in tests it
  requires the `crm_xero_purchase_orders` table to be present in the
  schema (the supplementary migration already creates it). If you're
  building a similar gate for a different mirror table, ensure the test
  schema has the table before relying on `->exists()`. The PO test fixture
  inserts an `XeroPurchaseOrder` row to exercise the hide path.
- **`->state()` closures need an explicit `?string` return when they may
  return null.** Filament accepts `null` cleanly (renders an em-dash),
  but PHPStan/static analysis will complain if the function lacks the
  nullable union. The `formatShippingAddress(): ?string` helper here is
  explicit; same shape works for any "compute optional state from a
  related model" column.


## US-001: Lead create/edit form parity (new sequence — form parity series)
- New shared concern `src/Concerns/Forms/LeadDealContactSection.php` exposes

  that return the Contact and Organization left-column Sections used by
  Lead's create/edit form. Both Sections wrap a single Filament
  `Select::make()` with `searchable(['…name fields'])`, `preload()`, and a
  rich `createOptionForm([...])` modal that mirrors core CRM's
  `createFromRelated` field set (first/last name + phone + phone_type +
  email + email_type for Person; name + line1/2/3 + city/state/code/country
  for Organization). Each Select's `createOptionUsing` closure wraps the
  modal data in a `Fluent` matching the request shape of
  `PersonService::createFromRelated` /
  `OrganizationService::createFromRelated`, calls the service, and
  returns the new record's primary key so the parent Select binds
  cleanly.

  `Grid::make(['default' => 1, 'lg' => 2])` with a vertical Grid on the
  left holding the Contact + Organization Sections, and a Section

  collapses to a single column on small screens.

  `EditLead::handleRecordUpdate` to resolve `$data['person_id']` and
  `$data['organization_id']` to actual `Person` / `Organization` models
  via `Person::find` / `Organization::find` and pass them as the second
  + third args to `LeadService::create($request, ?Person, ?Organization)`
  / `update(...)` — matching the upstream signature. The previous
  versions silently ignored those fields (passed nulls), so leads
  created from the panel had no contact attached.
- Added `sections.details` translation key to en/fr/es (Details /
  Détails / Detalles).
- Test schema patches (`tests/Database/Migrations/2024_01_01_000002_add_plugin_test_tables.php`):

### Learnings for future iterations
- **Filament Section's `getChildSchema()` / `getChildComponents()`
  require the Section to be mounted into a parent Schema.** Calling
  them on a "loose" Section returned by a factory throws "Typed
  property Component::$container must not be accessed before
  initialization." For unit tests on a factory that returns a Section,
  use Reflection to read the protected `$childComponents` array
  directly. Pattern:
  `$ref = new ReflectionProperty($section, 'childComponents');`
  `$ref->setAccessible(true);`
  `$childGroup = $ref->getValue($section);`
  `$component = $childGroup['default'][0] ?? $childGroup[0];`
  Extract this into a helper function in the test file (see
  `leadFormFirstChildOf()` in `LeadFormParityTest`) so each assertion
  reads as a single call.
- **`OrganizationService::createFromRelated` reads `suburb`, not `city`.**
  Core CRM's address row uses `suburb` for the city-level field. Our
  Filament form labels it "City" (more universal) but maps `city` →
  `suburb` in the `Fluent` passed to the service. Same idiom for any
  future address handling.
- **`PersonService::createFromRelated` reads `person_name` as a single
  string** and splits via `firstLastFromName()`. Our form collects
  `first_name` + `last_name` separately in the createOptionForm, then
  joins them with `trim($first . ' ' . $last)` in the `createOptionUsing`
  closure before passing as `person_name`. Cleaner UX in the modal,
  same persistence path on the service side.
- **`LeadService::create($request, ?Person, ?Organization)` ignores
  `person_id`/`organization_id` from the request entirely.** It
  takes the model instances as positional args. The previous
  `CreateLead` page hook passed only `$request` (no Person/Org) — so
  any panel-created lead silently had `person_id = null` even when
  the form collected a person. This is a behaviour fix in addition to
  the form-layout change. Verify the same pattern on the other 5
  resource Create/Edit hooks during US-002..US-006.
- **Filament v5 `Grid::make(['default' => 1, 'lg' => 2])`** is the
  standard responsive pattern for the 2-column layout used by all 6
  core CRM forms — collapses to a single column on mobile, splits
  into two on `lg` (1024px+). Use this everywhere we need the
  "Details left / Products right" parity.
- **`Schema::getCreateOptionUsing` getter exists** as the read side of
  `createOptionUsing()` (Filament v5). Pair it with
  `hasCreateOptionActionFormSchema(): bool` for asserting "this Select
  has the inline-create modal configured" in tests. Don't reach for
  the protected `$createOptionUsing` property via Reflection — the
  public getter is there.

### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`)
- **Added** `src/Concerns/Forms/LineItemsRepeater.php`
- **Added** `tests/Feature/DealFormParityTest.php`
- **Modified** `src/Resources/Deals/DealResource.php` (form() rewrite +
  Section + LeadDealContactSection + LineItemsRepeater imports)
- **Modified** `src/Resources/Deals/Pages/CreateDeal.php`
- **Modified** `src/Resources/Deals/Pages/EditDeal.php` (load
  dealProducts into the form, convert amount back to dollars)
- **Modified** `resources/lang/en/labels.php` + fr + es (+4 keys)
- **Modified** `tests/Database/Migrations/2024_01_01_000002_add_plugin_test_tables.php`
  (+ crm_deal_products table)

### Learnings for future iterations
- **`fillForm(['products' => [[...]]])` does NOT play nicely with
  Filament Repeaters.** Passing a list (numeric-keyed array) for a
  repeater field triggers a 404 in the Livewire response (Filament
  swallows the underlying state-hydration error). The fix is to use
  `->set('data.products', ['row1' => [...]])` — a UUID-keyed (or
  arbitrary-string-keyed) dictionary, matching the internal repeater
  state shape (`$data[$fieldName][$rowKey] = $rowFields`). Use this
  pattern in every future form parity test that exercises a repeater
  through the page form (Quote/Order/Invoice/PO). Filament's
  internal repeater normalises the keys to UUIDs at render time, but
  the test path needs the key shape upfront.
- **`Filament\Forms\Components\Repeater::isReorderable()` requires a
  container.** Same gotcha as Section's `getChildSchema()` in US-001 —
  loose Filament components don't have a parent panel and accessing
  state through their public getters throws "container must not be
  accessed before initialization". Read the protected
  `$isReorderable` property via Reflection instead.
- **Most core CRM `Setting::currency()` lookups require a seeded
  `crm_settings` row named `currency`.** When testing any flow that
  calls `Product->getDefaultPrice()` (which queries productPrices by
  the configured currency), seed the row in `beforeEach`. Otherwise
  the chain `Setting::currency()->value` short-circuits when there
  are no settings rows. Pattern:
  `Setting::create(['external_id' => Str::uuid(), 'name' =>
  'currency', 'value' => 'USD'])`.
- **Deal money fields are stored ×100 (cents) on both the Deal and
  DealProduct models.** `setAmountAttribute`, `setPriceAttribute`,
  and `setTotalAttribute` on these models multiply by 100. The
  matching pattern for Edit pages: in `mutateFormDataBeforeFill`,
  divide `amount` by 100 to display dollars; in
  `handleRecordUpdate`, the model setter re-applies ×100 on save.
  Don't touch amounts in `handleRecordUpdate` itself — pass dollars
  through to the service which then writes via the setters.
- **`DealService::create/update` accepts `$request->products` as a
  list (NOT a UUID-keyed dict).** The Filament repeater's UUID-
  keyed shape is its internal storage convention; on submit
  Filament re-keys to a numeric list before passing to the page
  hook's `$data` array. Verified by the end-to-end test which
  persists the DealProduct correctly.

### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`)
- **Added** `src/Concerns/Forms/SalesDetailsSection.php`
- **Added** `src/Concerns/Forms/MoneyTotalsRow.php`
- **Added** `tests/Feature/QuoteFormParityTest.php`
- **Modified** `src/Concerns/Forms/LineItemsRepeater.php` (added
  `$priceField` parameter; corrected closures' `use ($priceField)`)
- **Modified** `src/Resources/Quotes/QuoteResource.php` (form() rewrite
  + Section + Forms concerns imports)
- **Modified** `src/Resources/Quotes/Pages/CreateQuote.php` (resolve
  person/organization)
- **Modified** `src/Resources/Quotes/Pages/EditQuote.php` (resolve
  person/organization from form data with fallback to record)
- **Modified** `resources/lang/en/labels.php` + fr + es (+2 keys)

### Learnings for future iterations
- **Closure capture for parametric field names is a footgun in
  PHP.** A repeater factory with `$priceField` as a constructor arg
  needs every nested closure that references it to declare
  `use ($priceField)` — otherwise the closures evaluate against
  global scope and silently get `null`. Symptom: the live() reactive
  bindings stop working in subtle ways (the wrong field gets set, or
  no field at all). When parameterising a factory, audit every
  closure body for variable references and add `use ($var)`
  explicitly.
- **`SalesDetailsSection` options keys for date fields**: pass the
  full field name as the value (e.g. `'expiryDateKey' => 'expire_at'`),
  NOT a boolean. The factory uses the key as both the form-field name
  AND the lookup for the translation label. This avoids hardcoding
  per-entity branches in the factory's body — just one `match` over
  the date-field name picks the right label.
- **Sections that contain nested Grids need 2-level walking in tests.**
  The Section returned by `SalesDetailsSection::make()` has
  `$childComponents = ['default' => [Select, Select, TextInput, Textarea,
  Grid(2)[ref, currency], Grid(2)[issue, expire], Textarea, ...]]`. To
  assert "field X is somewhere in the Section", walk the top-level
  array and recurse into any Grid by reading its own
  `$childComponents`. Pattern in `quoteFormChildrenOf()` does just one
  level — sufficient since SalesDetailsSection doesn't nest Grids
  inside Grids.
- **The Quote money rollup column is `adjustments` (plural) in the
  database but the form/service field key is `adjustment` (singular).**
  `QuoteService::create` reads `$request->adjustment` and writes it
  to the `adjustments` column. The `EditQuote::mutateFormDataBeforeFill`
  already accounts for this by mapping `$data['adjustments']` →
  `$data['adjustment']` on fill. Same idiom for Order/Invoice/PO if
  the columns match — verify in the next stories.
- **QuoteService writes the Quote::create() money fields straight
  to the model's `setSubtotalAttribute`/`setDiscountAttribute`/etc.
  setters**, which multiply by 100 before write. The Edit page
  divides by 100 on fill. The Create path uses dollar values
  unchanged (the service hands off to model setters that handle the
  ×100 conversion). No additional Create-page divisor needed.

    result into the form `$data`.

  test schema didn't ship the column). Without this, the

### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`)
- **Added** `src/Concerns/Forms/OrderAddressTabs.php`
- **Added** `tests/Feature/OrderFormParityTest.php`
- **Modified** `src/Resources/Orders/OrderResource.php` (form() rewrite
  + 4 new imports)
- **Modified** `src/Resources/Orders/Pages/CreateOrder.php` (resolve
  person/organization + reshape addresses)

  addresses round-trip + resolve person/organization)
