- **Modified** `tests/Database/Migrations/2024_01_01_000002_add_plugin_test_tables.php`
  (+ softDeletes on crm_address_types)

### Learnings for future iterations
- **Filament's `Tabs::make()` + `Tab::make()` pattern**: import both
  `Filament\Schemas\Components\Tabs` and the nested
  `Filament\Schemas\Components\Tabs\Tab` class. Each Tab takes
  `->schema([...])` of components and renders as a clickable tab. Use
  prefixed field names inside each Tab (`'billing_address.line1'`,
  `'shipping_address.line1'`) so Filament's dot-path notation maps the
  state into nested arrays on the form's `$data`.
- **Use a single flat associative array per tab** (e.g.
  `['billing_address' => [..fields..]]`) NOT a numeric-keyed list
  (`['addresses' => [[..]]]`). The dot-prefix on each field name
  binds Filament's state into the right slot automatically, no
  manual array reshape needed at fillForm time.
- **Address type lookups should be by name, not id.** Core's
  `LaravelCrmSampleDataSeeder` references `AddressType::where('name',
  'Billing')->first()->id ?? 5` — the id changes across migrations
  but the name is stable. Mirror this in any concern that needs to
  resolve a type id.
- **`AddressType` ships with `SoftDeletes` in core**, but the plugin's
  test schema didn't include the `deleted_at` column. When
  introducing a feature that queries `AddressType::query()`, audit
  the test schema for missing `deleted_at` — same gotcha applies to
  any softDeleted model.
- **Filament tab content reshape on Edit needs `array_merge`,
  not assignment**, because the page hook's `$data` already contains
  the form fields (title, description, etc.) and we just want to
  *add* the two tab keys. Use
  `$data = array_merge($data, OrderAddressTabs::toFormData($order->addresses))`.

  If a future story removes labels from one of those forms for
  parity reasons, drop that resource from the test's dataset (or
  keep labels in the form even if the AC says "no labels"). The
  labels relationship is a high-value feature and dropping it just
  to mirror core's UI is rarely worth the regression.
- **For SalesDetailsSection consumers that link to a parent record
  (Invoice → Order; PurchaseOrder → Order), pass `'orderLink' =>
  true`.** The Select is rendered as the FIRST field in the Details
  card. The factory's `array_unshift` ensures the order-link Select

### Learnings for future iterations
- **`Filament\Schemas\Components\Utilities\Get`** is the canonical
  type for the `Get $get` closure parameter Filament passes to
  `->visible(fn (Get $get) => ...)` and `->afterStateUpdated(fn (Get
  $get) => ...)`. Import explicitly when the closure references it.
- **The `delivery_address` Select option source needs to be a flat
  `[id => label]` array, not a relation.** `Address` is polymorphic
  via `addressable_type`/`addressable_id`, so we can't use
  Filament's `relationship('addresses', 'line1')` shortcut. Instead,
  the factory queries `Address::where('addressable_type',
  Organization::class)` and joins to Organization names in PHP for
  the label string ("Org Name — line1, city").
- **Sed-based label-file patching with shared keys is fragile.**
  When inserting `sections.delivery_details`, the regex matched the
  first `'products' => '...'` occurrence — which was `money.products`,
  not `sections.products`. Use a more specific lookahead-based regex
  that walks into the `sections =>` block: `('sections' => \[\s*(?:.
  *?\n)*?\s*'products' => '[^']+',)` (non-greedy multi-line match
  to anchor inside the right array). Same pitfall applied to US-002
  with `actions.add_line_item` — be defensive when a key name like
  `products` exists in multiple namespaces.
- **`PurchaseOrderService::update` reads `$request->purchaseOrderLines`
  while `create` reads `$request->products`.** Inconsistency in
  core. The Filament EditPurchaseOrder page handles this by
  pre-copying `$data['products']` into `$data['purchaseOrderLines']`
  before the service call. Mirror this in any future entity whose
  service signature splits create vs update.

### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`)
- **Modified** `src/Concerns/Forms/LineItemsRepeater.php`

### Learnings for future iterations
- **A Repeater's `->columns(1)` plus a nested `Grid::make($n)` inside
  its `->schema([...])` is the cleanest Filament v5 way to render a
  "row of stacked rows" form pattern.** The outer single-column
  schema makes the Hidden FK + Product Select + nested Grid + Comments
  Textarea stack vertically; the nested Grid gives you the
  side-by-side money fields without polluting the outer column count.
  Don't try to do this with the outer Repeater set to 5 cols and
  `->columnSpanFull()` overrides on individual fields — it works
  visually but Filament's layout heuristics keep biting on
  per-component span recalculations whenever you toggle conditional
  fields (here: the optional `tax_amount`).
- **Walk-one-level-into-Grids is the right test helper shape** when a
  schema's structural layout is intentionally split across nested
  Grids but the test cares about the flat leaf-field list. Define a
  small `collectLeafNames(Repeater|Section|Grid)` function per test
  file (or extract to a shared helper if used 5+ times) that reads
  `$childComponents['default']` via Reflection and, when a child is
  a Grid, reads ITS `$childComponents['default']` to splice in the
  inner names. This keeps the per-test assertions focused on the
  field name list rather than the structural layout.
- **`tax_amount` is stored in cents on the line-item tables** for
  every entity in the family (quote_products / invoice_lines /
  order_products / purchase_order_lines / deal_products all use
  `integer('tax_amount')->nullable()`). When hydrating into a
  read-only form field, divide by 100 the same way `price` and
  `amount` are. The line-item model setters don't multiply by 100 on
  save for `tax_amount` (unlike `price` / `amount` which DO multiply)
  — but the field is read-only on the form, so the user can't write
  to it from the panel anyway and any post-service tax recalculation
  would land on a separate field. Worth checking the relevant
  `*Service::update` behavior if any future story makes tax_amount
  editable.
- **Pest top-level `function foo() {}` declarations are file-local
  and visible to every test closure in the file** — but a top-level
  function with the same NAME in two different test files is fine,
  because Pest scopes each test file's function-declaration cycle to
  its own require pass. Different file → different declaration —
  unique helper names per file keep the safety margin, but pure
  collisions are not what causes "undefined function" errors. What
  DID cause them here: my python text-replace script's anchor regex
  failed to match, so the helper was never inserted. Always
  `grep -n helperName tests/Feature/Foo.php` to confirm the helper
  body is actually present BEFORE running pest; otherwise the failure
  message ("undefined function") is the same whether the helper was
  never inserted or was inserted in the wrong file.
- **`./vendor/bin/pint --dirty` only reformats files git considers
  dirty in the index/working tree.** Useful for a focused cleanup
  after a story without reformatting unrelated files. Pair with
  `./vendor/bin/pint --test` for a final pre-commit confirmation.

### Fixup: drop Forms\Get / Forms\Set typehints
- Reactive `live()` callbacks blew up at runtime with
  `TypeError: Argument #2 ($set) must be of type Filament\Forms\Set,
  Filament\Schemas\Components\Utilities\Set given` on the create
  page. The nested `Filament\Schemas\Components\Grid` we now wrap
  the row-2 fields in causes Filament to resolve Set/Get from the
  Schemas namespace rather than the Forms namespace. Pest didn't
  catch this because no test exercises `live()` reactivity end-to-end.
- Fix: drop the Forms\Get / Forms\Set typehints from every closure
  in `LineItemsRepeater::products()`. Filament resolves these by
  parameter name (`$get` / `$set`), not type — so untyped closures
  work for both the Forms-namespace and Schemas-namespace variants.
  Pattern is now: `function ($state, $get, $set) use ($priceField)
  { ... }`. Apply this anywhere a closure inside a Forms component
  could be hosted inside a Schemas container.

- **Edit/Write tools refuse paths outside the humble-koi clone.** Same
  constraint noted across the v0.x and form-parity series. For files in
  `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament` use a `cat > … <<'EOF'`

  rate via `$product->taxRate?->rate` — the `taxRate` accessor returns a
  `TaxRate` model (or null), and the model's `rate` column holds the

  in the global instructions trips bash parsing** when run via Polyscope's
  Bash tool — got an "unexpected EOF" error on the literal subprocess
  syntax. Workaround: pass the commit body as a multi-line double-quoted
  argument and replace internal single-quoted apostrophes (`CRM's` →
  `CRMs`) so the shell doesn't get confused by quoting boundaries. Easier
  than fighting subshell + heredoc + nested quotes.


## US-002: Add per-row recalc helper that computes line amount and tax_amount
- New private static `LineItemsRepeater::recalcRow($get, $set, string $priceField)`
  helper consolidates the per-row math into one code path. Reads
  `unit_price` (or `price` for Deal) and `quantity` from the row, writes
  `amount = unit_price * quantity` (line subtotal — tax NOT included,
  matching core CRM `LiveQuoteItems::calculateAmounts` line 148). When
  `$priceField === 'unit_price'`, resolves the product id from the row's
  `id` field, calls the v0.x `resolveTaxRate()` (US-001), and writes
  `tax_amount = amount * (rate / 100)`. Deal branch (`price`) intentionally
  skips `tax_amount` since deal_products has no such column.
- Pure helper introduction. No call sites yet — the reactive
  `afterStateUpdated` closures still use their inline math (and won't
  trigger form-totals recalc until a later story).
- New Pest test `tests/Feature/LineItemsRepeaterRecalcRowTest.php`
  (+7 tests / 18 assertions; full plugin suite now **845/845**,
  up from 838 in US-007 of the form-parity series): asserts the
  method's reflection contract (private + static + 3 params with
  `priceField: string`); amount math with `unit_price`; amount math
  with Deal `price` AND that `tax_amount` is NOT set; tax_amount via
  `Product->taxRate` relation; tax_amount via default TaxRate fallback;
  tax_amount=0 when no rate resolvable; null-safe handling of null
  unit_price/quantity (both default to 0.0).
- Pint clean.

### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`)
- **Modified** `src/Concerns/Forms/LineItemsRepeater.php`
- **Added** `tests/Feature/LineItemsRepeaterRecalcRowTest.php`

### Learnings for future iterations
- **`ReflectionMethod::invokeArgs(null, [...])` is the right way to
  call a private static helper from a test** without `setAccessible`
  on the call site separately. Pair with closures that capture a
  `$row` array by reference for both `$get` and `$set`, so the test
  can assert on the post-call array shape. Pattern in
  `recalcRowInvoke()` keeps each test's body to a single arrange
  + invoke + expect block, mirroring the form-state get/set
  protocol Filament uses internally.
- **`(float) null === 0.0` in PHP**, so the helper's
  `(float) $get('quantity')` doesn't need explicit null guards.
  Same for `unit_price`. Filament always seeds repeater rows with
  the declared default (1 for quantity), but null-safety means the
  helper can be called from anywhere — including before initial
  state hydration — without TypeError.
- **`tax_amount = amount * (rate / 100)` matches core CRM** exactly
  (`LiveQuoteItems.php:150`). The rate is stored as a percentage
  (e.g. 10 for "10%"), so the division by 100 is necessary. Don't
  use `amount * rate` directly even if a future refactor stores
  the rate as a decimal — keep the helper's math aligned with how
  `TaxRate->rate` is stored in core.


## US-003: Add form-totals recalc helper using Filament relative paths
- New private static `LineItemsRepeater::recalcFormTotals($get, $set)` aggregates
  sibling rows up to the form-level `sub_total`, `tax`, and `total` fields by
  reading `$get('../../')` (the rows array keyed by row UUID), summing each
  row's `amount` into `../../../sub_total` and each `tax_amount` into
  `../../../tax`, then writing `total = sub_total + tax` to `../../../total`.
  Discount and adjustment are NOT included — matches core CRM
  `LiveQuoteItems.php:155-161` exactly (those are applied server-side at save).
- Pure helper introduction — no call sites yet. A later story will wire it into
  the row's reactive `afterStateUpdated` closures so changing a line's unit
  price / quantity / product fans out into a recompute of the entire footer.
- Values cast to float defensively via `(float) ($row['amount'] ?? 0)`, so
  numeric strings and nulls are handled without TypeError. Null result from
  `$get('../../')` (when no rows are hydrated yet) defaults to `[]` and the
  three fields all write 0.0.

### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`)
- **Modified** `src/Concerns/Forms/LineItemsRepeater.php` (+ `recalcFormTotals`
  private static helper)
- **Added** `tests/Feature/LineItemsRepeaterRecalcFormTotalsTest.php` (+7
  tests / 23 assertions)

### Learnings for future iterations
- **Filament's relative-path resolution from inside a Repeater row's reactive
  closure follows a predictable stair-step**: `..` walks up one level in the
  state tree. From inside a row field (`data.products.{uuid}.unit_price`):
  - `../` → `{uuid}` (the row itself)
  - `../../` → `products` (the rows-array map, keyed by UUID)
  - `../../../X` → `data.X` (a sibling field at the form level)
  Cache this as the canonical path layout for any future "row → form totals"
  recalc. Don't try `$get('data.sub_total')` or absolute paths — Filament's
  `Get/Set` resolve relative to the closure's host component, so absolute
  forms fail silently.
- **`$get('../../')` returns either an array or null** depending on whether
  the parent state has been hydrated yet. The first frame of a freshly
  mounted repeater can return null while Filament is still threading the
  initial state through. Always `?? []` the result before `foreach` —
  iterating over null would TypeError under PHP 8.x strict.
- **Tests for relative-path helpers can be invoked without a Filament
  context** by passing two test-local closures that act as a fake Get/Set.
  The closure captures a `$rows` array (for Get) and a `$form` array by
  reference (for Set), and translates the three known relative paths into
  array assignments. Cleaner than mounting a full Filament Form just to
  exercise the math. Same pattern as `recalcRowInvoke()` from US-002 —
  consider extracting to a shared test helper if more relative-path
  helpers land.

### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`)
- **Modified** `src/Concerns/Forms/LineItemsRepeater.php`
- **Added** `tests/Feature/LineItemsRepeaterProductSelectAutofillTest.php`

### Learnings for future iterations
- **The `ProductPrice` model has NO `price` column or accessor — the only
  catalog-price column is `unit_price`** (stored ×100, multiplied by 100
  on save via `setUnitPriceAttribute`). The original code's `$price->price`
  was returning null, so `null / 100 === 0` silently overwrote whatever
  manual price the user had typed. Always cross-reference the
  `vendor/.../database/migrations/create_laravel_crm_*_table.php.stub`
  before naming a model attribute — even when the prose name ("price")
  reads naturally, the actual column may use a different name.
- **PHP arrow functions (`fn () => ...`) capture by value, not by
  reference.** When writing test helpers that simulate Filament's
  `$get`/`$set` callables with a shared `$row` array, the `$get` closure
  must be a regular `function (string $key) use (&$row) { ... }` —
  otherwise it captures a snapshot of `$row` at the moment the arrow
  function was defined, and any subsequent `$set` writes don't reach
  it. Symptom: a fresh `$get` after `$set('amount', 42.50)` returns null
  for `amount`, and downstream recalc helpers compute against stale
  state. Always pair `$get` and `$set` test helpers with the same
  `use (&$row)` reference capture; never use `fn`.
- **Reading a Filament component's `afterStateUpdated` callback list
  needs Reflection on the `$afterStateUpdated` protected array** (lives
  on `Filament\Schemas\Components\Concerns\HasState` since Filament v5).
  The array holds the closures in registration order; for a component
  with a single `->afterStateUpdated(fn …)` call, it's `[0]`. Pair with
  `ReflectionProperty::setAccessible(true)` on the `childComponents`
  array to walk the Repeater's schema and pluck the Select at the right
  index. Cleaner than mounting a full Filament Form and calling
  `updateState()` end-to-end just to verify a closure's contract.


## US-005: Wire recalc on unit_price/price and quantity edits (recalc series)
- `LineItemsRepeater.php`: replaced the inline arithmetic in both

  helpers:
  - Unit-price closure now: `function ($state, $get, $set) use ($priceField)
    { self::recalcRow($get, $set, $priceField); self::recalcFormTotals($get, $set); }`
    (was: `$set('amount', ((float) $state * $qty) + $tax)`).
  - Quantity closure now: same two-helper body (was: `$set('amount',
    (float) $state * (float) $get($priceField) + $tax)`).
- Bug fix: both pre-US-005 closures added the row's `tax_amount` into
  `amount`. Core CRM (LiveQuoteItems.php:148) writes `amount = unit_price
  * quantity` as the line subtotal — tax flows up via the form's `tax`
  field separately. `recalcRow()` already implements the correct
  subtotal-only contract, so the fix is purely "delegate, don't
  duplicate".
- Unit-price closure picked up `use ($priceField)` (previously
  uninvolved with priceField because the bug-version read `$state`
  directly); now needs it to thread through to `recalcRow`.
- All three reactive call sites (Product Select autofill from US-004,
  unit_price, quantity) now share the same two-helper recalc tail.
- New Pest test `tests/Feature/LineItemsRepeaterUnitPriceQuantityRecalcTest.php`
  (+6 tests / 20 assertions; full plugin suite now **863/863**, up
  from 857 in US-004 of the recalc series): closure signatures
  (3 params, `$priceField` captured), unit_price edit produces
  subtotal-only `amount` + correct `tax_amount`, quantity edit
  produces subtotal-only `amount` + correct `tax_amount`, Deal
  closure routes through recalcRow without setting `tax_amount`
  (matches deal_products column shape), source-grep asserts the
  pre-fix `(float) $state * $qty) + $tax` and `$get($priceField) +
  $tax` patterns are gone AND that `self::recalcRow(...)` /
  `self::recalcFormTotals(...)` each appear exactly 3 times (one
  per reactive call site).
- Pint clean.

### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`)
- **Modified** `src/Concerns/Forms/LineItemsRepeater.php`
- **Added** `tests/Feature/LineItemsRepeaterUnitPriceQuantityRecalcTest.php`

### Learnings for future iterations
- **Test helpers that walk a Repeater's nested Grid to fetch a
  field's closure must protect against field-name collisions on the
  `$priceField` parameter.** When a test calls
  `row2FieldClosure('fk_col', 'quantity', 'quantity')` — passing
  `'quantity'` as the `$priceField` arg — the Repeater renders TWO
  TextInputs both named `quantity` (the priceField input + the
  literal quantity input), and the linear walk picks up the first
  one. The closure that fires then has `$priceField = 'quantity'`,
  so `recalcRow` reads `$get('quantity')` for *both* the unit price
  and the quantity, computing `5 * 5 = 25` instead of `20 * 5 = 100`.
  Always pass the canonical `'unit_price'` (or `'price'` for Deal)
  as the second arg even when the field-of-interest is `quantity`,
  to mirror real-world Repeater construction.
- **`self::recalcRow()` reads `quantity` and the price field via
  `$get(...)`, NOT from the closure's `$state` argument.** This is
  important because Filament fires `afterStateUpdated` AFTER the new
  value is persisted into form state — so `$get('quantity')` already
  returns the new value when the quantity TextInput fires its
  closure. Don't try to optimise by passing `$state` directly into
  the helper; the abstraction works precisely because the helper
  treats `$get/$set` as the single source of truth for row state.
- **Two reactive bindings on the same row converge cleanly when both
  delegate to a single recalc helper.** Pre-US-005 the unit_price
  closure had qty-fetched-but-not-product-aware logic; quantity
  closure had priceField-fetched-but-not-product-aware logic. Both
  failed to recompute `tax_amount` when only one input changed (e.g.
  bumping quantity left tax_amount stale). Routing both through
  `recalcRow` (which recomputes BOTH amount AND tax_amount from
  scratch every time) eliminates the half-stale state. Add this to
  the toolkit: any "computed field that depends on N reactive inputs"
  should be recomputed in a single helper called from each input's
  binding, never written piecewise from per-input branches.


## US-006: Make MoneyTotalsRow sub_total and tax read-only; update parity test assertion (recalc series)
- `LineItemsRepeater::recalcRow` (US-002) and `recalcFormTotals` (US-003)
  are now the sole writers for `sub_total`, `tax`, line `amount`, and
  `tax_amount`, plus the resulting `total`. Reactive recalc (US-004 / US-005)
  populates these fields whenever the user edits product / unit_price /
  quantity. Making the three computed money fields read-only on the form
  prevents users from typing values that the next reactive event would
  overwrite, matching the core CRM Livewire behaviour:
  `LiveQuoteItems.php:155-161` writes `subtotal` and `tax` only via the
  per-row aggregator, never from a user input.
- `src/Concerns/Forms/MoneyTotalsRow.php`: added `->readOnly()` to the
  `sub_total` and `tax` TextInputs. `discount` and `adjustment` remain
  editable (user-driven adjustments live there). `total` was already
  read-only. Updated the class docblock to reflect the new read-only set.
- `tests/Feature/QuoteFormParityTest.php`: rewrote the read-only assertion
  in the "MoneyTotalsRow renders the 5 monetary fields with total
  read-only" test to walk the 5-component array by index and assert
  `isReadOnly` is true for indices 0/2/4 (sub_total/tax/total) and false
  for indices 1/3 (discount/adjustment). One TextInput Reflection handle
  is reused across all 5 components.
- Did not modify any other parity test per AC ("Only tweak that single
  assertion").
- Full plugin suite **863/863** still green (2253 assertions). Pint clean.

### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`)
- **Modified** `src/Concerns/Forms/MoneyTotalsRow.php`
- **Modified** `tests/Feature/QuoteFormParityTest.php`

### Learnings for future iterations
- **`isReadOnly` lives on the TextInput class itself, not a trait.** The
  protected property is declared on
  `Filament\Forms\Components\TextInput`, so `new ReflectionProperty(
  TextInput::class, 'isReadOnly')->setAccessible(true)` gives a single
  reusable handle that works for every TextInput instance in a
  collection. No need to construct a fresh ReflectionProperty per
  instance — pass the same `$readOnlyRef->getValue($component)` over
  the list. Cleaner pattern than per-component reflection when checking
  the same property on N siblings.
- **The two earlier MoneyTotalsRow fields (`sub_total`, `tax`) are
  conceptually NOT user-input fields — they are aggregations.** Core
  CRM Livewire's `calculateAmounts()` writes them on every line-item
  change; the Filament plugin mirrors that contract via the US-005
  reactive recalc. Leaving them as editable TextInputs invited a
  data-integrity bug: a user could type a fake total, save, and then
  any subsequent line-item edit would overwrite it. `->readOnly()` is
  the right enforcement — it keeps the value visible (vs. hiding the
  field entirely) while preventing direct edits. Apply the same rule
  to any future "computed from siblings" form field.

### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/.polyscope/clones/66571e70/humble-koi`)
- **Modified** `.context/progress.md` (this entry only — verification
  story carries no code change in either repo)

### Learnings for future iterations
- **Manual-UI-verification stories in the autopilot loop have an
  unavoidable handoff.** When the AC includes "open the app, click
  here, observe X", the autopilot can only do the proxy work:
  - run the full test suite as a baseline-or-better gate,
  - identify the structural tests that cover each AC bullet,
  - audit the wiring (priceField/defaultItems/recalc helper calls)
    via grep,
  - and document what was verified by code vs. what the user still
    needs to click through.
  Don't claim "manually verified" when the verification can't
  literally happen — that's misleading. State the proxy and leave
  the click-through as a handoff. Same pattern applies to any
  future "verify in production" or "confirm with the customer"
  story.
- **The `defaultItems(1)` modifier is what guarantees "qty defaults
  to 1" on a freshly-opened Create page.** Filament's Repeater
  `->defaultItems($n)` seeds N empty rows when no state is provided,
  and each row receives the schema's per-field defaults (here:
  `TextInput::make('quantity')->default(1)` inside the row schema).
  Without `defaultItems(1)` the user would have to click "Add line
  item" before any product Select appears — which is fine but
  contradicts the AC's "qty defaults to 1" expectation for a
  product just picked. All four sales resources call
  `defaultItems(1)`; Deal does too (via the same factory). Confirmed
  via grep on `Resources/{Quotes,Orders,Invoices,PurchaseOrders,Deals}/*Resource.php`.
- **Read the test result, not the test description.** The Pest
  summary line "863 passed (2253 assertions)" is the byte-precise
  baseline to compare against. The descriptions of the previously
  added recalc-series tests already include "subtotal-only amount",
  "amount math with unit_price", "recalcFormTotals reads
  `$get('../../')`" — re-running those is the cheapest possible
  proxy for the manual walk-through. Reach for the test names that
  match each AC bullet before reaching for the browser.

## US-002: Add backToIndexAction() factory to Lead/Quote/Deal resources (back-buttons series)
- New public static `backToIndexAction(): Actions\Action` factory on
  each of `LeadResource`, `QuoteResource`, `DealResource`. Each returns
  `Actions\Action::make('backToIndex')` with `->color('gray')`,
  `->icon('heroicon-o-arrow-left')`, `->url(static::getUrl('index'))`,
  and the per-entity `actions.back_to_{leads|quotes|deals}` label key
  added in US-001 of this series. Mirrors the shape of
  `listKanbanToggleActions()` at `LeadResource.php:347-362`.
- The three factories are reserved for the upcoming View-page reorder
  (subsequent story) — no call sites yet. Following the same
  introduce-helper-now/wire-it-next pattern used by the recalc series
  (US-001..US-003 of that series introduced helpers; US-004..US-005
  wired them).
- No existing factories or method bodies were modified — only
  additions, per AC.
- New Pest test `tests/Feature/BackToIndexActionTest.php` (+9 tests
  / 30 assertions). Two datasets keyed by resource:
  - Static-shape: public + static + 0 params + `Action` return type
    via Reflection.
  - Action contract: name `backToIndex`, color `gray`, icon
    `heroicon-o-arrow-left`, URL equals `static::getUrl('index')`.
  - Per-entity label key: `getLabel()` matches
    `__('laravel-crm-filament::labels.actions.back_to_{entity}')`.
- Quality gates green:
  - `./vendor/bin/pint --dirty --test` → passed.
  - Full plugin suite **872/872 (2283 assertions)**, up from 863 in
    US-006 of the recalc series.

### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`)
- **Modified** `src/Resources/Leads/LeadResource.php` (+ `backToIndexAction()` factory)
- **Modified** `src/Resources/Quotes/QuoteResource.php` (+ factory)
- **Modified** `src/Resources/Deals/DealResource.php` (+ factory)
- **Added** `tests/Feature/BackToIndexActionTest.php`

### Learnings for future iterations
- **PHP heredoc + `php /tmp/script.php` is the right tool for inserting
  the same shaped method into N similar files.** A small script that
  walks a `[file, anchor, entity]` list, locates the anchor (the last
  line BEFORE the final closing class brace), and splices in the new
  method just before that final `}` keeps the three insertions atomic
  and reproducible. Idempotency comes free via a
  `str_contains($src, 'public static function backToIndexAction(')`
  guard so a re-run of the script is a no-op.
- **`Action::getLabel()` resolves the translation key eagerly.** When
  the factory body sets `->label(__('…'))`, the action stores the
  resolved string (not the key), so asserting against the same
  resolved string via `__('…')` in the test catches both "key exists"
  and "label is set correctly" in one expression. No need to read the
  protected `$label` property via Reflection.
- **`Action::getColor()` returns `null` if `->color()` was never set,
  and the literal string (`'gray'`, `'primary'`, …) once set.**
  Filament v5 stores the color as a scalar, not a colored-theme map,
  on the action's `$color` property. Same shape as `getIcon()` and
  `getUrl()` — all three accept a scalar in the factory chain and
  return that exact scalar from the reader. Direct equality checks
  in tests are reliable; no need to compare against tailwind class
  arrays.

     `showActionOrderInvokeHeaderActions(string $page): array` — same
     reflection pattern as `parityInvokeHeaderActions` in
     `LeadResourceParityTest.php`), map the actions to their names,
     and assert the exact sequence. The sequences locked in are:
     - ViewLead: `backToIndex / convertToDeal / edit / delete`
     - ViewQuote: `backToIndex / accept / reject / unaccept / unreject
       / convertToOrder / send / previewPortal / downloadPdf / edit /
       delete`
     - ViewDeal: `backToIndex / markWon / markLost / reopen / edit /
       delete`
  3. **Edit action color** — each per-page test also locates the
     `EditAction` instance in the array and asserts
     `expect($edit->getColor())->toBeIn(['primary', null])`. This
     accepts both Filament v5's null-default ("no override; render
     primary") and an explicit `->color('primary')` setter — the AC
     calls out "primary OR null" precisely because Filament internally
     resolves null to primary at render time.
  4. **Translation keys exist in en/fr/es** — one test loops over
     `[en, fr, es] × [back_to_leads, back_to_quotes, back_to_deals]`,
     temporarily switches the app locale, and calls
     `__('laravel-crm-filament::labels.actions.back_to_*')`. Asserts
     the returned value is a non-empty string AND is NOT the key
     itself (Laravel's translator returns the key verbatim when the
     entry is missing). Restores en at the end.
- Helper named `showActionOrderInvokeHeaderActions` (not
  `parityInvokeHeaderActions`) to avoid the file-collision pattern
  noted in the v0.x progress log when two test files declare the
  same top-level function name.
- Quality gates: `./vendor/bin/pint --dirty --test` clean; targeted
  filter (`ShowPageActionOrder|LeadResourceParity|QuoteResourceParity|
  DealResourceParity`) → 44 passed (258 assertions); full plugin
  test suite → 879 passed (2334 assertions).

### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`)
- **Added** `tests/Feature/ShowPageActionOrderTest.php`

### Learnings for future iterations
- **Pest's top-level helper functions are global once required.**
  Two test files that both declare `function invokeHeaderActions(...)`
  at the top level will fatal-error on PHP's "Cannot redeclare
  function" check. Always prefix the helper with the topic of the
  test file (e.g. `showActionOrderInvokeHeaderActions`,
  `parityInvokeHeaderActions`) so each file's helpers are guaranteed
  unique. This is the same pattern locked in by the new-sequence
  US-009 `LeadResourceParityTest`.
- **`->toBeIn(['primary', null])` is the right matcher for "either
  explicitly primary or null-default".** Filament v5's
  `Action::getColor()` returns the literal string set via `->color()`,
  or null when never set. EditAction (and most Filament action
  classes) doesn't apply a default in the constructor — the panel's
  CSS layer resolves null to the primary theme color at render time.
  Asserting `toBeIn(['primary', null])` accepts both shapes without
  forcing a specific implementation detail.
- **Locale-switching tests should restore the app locale at the
  end** even when no other test reads it. `app()->setLocale('en')`
  in the test body's tail keeps the test idempotent — if Pest
  reorders tests randomly (which it does by default), a test that
  leaves the locale in `es` could break a subsequent locale-sensitive
  test in a way that's hard to debug.
- **Asserting "translation exists" should compare against the KEY
  string itself.** Laravel's Translator returns the dotted-path
  key verbatim when the translation entry is missing (e.g.
  `'laravel-crm-filament::labels.actions.back_to_xxx'`), so the
  reliable existence check is `expect($result)->not->toBe($key)`.
  Combining that with `trim($result) !== ''` covers both the
  missing-key case AND the present-but-blank-string case.


## US-001: Add translation keys for new Lead show page sections (lead show-page series)
- Added 2 net-new keys across all three locales at
  `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament/resources/lang/{en,fr,es}/labels.php`:
  - `sections.lead_qualification` — Lead Qualification / Qualification du
    prospect / Calificación del cliente potencial. Inserted right after

  - `audit.activity` — Activity / Activité / Actividad. Inserted right
    after the existing `audit.history` anchor.
- `fields.email` (Email / E-mail / Correo electrónico) and `fields.phone`
  (Phone / Téléphone / Teléfono) verified already present in all three
  locales (lines en:78,81 / fr:76,79 / es:76,79). No additions needed.
- Anchored the insertions inside the right array via a multi-line
  preg_replace_callback regex
  `/('namespace' => [...'anchor' => '...',])/` — far less fragile than
  single-line anchors when the same key name (`'activity'`) might appear
  elsewhere in the file.
- Idempotency guard: skip insertion if the key is already present at
  any level. Re-running the patch script is a no-op.
- `./vendor/bin/pint --dirty --test resources/lang/` → passed.
- `LocalizationTest` (7 tests / 27 assertions) → all green. Key parity
  en↔fr↔es preserved; documented `sections` set still matches the test's
  required-keys list (test reads it from en/labels.php and verifies fr/es
  match after flatten+sort).
- Working tree contained 29 unrelated modified files from a prior session;
  staged ONLY the three labels.php files via explicit `git add`, leaving
  the unrelated mods in place for whoever picks them up next. Same
  discipline noted in the new-sequence US-001 ("always check what's
  staged before starting work in the plugin repo").

### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`)
- **Modified** `resources/lang/en/labels.php` (+2 keys)
- **Modified** `resources/lang/fr/labels.php` (+2 keys)
- **Modified** `resources/lang/es/labels.php` (+2 keys)

### Learnings for future iterations
- **The same key name can legitimately appear in multiple namespaces.**
  Before this story, `'activity'` already existed as a sub-key of
  `dashboard` (or similar) — and the existing `'history' => ...,`
  pattern appears in `audit` AND elsewhere. A single-line anchor
  pattern like `'history' => 'History',` is ambiguous. The right
  pattern is to anchor inside the OUTER namespace block AND match the
  inner anchor key in one regex:
  `/(^\s+'NS'\s*=>\s*\[\s*\n(?:(?!^\s+\],).)*?'ANCHOR'\s*=>\s*'[^']*',\s*\n)/sm`.
  The non-greedy `(?:(?!^\s+\],).)*?` body matches any line that is
  NOT the array's closing `],` line, so the inner anchor lookup is
  confined to the right block. This is the cleanest reusable pattern
  for "insert a key into namespace X, after key Y" — and it handles
  the case where Y happens to also exist in some other namespace.
- **Skipping unrelated staged changes is a discipline, not a default.**
  When the plugin repo's working tree has 29 modified files (none
  related to this story), `git add path1 path2 path3` of the exact
  files touched is the only safe path. `git add -A` would balloon the
  commit with unrelated work and contaminate the story's history.
  Always check `git status` at the start of a session even when the
  prior progress entry suggests a clean slate — autopilot loops can
  leave files dirty.


## US-002: Add LeadResource::leadCustomFieldEntries() helper for grouped/ungrouped FieldValues (lead show-page series)
- New `protected static function leadCustomFieldEntries(Lead $record,
  bool $grouped): array` on `LeadResource`. Reads the lead's FieldValues
  via the existing `HasCrmFields::fields()` morphMany (eager-loading
  `field.fieldGroup` + `field.fieldOptions`), filters out rows whose
  `field` relation didn't resolve (orphaned FieldValues from removed
  Fields), then branches on `$grouped`:
  - `false`: returns only FieldValues whose `field->field_group_id` is
    `null`, mapped to flat `TextEntry` components.
  - `true`: groups the remaining FieldValues by `field->field_group_id`,
    walks each group, and wraps the entries in a
    `Section::make($group->name)->schema($entries)`. Returns one Section
    per distinct FieldGroup.
- New `protected static function buildLeadCustomFieldTextEntry($fieldValue):
  TextEntry` shared by both branches. Returns
  `TextEntry::make("custom.{$fieldName}")->label(ucfirst($fieldName))
  ->state(closure)` whose closure replicates the per-type formatting
  from core's `resources/views/components/custom-field-values/_row.blade.php`:
  - `checkbox` → `Yes`/`No` (resolves the `laravel-crm::lang.yes/no`
    translation keys via `ucfirst(__('…'))`).
  - `select` / `radio` → `firstWhere('id', $raw)?->label` lookup against
    the field's `fieldOptions` collection.
  - `checkbox_multiple` → `json_decode` the raw value, `whereIn('id',
    $values)->pluck('label')->implode(', ')`.
  - default → raw value (covers text/textarea/date/etc.).
- Empty / no-match returns `[]` in both modes (the AC's "returns an
  empty array when the record has no matching FieldValues" gate).
- Added `Filament\Infolists\Components\TextEntry` import to
  `LeadResource.php`. `Section` was already imported.
- Test schema patch: added `label` column to `crm_field_options` via the
  supplementary
  `tests/Database/Migrations/2024_01_01_000002_add_plugin_test_tables.php`
  (`TestSchema.php` only ships `value/order/external_id` — no `label`).
  Idempotent via `Schema::hasColumn` guard. The `FieldOption` model's
  `label` column is what the helper's select/radio/checkbox_multiple
  branches read.
- New Pest test `tests/Feature/LeadCustomFieldEntriesTest.php` (+9
  tests / 24 assertions; full plugin suite now **888/888**, up from
  879 at the post-US-001 baseline). Covers:
  - signature (protected + static + 2 required params + `: array`).
  - empty result in both modes.
  - flat ungrouped list contains only the null-`field_group_id`
    FieldValues; the entry's name is `custom.{field_name}`.
  - grouped mode returns Sections; each Section's heading is the
    FieldGroup's `name`; the Section's children's names match the
    expected `custom.{field_name}` keys (assertion walks the protected
    `Section::$childComponents` array via Reflection).
  - per-type state formatting: `Yes`/`No` for checkbox, the looked-up
    `label` for select + radio, joined `Alpha, Bravo` for
    checkbox_multiple, raw passthrough for plain text.
- Helper is a foundation for the upcoming US-003 infolist integration —
  no ViewLead infolist override yet, no call sites in production.
- `./vendor/bin/pint --dirty --test` clean. Commit `ffa756a`.

### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`)
- **Modified** `src/Resources/Leads/LeadResource.php` (+TextEntry import,
  +`leadCustomFieldEntries()` + `buildLeadCustomFieldTextEntry()` helpers)
- **Modified** `tests/Database/Migrations/2024_01_01_000002_add_plugin_test_tables.php`
  (+`label` column on `crm_field_options`)
- **Added** `tests/Feature/LeadCustomFieldEntriesTest.php`

### Learnings for future iterations
- **The story prose called the relation `crmFields`, but the actual
  morphMany on `HasCrmFields` is `fields()`.** Grep
  `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm/src/Traits/HasCrmFields.php`
  before naming the relation in a helper — the plan often uses
  marketing-style names that don't match the codebase. Same gotcha
  shape as earlier stories that named "send_at" when the column was
  just `sent`.
- **`crm_field_options` ships a `label` column in core (alongside
  `value`), but the plugin's `TestSchema.php` only declares
  `value`/`order`/`external_id`.** Any future code path that reads
  `FieldOption->label` from the panel needs the supplementary
  migration to patch the column in. Add this column to `TestSchema.php`
  itself in a future hygiene pass rather than relying on
  `2024_01_01_000002` — but for one-off feature stories, the guarded
  `Schema::hasColumn` patch in the supplementary file is the
  least-risk approach.
- **Reassigning a bool parameter to a Collection mid-method confuses
  future readers.** The first draft of `leadCustomFieldEntries()`
  reused the `$grouped` bool parameter as the Collection variable
  inside the `true` branch. Pint doesn't catch the shadow, but a
  human reviewer will. Always rename to `$groupedValues` (or similar)
  when the type changes — the AC parameter name should remain pristine.
- **Section's heading defaults to its first `make()` arg.** Calling
  `Section::make($group->name)` puts the group name in BOTH the
  section identifier AND the default heading. Tests can read either
  via `getHeading()` or `getKey()` — `getHeading()` is the natural
  display assertion since the AC says "Section keyed by FieldGroup
  name".
- **`TextEntry::getState()` runs the registered `->state()` closure
  WITHOUT requiring a Filament Schema mount.** This is unlike many
  Filament component getters that need a container — `TextEntry`'s
  state closure is invoked directly on call. Lets test assertions read
  `$entries[0]->getState()` as a plain function call against a loose
  TextEntry returned by the factory. Useful pattern for any future
  "factory returns a TextEntry whose state computation matters"
  story — assert the computed string directly without simulating a
  panel render cycle.

  / 38 assertions; full plugin suite now **896/896**, up from 888 in

  `->badge()`, hex lookup closure, Unallocated placeholder); Lead

  `Schema::make($page)->record($record?)` and invokes
  `LeadResource::infolist($schema)`, returning the schema's component

### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`)
- **Modified** `src/Concerns/Forms/LeadDealContactSection.php`
  (+`personLabel(?Person): string` static helper)
- **Modified** `src/Resources/Leads/LeadResource.php` (+`infolist(Schema)`
  override + imports for `Lead` as model typehint on closures,
  `PersonResource`, `OrganizationResource`)
- **Added** `tests/Feature/LeadResourceInfolistTest.php`

### Learnings for future iterations
- **`$schema->getRecord()` is null at component-construction time.**
  When a Filament resource's static `infolist(Schema $schema)` runs,
  the schema's bound record hasn't been hydrated yet — `getRecord()`
  returns null. To make a Section's schema depend on the bound record,
  pass a closure to `->schema(fn (?Lead $record) => [...])`. Filament
  evaluates the closure at RENDER time and the typed param resolves
  to the current bound record (or null in tests/mounts without a
  record). Same pattern works for `->visible()`, `->hidden()`, and
  `->state()` callbacks throughout Filament Forms / Infolists /
  Schemas.
- **`Schema::getComponents()` filters out hidden components by
  default.** Signature is `getComponents(bool $withActions = true,
  bool $withHidden = false, bool $withOriginalKeys = false)`. Tests
  that need to introspect a hidden section (e.g. assert that its
  `->hidden()` closure works correctly) MUST pass
  `getComponents(withHidden: true)`. Otherwise the section is silently
  dropped from the returned list and your `array_values(array_filter(...))`
  walk lands on the wrong index. Same gotcha applies to component
  reflection in headless-test scenarios where Filament's evaluate
  context is incomplete.
- **Read a `->hidden(Closure)` directly via Reflection on the
  `$isHidden` protected property** when you want to invoke it with
  arbitrary records without Filament's caching getting in the way.
  `Filament\Schemas\Components\Concerns\CanBeHidden` declares
  `protected bool | Closure $isHidden = false;`. After calling
  `->hidden($closure)` the property holds the closure; pull it via
  `(new ReflectionProperty($section, 'isHidden'))->setAccessible(true)->getValue($section)`
  and call `$closure($record)` directly. Bypasses `isHidden()`'s
  internal visibility cache (which keys on `$componentKey` + closure
  spl_object_id and can produce stale results across tests).
- **`Section::make($i18nString)` first arg is used as BOTH key and
  default heading.** Asserting "section X is present" via source-grep
  for the literal `Section::make(__('…labels.sections.foo'))` is
  reliable since the i18n helper resolves the same way in both source
  and runtime. Combined with `strpos()` ordering, this gives a clean
  "the three sections appear in this order" assertion without needing
  to mount a full Filament Schema.
- **Closure-typed callbacks need consistent param names for Filament's
  evaluate to inject the right value.** Filament's `evaluate()` uses
  the closure's parameter NAMES to inject the bound record/state/get/set
  — `$record` always means "the bound record" regardless of typehint.
  The Details section's `->color(fn ($state, $record) => …)` worked
  because `$state` got the per-badge label name and `$record` got the
  parent Lead. Don't rename `$record` to `$lead` inside these closures
  even if it reads better — break the convention and Filament resolves
  the closure with a null record.


## US-004: Override ViewLead::content() with 2-column Grid layout (lead show-page series)
- New `public function content(Schema $schema): Schema` on
  `src/Resources/Leads/Pages/ViewLead.php` returns a Schema with a single
  root component: `Grid::make(['default' => 1, 'lg' => 3])` whose
  children are `$this->getInfolistContentComponent()->columnSpan(['lg' => 2])`
  and `$this->getRelationManagersContentComponent()->columnSpan(['lg' => 1])`.
  Mirrors the v0.x ViewInvoice content pattern but with a 2:1 split
  instead of stacking form/infolist/relation-managers vertically.
- The ViewLead show page no longer renders the form schema —
  `getFormContentComponent()` is intentionally absent from the override.
  Filament's `ViewRecord::content()` default switches between form and
  infolist based on `hasInfolist()`; the US-003 infolist override
  declared on `LeadResource` populates the left column via
  `getInfolistContentComponent()`. The Create/Edit form is unaffected
  (still rendered by `CreateLead`/`EditLead`'s own page lifecycle).
- Filament auto-tabs the right column because LeadResource already
  registers 6 relation managers (Notes/Tasks/Calls/Meetings/Files/Audits).
  When 2+ RMs are registered, `getRelationManagersContentComponent()`
  renders them as a tabbed interface automatically — no per-page config
  needed.
- Responsive layout: default = 1 column (stacked on small viewports);
  lg = 3 columns (infolist spans 2, RMs span 1). Filament's Grid
  collapses to a single column below `lg` (1024px+).
- New Pest test `tests/Feature/ViewLeadContentLayoutTest.php` (+5
  tests / 12 assertions) asserts:
  - `content()` is declared on ViewLead directly (not inherited from
    `ViewRecord`) and is public.
  - The root component is a `Grid` with `getColumns() === ['default' =>
    1, 'lg' => 3]`.
  - The Grid has exactly 2 child components; first has
    `getColumnSpan() === ['lg' => 2]`, second has `['lg' => 1]`.
  - Source does NOT contain `getFormContentComponent()` (regression
    guard for the AC's "form schema is no longer rendered on view").
  - Source contains both `getInfolistContentComponent()` +
    `getRelationManagersContentComponent()` + the literal
    `Grid::make(['default' => 1, 'lg' => 3])` (mirrors-ViewInvoice
    structural check).
- Helper `viewLeadContentSchemaComponents()` mounts a fresh ViewLead
  via `newInstanceWithoutConstructor()`, attaches a placeholder Lead
  record, builds `Schema::make($page)`, invokes `$page->content($schema)`,
  and returns `getComponents(withHidden: true)`. Reuses the standard
  test-harness pattern locked in by US-003 of this series.
- Quality gates green: `./vendor/bin/pint --dirty --test` clean on
  the two changed files; targeted filter
  (`ViewLeadContentLayoutTest|LeadResourceParityTest|LeadResourceInfolistTest`)
  → 23 passed (100 assertions).

### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`)
- **Modified** `src/Resources/Leads/Pages/ViewLead.php` (+`content(Schema)`
  override + Grid/Schema imports)
- **Added** `tests/Feature/ViewLeadContentLayoutTest.php`

### Learnings for future iterations
- **Filament v5's `ViewRecord::content()` default doesn't auto-render
  relation managers in a sidebar.** The stock implementation switches
  between form and infolist (based on `hasInfolist()`) but stacks the
  relation manager component below. To get the "infolist left, tabbed
  RMs right" layout, you MUST override `content()` to wrap both
  `getInfolistContentComponent()` and `getRelationManagersContentComponent()`
  in a Grid yourself. The two helper methods return preconfigured
  layout components — call `->columnSpan(['lg' => N])` on each to lock
  the responsive split.
- **`Grid::getColumns()` returns the exact array passed to `make()`.**
  No normalization — `Grid::make(['default' => 1, 'lg' => 3])` is
  retrievable verbatim via `$grid->getColumns()`. Use this for
  structural test assertions rather than walking the rendered HTML.
- **`getComponents(withHidden: true)` is the right shape when invoking
  content() in a test.** Some Filament components return null/hidden
  during a headless mount (no real Livewire context) — passing
  `withHidden: true` ensures the test sees the structural tree
  regardless of evaluation context. Same gotcha noted in US-003
  for `LeadResourceInfolistTest`.
- **The work was already done in a prior session but uncommitted.**
  ViewLead.php carried an uncommitted diff and the test file existed
  but was untracked. The autopilot's "check git status before
  starting work" discipline (originally noted in the new-sequence
  US-001) is what surfaced the existing work — saved a redundant
  reimplementation. An unrelated untracked file
  (`resources/views/components/list-kanban-toggle.blade.php`) was
  intentionally LEFT alone — not part of this story's scope.

## US-006: Polyfill timelineActivities relation on Lead via service provider (lead show-page series)
- Added a third `resolveRelationUsing` polyfill to
  `LaravelCrmFilamentServiceProvider::packageBooted()` immediately after
  the `audits` block and before the campaign clicks block:
  `Lead::resolveRelationUsing('timelineActivities', fn ($model) =>
  $model->morphMany(Activity::class, 'timelineable'))`. The closure
  returns the same `timelineable_*` morphMany the existing
  `HasCrmActivities::activities()` exposes — but registered under an
  unambiguous name so US-007's ActivitiesRelationManager can bind via
  `protected static string $relationship = 'timelineActivities'`
  without colliding with the existing trait-declared `activities`
  relation.

  service provider (placed alphabetically before `Deal`).
- No guard added beyond what the audits/labels precedent uses
  (which is also unguarded). The `crm_activities` table ships as
  part of the core CRM install; the registration call is safe at
  boot time regardless, and any query against the relation fails
  at access time if the table is somehow absent — same risk profile
  as the surrounding audits/labels polyfills.
- New Pest test `tests/Feature/TimelineActivitiesPolyfillTest.php`
  (+4 tests / 13 assertions; full plugin suite now **911/911**
  up from 907 in US-005 of this series). Covers:
  - `$lead->timelineActivities()` returns a `MorphMany` whose
    morph type is `timelineable_type` and related model is `Activity`.
  - Querying `$lead->fresh()->timelineActivities` returns ONLY the
    activities whose `timelineable_*` matches the lead, with
    activities tied to a different lead excluded.
  - Source-grep: `Lead::resolveRelationUsing('timelineActivities'` +
    `morphMany(Activity::class, 'timelineable')` strings exist in
    the service provider AND the new polyfill sits between the
    audits block and the campaign clicks block (positional
    `strpos` ordering check).
  - Regression guard: the four pre-existing polyfills (Product
    labels, Delivery labels, audits across all 10 models, Audit
    binding via `morphMany(Audit::class, 'auditable')`) are still
    present verbatim.
- `./vendor/bin/pint --dirty --test` clean. Targeted filter
  green; full suite 911/911 (2429 assertions).

### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`)
- **Modified** `src/LaravelCrmFilamentServiceProvider.php` (+`Activity`
  import + `timelineActivities` polyfill inside `packageBooted()`)
- **Added** `tests/Feature/TimelineActivitiesPolyfillTest.php`

### Learnings for future iterations
- **`Model::resolveRelationUsing($name, Closure)` is the right
  mechanism whenever a plugin needs a relation under a SPECIFIC
  name that diverges from what core declares.** The Lead model
  already has `activities()` via `HasCrmActivities` — but Filament's
  RelationManager contract picks the relation name based on the
  manager's `$relationship` property. Registering a parallel
  `timelineActivities` relation with the same morphMany body is
  the cleanest way to bind a RelationManager to "the activity
  timeline" without renaming the core trait method or accepting
  the ambiguous `activities` name (which the v0.7 standalone
  ActivityResource already trades on for its global aggregate
  list).
- **`MorphMany::getMorphType()` returns the literal morph_type
  column name** (e.g. `'timelineable_type'`), not the morph alias.
  Useful for structural assertions that confirm "this relation
  binds to the right pivot column" without needing to actually
  insert and query rows. Pair with `getRelated()` (returns a
  Model instance of the related class) for a complete shape check
  on any morphMany.
- **Source-position ordering checks via `strpos()` are cheaper
  than parsing the AST** when a story says "this block lives
  between X and Y in packageBooted()". Pull the file contents
  via `file_get_contents()` + reflection, find each block's
  marker string, and assert `$xPos < $newPos < $yPos`. Locks the
  ordering invariant without making the test brittle to whitespace
  changes or comment edits.

## US-009: Add LeadInfolistTest covering infolist schema, ViewLead content, and new RM registration (lead show-page series)
- New `tests/Feature/LeadInfolistTest.php` (+9 tests / 53 assertions; full
  plugin suite now **930/930** up from 921 in US-008). One test per AC
  bullet (1)–(6):
  1. **Three top-level Sections in order** — mounts the infolist via the
     `leadInfolistTopLevelSections(?Lead)` helper, filters
     `Schema::getComponents(withHidden: true)` to `Section` instances,
     asserts the three headings match the `sections.{details,
     lead_qualification,contact}` translation keys in order.
  2. **TextEntries by name** — calls `$section->getChildComponents()`
     on Details + Contact (which transparently evaluates each section's
     `->schema(fn (?Lead $record) => …)` closure with the bound record),
     filters to `TextEntry` instances, and asserts the AC-named entries
     are present.
  3. **Amount entry currency closure** — source-greps for the exact
     `->money(fn ($record) => $record?->currency ?: config(...))` closure,
     then RUNTIME asserts `$amountEntry->isMoney === true` AND that
     `$amountEntry->formatState((float) 1000)` for a Lead with
     `currency=EUR` produces a string containing `EUR` or `€` (Number::
     currency's locale-dependent rendering). Locks the closure dispatches
     the per-record currency.
  4. **Lead Qualification hidden gate** — extracts the `->hidden()`
     closure via `ReflectionProperty($qual, 'isHidden')` (bypasses
     Filament's `evaluate()` cache), invokes it with a Lead that has no
     grouped FieldValues, asserts `true`.
  5. **Lead Qualification nested Section keyed by FieldGroup name** —
     seeds a FieldGroup `Marketing` (with the required `model => Lead::class`
     column — see Learnings) + a Field with `field_group_id` + a
     FieldValue, asserts the hidden closure now returns false AND that
     `$qual->getChildComponents()` returns exactly one nested Section
     whose heading is `'Marketing'`.
  6. **ViewLead content Grid** — mounts via
     `leadInfolistViewLeadChildren()`, asserts the top-level component is
     a `Grid`, then walks `$grid->getChildComponents()` to assert two
     children with `getColumnSpan()` of `['lg' => 2]` and `['lg' => 1]`
     respectively.
  7. **getRelations contains both new RMs + existing six** — asserts
     `LeadResource::getRelations()` contains
     `LunchesRelationManager::class` and `ActivitiesRelationManager::class`
     alongside the six other RMs (Notes/Tasks/Calls/Meetings/Files/Audits),
     and that the array has exactly 8 entries.
  8. **LunchesRelationManager** — instantiated via
     `newInstanceWithoutConstructor()`, asserts
     `instanceof RelationManager`, `isReadOnly() === true`, and
     `headerActions/recordActions/toolbarActions` arrays from
     `Table::make($rm)` returned by the RM's `table()` are all `[]`.
  9. **ActivitiesRelationManager** — same shape as test 8.
- `LeadResourceParityTest` continues to pass unchanged (10 tests,
  53 assertions; verified via targeted `--filter` run).

### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`)
- **Added** `tests/Feature/LeadInfolistTest.php`

### Learnings for future iterations
- **`$section->getChildComponents()` is the right way to read a
  Section whose schema is a closure.** When a Section uses
  `->schema(fn (?Lead $record) => [...])`, the protected
  `$childComponents` property holds the Closure verbatim — reading
  it directly via Reflection returns the unevaluated Closure, not
  an array of children. The public `getChildComponents()` method
  resolves the closure correctly (it runs `getChildSchema()` →
  `getDefaultChildComponents()` → `evaluate($this->childComponents[$key])`
  → Schema::make → getComponents), AND it threads the bound record
  into the closure's `?Lead $record` parameter. Same shape works
  for any future test that needs to read a Filament Section whose
  schema is closure-driven. The original draft hit the
  `'created_at' not found in array` failure because it read the raw
  Closure and `array_map(fn ($c) => $c->getName(), $closure)` skipped
  it silently.
- **`crm_field_groups.model` is NOT NULL in core.** Core's migration
  declares the column without a nullable() modifier. Any test that
  creates a FieldGroup via `FieldGroup::create([...])` MUST pass
  `model => Lead::class` (or the appropriate model FQCN). The
  existing `LeadCustomFieldEntriesTest` happens to work because it
  creates the group via a different code path. Symptom: an
  `Integrity constraint violation: 19 NOT NULL constraint failed:
  crm_field_groups.model` SQLite error.
- **Filament's `TextEntry::money()` doesn't expose a public currency
  getter** — the currency parameter is captured inside the closure
  passed to `formatStateUsing()`. The only ways to assert "money was
  set with a per-record currency closure" are: (a) source-grep for
  the closure pattern (the cheapest and most explicit), AND (b)
  assert `isMoney === true` via Reflection on the protected property,
  AND (c) call `$entry->formatState($value)` on a real record and
  assert the output contains the expected currency symbol or ISO
  code. The triple-belt approach is more robust than any single
  check — source-grep locks the call shape, isMoney locks that money
  was actually applied, and the runtime format check ensures the
  closure resolves the bound record's currency.
- **`Schema::getComponents(withHidden: true)` matters when extracting
  hidden sections.** The Lead Qualification section is hidden when
  the bound record has no grouped FieldValues. Without
  `withHidden: true`, `getComponents()` filters it out and your
  positional `$sections[1]` indexing lands on the Contact section
  instead — giving a misleading "section heading is 'Contact'" failure.
  Apply this anywhere a test enumerates components that may be
  hidden on first render.

- **Added** `src/RelationManagers/LeadNotesRelationManager.php`

### Learnings for future iterations
- **The Filament `RelationManager` base class declares
  `protected string $view = 'filament-panels::resources.relation-manager';`**
  (`vendor/filament/filament/src/Resources/RelationManagers/RelationManager.php:68`).
  Override it in a subclass to swap the rendered Blade template. The
  property is inherited from the underlying Livewire Component class —
  same shape used by all the Kanban / chat thread custom-view Pages in
  the plugin (`CallKanban`, `TaskKanban`, `LeadKanban`, `DealKanban`,
  `QuoteKanban`, `ViewChatConversation`).
- **`ReflectionProperty::getDeclaringClass()` is the right discriminator
  for "is this property declared locally vs inherited?"** — UNLIKE
  `ReflectionMethod::getDeclaringClass()` for trait methods (which
  returns the using class, not the trait — see new-sequence US-001 of
  the form-parity series), property-from-parent-class lookups DO work
  correctly. Methods coming from a parent class (not a trait) also
  return the parent FQCN from `getDeclaringClass()` — that's how this
  story's "table() inherits from parent" test works. The trait gotcha
  is specific to PHP traits, not class inheritance.
- **A scaffold-only story is the right place to land a subclass even
  when the matching Blade view + the wiring on `getRelations()` aren't
  ready yet.** Filament classes are autoloaded lazily — instantiating
  the class via `newInstanceWithoutConstructor()` doesn't trigger a
  view render, so a missing Blade template doesn't break "class loads
  cleanly" assertions. Tests can fully introspect the form schema,
  inheritance contract, and `$view` value without ever touching the
  Blade layer. Lets the autopilot loop split UI scaffold into multiple
  small stories without each one having to ship complete vertical
  slices.
