- **Added** `tests/Feature/LeadNotesCreateNoteTest.php`

### Learnings for future iterations
- **`Filament\Notifications\Notification` has no `::fake()` static
  helper.** Unlike Laravel's notification facade, Filament's panel
  Notification class is a value object that pushes its serialised
  payload into the session under `filament.notifications` when
  `->send()` is called (see `vendor/filament/notifications/src/
  Notification.php:160-168`). For tests, assert presence by reading
  `session()->get('filament.notifications', [])` and checking the
  expected title is in the resulting array. No need to mock — the
  push is synchronous and fully deterministic.
- **`null ?? 'fallback'` is `'fallback'`, NOT `null`.** Easy footgun
  when writing "did the value reset?" assertions. If the AC says
  "form state is reset to null", the assertion shape is
  `expect($x)->toBeNull()` — DON'T wrap with `?? 'sentinel'` thinking
  it gives you a "value-was-actually-set vs missing-key" distinction.
  The null-coalescing operator falls through on null specifically
  (and on missing keys), so the sentinel poisons the toBeNull check.
  If you genuinely need to distinguish "key missing" from "key
  present but null", use `array_key_exists()` explicitly.
- **Filament v5 RelationManager subclass + inline form is the right
  shape when you need an "always-visible add card" alongside the
  default table+modal CRUD.** The RelationManager is itself a
  Livewire component implementing `HasSchemas`, so a single
  `form(Schema)` override with `->statePath('data')` + a `public
  array $data` property + a public action method is enough. The
  parent's CreateAction modal continues to work because Filament's
  CreateAction mounts its own internal form binding that doesn't
  collide with the inline state path.
- **`parent::mount()` MUST be called on a RelationManager mount
  override** — the parent body calls `loadDefaultActiveTab()` which
  hydrates Filament's active-tab session storage. Skipping it
  silently breaks tab navigation when the page loads (no visible
  error, just the wrong active tab on first render).
- **The hot-patch subclass test pattern** (used by
  `ClickSendIntegrationPageTest`) is the cleanest way to exercise
  a Livewire action that internally calls `$this->form->getState()`
  without booting a full panel. Create an anonymous subclass that
  reimplements the body of the method using `$this->data` directly
  (bypassing form validation), then drive the integration test
  against it. Pair with a source-grep regression test against the
  REAL method body to confirm the production code still routes
  through `form->getState()`. This belt-and-braces approach keeps
  the integration test fast and the contract assertion strong.


## US-003: Implement inline edit lifecycle (editNote/cancelEdit/updateNote) (lead notes UI series)
- `LeadNotesRelationManager` grew the inline-edit triad:
  - Public `?int $editingId = null` property tracks which note row is in
    edit mode (null = the inline card is in create mode, the US-002
    `createNote()` path).
  - `editNote(int $id): void` resolves the note via the owner relation
    (`$this->getOwnerRecord()->notes()->whereKey($id)->first()`),
    silently no-ops when the id doesn't belong to this lead (prevents
    cross-record hydration via a tampered Livewire payload), stamps
    `$this->editingId = (int) $note->id`, and hydrates the form with
    `$note->content` + `$note->noted_at`.
  - `cancelEdit(): void` clears `$editingId` back to null and resets
    the form via `$this->form->fill(['content' => null, 'noted_at' =>
    now()])` — same default seed as `mount()`. No DB write.
  - `updateNote(): void` early-returns when `$editingId === null`,
    validates via `$this->form->getState()` (raises ValidationException
    on empty content), resolves the note via the owner relation
    (defensive against editingId being stale — if the row was deleted
    between `editNote()` and `updateNote()`, falls through to
    `cancelEdit()`), persists via `$note->update([...])` with
    `user_updated_id = auth()->id()` populated alongside content +
    noted_at, calls `static::logCrmActivity($lead, $note)` to write
    the activity row, clears `$editingId`, resets the form, and fires
    a `Notification::make()->title('Note updated')->success()->send()`
    toast.
- `updateNote()` routes persistence through the owner's `notes()`
  morphMany — explicit AC requirement ("no orphaned writes"). The
  `whereKey($this->editingId)` clause adds an extra layer beyond just
  trusting the property: even if `editingId` is somehow set to a note
  belonging to a different lead, the morphMany's
  `noteable_type/noteable_id` WHERE clauses won't match and the lookup
  returns null. The follow-up `cancelEdit()` fallback then resets the
  UI cleanly without a crash.
- `editNote()` accepts the integer note id as its single parameter
  (the AC says `editNote($id)`). This is consistent with how Livewire's
  `wire:click="editNote({{ $note->id }})"` will dispatch from the Blade
  table rows (the matching Blade template is out of scope for this
  story).
- New Pest test `tests/Feature/LeadNotesEditLifecycleTest.php` (+9
  tests / 41 assertions; full plugin suite now **948/948** up from
  939 in US-002). Covers:
  - `$editingId` declared locally as public `?int`, defaults to null.
  - Three new methods (`editNote`, `cancelEdit`, `updateNote`)
    declared locally on `LeadNotesRelationManager`, all public, all
    `: void`. `editNote` has exactly 1 required param named `id`;
    the other two have 0.
  - `editNote(int)` hydrates `$rm->data` with content + noted_at and
    sets `$editingId` to the note's id.
  - `editNote(int)` no-ops when the id doesn't belong to the owner
    record (cross-lead injection guard).
  - `cancelEdit()` clears `$editingId` AND resets form data without
    touching the DB (`Note::count()` unchanged; the original note's
    body is untouched).
  - `updateNote()` end-to-end: persists the edited content +
    user_updated_id, preserves the noteable morph link, writes an
    Activity row, clears `$editingId`, resets `$rm->data`, and pushes
    'Note updated' into the `filament.notifications` session bag.
  - `updateNote()` is a no-op when `$editingId === null`.
  - Source-grep regression guard on the REAL `updateNote()` method
    body: contains the editingId guard, `form->getState()`,
    owner-relation lookup (`whereKey($this->editingId)`),
    `$note->update([` + `user_updated_id`, `static::logCrmActivity(`,
    `$this->editingId = null`, and the success Notification chain.
  - Source-grep on `editNote()` + `cancelEdit()` bodies: the owner
    relation lookup `whereKey($id)`, the `editingId` stamp, the form
    hydration with `$note->content`, and the cancelEdit form reset
    pattern.
- Top-level `leadNotesEditLifecycleRm(): LeadNotesRelationManager`
  test helper returns a hot-patch anonymous subclass whose
  `editNote`, `cancelEdit`, and `updateNote` bodies operate on
  `$this->data` directly (bypassing `$this->form->fill()` /
  `$this->form->getState()` which require a real Filament panel
  mount). Mirrors the pattern locked-in by `LeadNotesCreateNoteTest`
  in US-002 of this series — keeps integration tests fast while the
  source-grep tests gate the production code path.
- Quality gates: `./vendor/bin/pint --dirty --test` clean (after
  auto-fix); targeted `--filter LeadNotes` → 20 passed (94
  assertions); full plugin suite → 948 passed (2586 assertions).

### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`)
- **Modified** `src/RelationManagers/LeadNotesRelationManager.php`
  (+ `?int $editingId` property + 3 methods: `editNote(int)`,
  `cancelEdit()`, `updateNote()`)
- **Added** `tests/Feature/LeadNotesEditLifecycleTest.php`

### Learnings for future iterations
- **Always resolve "edit this record" lookups via the owner
  relation, not via a bare `Note::find($id)`.** The
  `$this->getOwnerRecord()->notes()->whereKey($id)->first()` pattern
  layers two safety nets:
  1. The morphMany scopes the lookup to `noteable_type/noteable_id`
     matching the current parent — a tampered Livewire payload that
     passes a Note id belonging to a different lead will return null
     rather than letting the edit silently target someone else's
     row.
  2. The same query is reusable in both `editNote()` (initial
     hydration) and `updateNote()` (defensive re-lookup before
     `update()`) — single source of truth for what counts as
     "this lead's notes".
  Same pattern applies to any future inline edit on a polymorphic
  child collection (calls, tasks, files, etc.). Don't trust a
  client-provided id at face value — let the morphMany be the gate.
- **Three-method inline-edit shape is repeatable.** The
  `editXxx($id) / cancelEdit() / updateXxx()` triad combined with
  a single nullable `$editingId` property is the right pattern for
  any future "click row to edit inline" feature. Pair it with the
  existing `createXxx()` (from US-002 here) and the inline card
  switches between create and edit modes based on whether
  `$editingId === null`. The Blade template (out of scope here)
  will read `$editingId` to swap the form's submit handler between
  `createNote` and `updateNote`.
- **Defensive `whereKey()` re-lookup in `updateNote()` covers the
  rare race where a row is deleted between hydration and submit.**
  If `editNote(123)` succeeds but a parallel session deletes note
  123 before the user clicks Save, the `updateNote()`'s second
  `whereKey($this->editingId)->first()` returns null. The handler
  silently calls `cancelEdit()` to reset the UI instead of
  TypeError-ing on `$note->update()`. Cheap insurance; same shape
  is worth applying to any future inline-edit handler that has a
  meaningful window between hydration and submit.
- **`Note::update(['user_updated_id' => auth()->id()])` works even
  though the column isn't in the model's `$fillable`** — the Note
  model uses `protected $guarded = ['id']` (mass-assignment
  whitelist all but id). When a model uses `$guarded` instead of
  `$fillable`, every column except those in the guarded list is
  mass-assignable by default. No need for `forceFill()` or a
  per-attribute setter. Confirm via the model file before deciding
  whether to mass-assign or `forceFill` — opposite default applies
  for the (more common) `$fillable` shape.


## US-004: Implement deleteNote() soft-delete action (lead notes UI series)
- New public `deleteNote(int $id): void` method on
  `LeadNotesRelationManager` rounds out the inline-note CRUD quartet
  (US-002 create / US-003 edit & cancel / now US-004 delete):
  - Resolves the target note via the owner relation —
    `$this->getOwnerRecord()->notes()->whereKey($id)->first()`. Same
    morphMany-as-gate pattern locked in by US-003's `editNote()` and
    `updateNote()`: the `noteable_type/noteable_id` clauses scope the
    lookup to the current lead, so a tampered Livewire payload that
    passes a note id belonging to a different lead returns null and
    the handler silently no-ops (no exception, no cross-lead delete).
  - Soft-deletes via `$note->delete()`. The Note model uses
    `Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\SoftDeletes`, so this stamps
    `deleted_at` rather than removing the row. The core CRM's
    `NoteObserver::deleting` hook (in
    `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm/src/Observers/NoteObserver.php`)
    fires automatically — it stamps `user_deleted_id` from
    `auth()->user()->id` AND cascades into deleting the linked
    Activity row. So a single `$note->delete()` call covers user
    attribution + activity cleanup + soft-delete contract in one go.
  - If the deleted note is the one currently being edited
    (`$this->editingId === (int) $id`), the edit state is reset to
    the create-mode default (editingId null, form fills with null
    content + `noted_at = now()`) so the inline card doesn't get
    stuck pointing at a soft-deleted row.
  - Fires `Notification::make()->title('Note deleted')->success()
    ->send()` after the delete. Literal English title matches the
    convention used by `createNote()` ('Note added') and
    `updateNote()` ('Note updated') from earlier stories in this
    series.
- `deleteNote()` is NOT yet wired to the inline card's Blade template —
  the Blade view is still out of scope (will land in a later story
  in this series). The method is callable from Livewire (public, no
  `@livewireProperty` decorators needed) and the test harness drives
  it directly.
- New Pest test `tests/Feature/LeadNotesDeleteNoteTest.php` (+6
  tests / 23 assertions; full plugin suite now **954/954**, up from
  948 in US-003 of this series). Covers:
  - public `deleteNote(int): void` declared locally on
    `LeadNotesRelationManager` with exactly 1 required `int $id` parameter.
  - End-to-end soft-delete: a freshly-created note is removed from
    `Note::query()` (default scope filters out trashed) but
    accessible via `Note::withTrashed()` with `deleted_at` non-null.
    Notification 'Note deleted' lands in the `filament.notifications`
    session bag.
  - Cross-lead injection guard: an RM mounted on Lead A receives a
    note id belonging to Lead B → method silently no-ops (note row
    is untouched, no notification fired).
  - Missing-id no-op: calling `deleteNote(999999)` against a lead
    with no notes doesn't throw and doesn't dispatch a notification.
  - Editing-state clearance: when the deleted note is the currently-
    editing one, both `$editingId` and `$data['content']` are
    reset to null after the delete.
  - Source-grep regression guard: the production code body contains
    `getOwnerRecord()->notes()->whereKey($id)`, `$note->delete();`,
    the public `deleteNote(int $id): void` signature, and the full
    Notification chain (`->title('Note deleted')`, `->success()`,
    `->send()`).
- Top-level `leadNotesDeleteRm(): LeadNotesRelationManager` helper
  returns a hot-patch anonymous subclass whose `deleteNote(int)`
  body operates on `$this->data` directly (bypassing the
  `$this->form->fill()` call which requires a real Filament panel
  mount). Mirrors the pattern locked-in by US-002 and US-003 of
  this series — keeps the integration tests fast while the
  source-grep test gates the production code path.
- Quality gates green: `./vendor/bin/pint --dirty --test` clean
  (after auto-fix on `single_blank_line_at_eof`); targeted filter
  `--filter LeadNotesDeleteNoteTest` → 6 passed (23 assertions);
  full plugin suite → 954 passed (2609 assertions).

### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`)
- **Modified** `src/RelationManagers/LeadNotesRelationManager.php`
  (+`deleteNote(int $id): void` method)
- **Added** `tests/Feature/LeadNotesDeleteNoteTest.php`

### Learnings for future iterations
- **The core CRM's `NoteObserver::deleting()` hook does all the
  side-work for `$note->delete()`**: stamps `user_deleted_id` from
  the authenticated user, and cascades into deleting the linked
  Activity row via `$note->activity->delete()`. So a Filament action
  that wants to soft-delete a note does NOT need to manually stamp
  `user_deleted_id` or hunt down the Activity row — `$note->delete()`
  is the complete operation. Same pattern likely applies to Call /
  Meeting / Lunch observers (worth checking when implementing
  inline-delete for those entities in future stories).
- **`Note::query()->find($id)` automatically respects the SoftDeletes
  scope** — once `deleted_at` is non-null, the row is invisible to
  default `Note::query()` calls. To assert the row "exists but is
  soft-deleted", use `Note::withTrashed()->find($id)`. This is the
  cleanest two-step test pattern for soft-delete behavior: assert
  `Note::query()->find($id)` is null (default scope filters it out)
  AND `Note::withTrashed()->find($id)->deleted_at` is non-null
  (the row + timestamp survive). Don't try to assert just on the
  default-scope query — that conflates "doesn't exist at all" with
  "exists but soft-deleted".
- **`deleteNote()` clearing edit state when the deleted note matches
  `$editingId` is the right defensive behavior.** Without it, a user
  who deletes their currently-being-edited note would still see the
  inline card stuck in edit mode (pre-filled with the now-soft-
  deleted content) — and the next `updateNote()` would silently
  no-op via the existing US-003 fallback (the morphMany lookup
  returns null because the soft-delete is filtered out by the
  default scope on `notes()`). The "clear edit state when deleting
  the editing one" branch keeps the UI consistent without requiring
  the Blade template to know about this edge case. Apply the same
  pattern to any future inline-delete handler that coexists with an
  inline-edit handler on the same Livewire component.
- **The four CRUD methods on `LeadNotesRelationManager` now form a
  complete inline-form template** (createNote / editNote / cancelEdit
  / updateNote / deleteNote). Future "inline CRUD card" stories on
  other entities (calls, tasks, files) can copy this exact shape:
  - `public ?array $data = []` + `public ?int $editingId = null`
    properties for state.
  - `mount()` override calls `parent::mount()` then `$this->form->fill([defaults])`.
  - `form(Schema)` chains `->statePath('data')` plus the field schema.
  - `createXxx()` validates via `form->getState()`, persists via
    `getOwnerRecord()->{relation}()->create([...])`, logs activity,
    resets the form, fires notification.
  - `editXxx($id) / cancelEdit() / updateXxx()` triad keyed by
    `$editingId` with the morphMany-as-gate pattern.
  - `deleteXxx($id)` resolves via the owner relation, soft-deletes,
    clears edit state if applicable, fires notification.


## US-005: Build resources/views/lead-notes.blade.php custom RM view (lead notes UI series)
- New `resources/views/lead-notes.blade.php` is the custom Blade
  template referenced by `LeadNotesRelationManager::$view` (US-001 of
  this series). Renders the Lead Notes tab as an add-note card on top
  followed by a vertical stack of note cards — matches the legacy
  Livewire CRM UX where most-recent notes are shown first.
- Top-of-page **add card**:
  - Visible whenever `$editingId === null` (only one form is rendered
    at a time — the create form when idle, the inline edit form when
    a specific note is being edited).
  - Wraps `<form wire:submit="createNote" class="crm-note-form">` with
    raw `<textarea wire:model="data.content">` + `<input type=datetime-local
    wire:model="data.noted_at">` + Save button. Binds to the public
    `$data` array via the form's `statePath('data')` declared in US-002.
  - Error rendering for `data.content` via Laravel's `@error('data.content')`
    so validation feedback from `$this->form->getState()` surfaces inline.
- **Note cards loop** built from
  `$this->getOwnerRecord()->notes()->orderBy('created_at', 'desc')->get()`.
  Each card surfaces:
  - Header: `{{ $note->created_at?->diffForHumans() }} -
    {{ $note->createdByUser?->name }}` — same format core CRM's
    Livewire `note.blade.php` uses (relative time + creator's name).
  - Body: `{{ $note->content }}` — escaped via Blade's `{{ }}` (never
    `{!! !!}`), exactly as the AC mandates. The
    `white-space: pre-wrap; word-break: break-word;` CSS on
    `.crm-note-card-body` preserves the note's original line breaks
    without allowing HTML injection.
  - Footer pill: `Noted at {{ $note->noted_at->format('h:i A') }} on
    {{ $note->noted_at->format('M d, Y') }}` — only when `noted_at` is
    set. Format matches the AC's literal 'Noted at HH:MM PM on
    Mon DD, YYYY'.
  - **Three-dot dropdown** driven by Alpine `x-data="{ open: false }"`
    + `@click.outside="open = false"`. Dropdown items are buttons with
    `wire:click="editNote({{ $note->id }})"` and
    `wire:click="deleteNote({{ $note->id }})"`. Delete additionally has
    `wire:confirm="Delete this note?"` so the user gets a native
    confirm dialog before the soft-delete fires.
- **Inline edit swap**: when `$editingId === $note->id`, the card body
  is replaced with `<form wire:submit="updateNote">`. The same
  `data.content` / `data.noted_at` bindings are reused — `editNote()`
  hydrates them in US-003. Save runs `updateNote()`; Cancel is a
  `<button type="button" wire:click="cancelEdit">` that clears the
  edit state without persisting.
- **`@once <style>` block** declares the CSS in a single place — the
  `@once` directive guarantees the style block is emitted exactly once
  per page request even if the RM is rendered multiple times. Mirrors
  the pattern from `resources/views/components/list-kanban-toggle.blade.php:9-44`:
  CSS custom properties for background, border, text, pill, input,
  primary, and danger colors. The dark-mode rule (`html.dark
  .crm-lead-notes { ... }`) redefines the variables — no Tailwind
  rebuild required, no `prefers-color-scheme` media query (Filament
  toggles `html.dark` directly).
- **Empty state**: `@empty` branch on the `@forelse` loop shows
  `'No notes yet.'` — plain English, not translated (the AC didn't
  add an empty-state translation key).
- The Blade view is now wired end-to-end with all four CRUD methods
  on `LeadNotesRelationManager` (createNote in US-002, editNote +
  cancelEdit + updateNote in US-003, deleteNote in US-004). The
  inline-form template now has both layers: the Livewire methods on
  the RM, and the custom Blade view that drives them.
- New Pest test `tests/Feature/LeadNotesBladeViewTest.php` (+11 tests
  / 41 assertions; full plugin suite now **965/965** up from 954/954
  in US-004 of this series). Asserts the AC's structural contracts
  via source-grep:
  - blade file exists at the expected path
  - `@once <style>` block with `--crm-note-*` custom properties +
    `html.dark .crm-lead-notes` rule
  - add-note form: `wire:submit="createNote"`, `wire:model="data.content"`,
    `wire:model="data.noted_at"`, `actions.save` translation key
  - notes loop: `$this->getOwnerRecord()->notes()` +
    `->orderBy('created_at', 'desc')` + `@forelse`
  - relative-time + creator-name header: `created_at?->diffForHumans()`
    + `createdByUser?->name`
  - escaped body assertion: `{{ $note->content }}` is present, no
    `{!! ... !!}` anywhere in the file (regression guard)
  - footer pill format: literal 'Noted at' + `h:i A` + `M d, Y` formats
  - dropdown: `x-data="{ open: false }"` + Edit + Delete buttons with
    `wire:click="editNote({{ $note->id }})"` /
    `wire:click="deleteNote({{ $note->id }})"`
  - inline edit swap: `@if ($editingId === $note->id)` +
    `wire:submit="updateNote"` + `wire:click="cancelEdit"`
  - shared `data.content` / `data.noted_at` bindings appear at least

### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`)
- **Added** `resources/views/lead-notes.blade.php`
- **Added** `tests/Feature/LeadNotesBladeViewTest.php`

### Learnings for future iterations
- **A custom RelationManager `$view` does NOT need to wrap with
  `<x-filament-panels::page>`.** That wrapper is for `Filament\Pages\Page`
  subclasses. A RelationManager is a Livewire component whose default
  view (`filament-panels::resources.relation-manager`) only renders
  `<div class="fi-resource-relation-manager">{{ $this->content }}</div>`.
  When you override `$view`, your custom blade replaces that wrapper
  entirely — start with a plain `<div>` (or no wrapper at all) and own
  the markup directly. Same shape for custom Page views like
  `tasks/kanban.blade.php` which DOES use the wrapper because
  TaskKanban extends `Filament\Resources\Pages\Page`.
- **`<x-filament-panels::form>` doesn't exist as a Blade component.**
  The AC's prose says to "inline an `<x-filament-panels::form>`
  driving createNote()" but there's no such component in
  `vendor/filament/filament/resources/views/components/`. The closest
  is `vendor/filament/schemas/resources/views/components/form.blade.php`
  (the Schemas form component used internally by `{{ $this->form }}`).
  For a custom RM blade that needs a Livewire-submitting form with
  arbitrary inputs, write the raw `<form wire:submit="method">` tag
  directly — bind inputs via `wire:model` (or render Filament's
  schema with `{{ $this->form }}` if you want the full schema renderer).
- **Rendering `{{ $this->form }}` twice in the same view is a footgun.**
  The schema is one Livewire form bound to `$data`; rendering it twice
  produces two DOM nodes with the same field names, causing Filament's
  form state machinery to thrash on input. The Lead Notes view sidesteps
  this entirely by using raw `<textarea wire:model="data.content">` +
  `<input wire:model="data.noted_at">` bindings — the same form state
  drives both the create form (when `$editingId === null`) and the
  inline edit form (when `$editingId === $note->id`), but only ONE form
  is in the DOM at any time because the two `@if` branches are mutually
  exclusive.
- **`@once <style>` block is the right pattern for view-local CSS that
  uses custom properties for dark mode.** The `--crm-*` custom property
  approach (set on a container selector, redefined inside `html.dark
  container`) lets a Blade view ship its own theme without depending
  on Tailwind class names or `dark:` variants. Mirrors the
  `list-kanban-toggle.blade.php:9-60` pattern. The `@once` directive
  guarantees the `<style>` block is emitted once per page even if the
  view is rendered multiple times (e.g. inside a tabbed
  RelationManager that mounts/unmounts on tab switches).
- **`wire:confirm` on a Livewire button gives a native browser confirm
  dialog before the action fires.** Cheaper than a Filament modal for
  destructive actions inside a custom view. Pair with the AC-driven
  `deleteNote()` soft-delete from US-004; the dropdown's Delete button
  uses `wire:confirm="Delete this note?"` so accidental clicks don't
  silently soft-delete a note. (Filament's `DeleteAction` modal would
  be the panel-native equivalent but requires wiring through a Filament
  Action — `wire:confirm` is faster and equivalent UX for this case.)
- **Order the notes loop by `created_at DESC` so the most recently
  added note appears immediately below the add card.** Matches how
  core CRM's Livewire `notes.blade.php` orders the notes collection.
  No need for a separate "pinned vs unpinned" branch — we dropped
  the `pinned` field from the form in US-001 of this series, so all
  notes are treated equal. Pinning could come back later as a future
  enhancement but is out of scope here.

- **Modified** `src/Resources/Leads/LeadResource.php` (swap RM class +

- **Modified** `tests/Feature/LeadInfolistTest.php`
- **Modified** `tests/Feature/RelationManagersTest.php` (split Lead from
  dataset + add Lead-only assertion)

### Learnings for future iterations
- **Subclass-swap stories on a Filament resource's `getRelations()`
  cascade into THREE classes of regression tests** that all need to
  shift along with the swap:
  1. Tests that assert positional `toBe([...])` ordering — the swap is
     a one-element substitution in the array literal.
  2. Tests that assert presence via `toContain($oldClass)` — they need
     to flip to the new subclass (toContain checks strict identity, NOT
     `is_a` / `is_subclass_of`).
  3. Dataset-driven tests that lumped the swapped resource together
     with peer resources — the swapped resource needs to be split out
     into its own assertion. The cleanest pattern is to drop the
     swapped resource from the dataset and add a same-shape new test
     that targets it explicitly.
  Grep for the old class name across `tests/` BEFORE the swap to find
  all three call sites. Skipping any of the three produces a
  green-then-red regression in the next story's CI run.
- **`toContain` is strict identity, not `is_a`.** Even though
  `LeadNotesRelationManager extends NotesRelationManager`,
  `expect([LeadNotesRelationManager::class])->toContain(NotesRelationManager::class)`
  FAILS — Pest's `toContain` matcher uses `in_array($needle, $haystack)`
  (which falls back to strict equality for class-name strings). If a
  future story needs an inheritance-aware "contains a subclass of"
  assertion, write a custom helper that uses
  `array_filter($relations, fn ($c) => is_subclass_of($c, $base))` —
  but for swap-locked-in tests, prefer explicit substitution to keep
  the assertion shape simple and the failure messages obvious.
- **Pint's `ordered_imports` fixer auto-sorts imports alphabetically
  in a case-sensitive way.** When inserting a new import where the
  existing alphabetical position is "off" (e.g. dropping
  `LeadNotesRelationManager` next to `NotesRelationManager` when the
  block already has `LunchesRelationManager` between L-E-A and L-U-N
  alphabetically), let pint do the sort rather than hand-placing the
  line. Saves one debug cycle on what "alphabetical order" means in
  pint's view (case-sensitive ASCII: `L < a` so `LeadNotes` comes
  before `LunchesRelationManager` correctly without thought).
- **Always grep the full test suite for the old class name before
  declaring a swap done.** This story's initial focused run hit only
  the AC-named `LeadResourceRelationOrderTest`. Without the wider
  `grep -rn NotesRelationManager tests/`, the `RelationManagersTest`
  and `LeadInfolistTest` regressions wouldn't have surfaced until
  someone ran the full suite. Cheap pre-flight check; expensive
  oversight if skipped.

### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`)
- **Modified** `tests/Feature/LeadNotesRelationManagerTest.php`
  (expanded from 5 to 9 tests, +4 new CRUD round-trip and Blade
  marker tests, + `leadNotesFocusedRm()` file-local helper)

### Learnings for future iterations
- **The "comprehensive single-file regression" story pattern coexists
  cleanly with the finer-grained sibling test files.** US-008's AC
  asks for ONE file that locks all five AC bullets — even though
  US-001 through US-005 already shipped per-method test files that
  cover the same surface area in greater depth. The right call is
  KEEP the existing per-method tests (they're the day-to-day
  regression gates that catch tighter contract violations like
  cross-lead injection or empty-content validation) AND add a focused
  test file that holds the canonical AC contract in one place. Two
  layers of coverage: per-method tests for nuance, single-file
  test for the at-a-glance "is the feature surface intact" check.
- **The hot-patch anonymous subclass pattern is the cleanest way to
  consolidate four CRUD method tests into one file.** Each sibling
  test file declared its own `leadNotesXxxRm()` helper (top-level
  Pest function with a globally-unique name). When merging into one
  file, define ONE `leadNotesFocusedRm()` helper whose anonymous
  subclass reimplements ALL four CRUD methods. Then each test calls
  the same factory and exercises only the method it cares about.
  Compared to copying the four sibling helpers into one file
  (which would collide on `editNote`/`updateNote`/`deleteNote` bodies
  if any two were reused), this gives a single source of truth for
  what the headless-test bodies should look like.
- **Top-level Pest function name uniqueness is per-file but
  GLOBALLY visible.** PHP's "Cannot redeclare function" error
  applies across the whole test run. The four sibling files use
  unique names (`leadNotesEditLifecycleRm`, `leadNotesDeleteRm`,
  etc.) — my new helper picked `leadNotesFocusedRm` to avoid any
  collision. Always prefix with the topic of the test file (or
  the AC story key when topic is generic), even if the test file
  is the only consumer. This is the same convention locked-in by
  `parityInvokeHeaderActions` / `showActionOrderInvokeHeaderActions` /
  `invokeLeadPageHeaderActions` across earlier stories.

### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`)
- **Added** `resources/views/partials/lead-card-styles.blade.php`
- **Modified** `resources/views/lead-notes.blade.php` (drop inline
  `@once <style>` block, add `@include`, rewrite every `crm-note-*`
  class attribute to `crm-card-*`)
- **Modified** `tests/Feature/LeadNotesBladeViewTest.php` (split + bump
  + +1 regression test)
- **Modified** `tests/Feature/LeadNotesRelationManagerTest.php` (bump
  AC(5) block to assert against the partial)

### Learnings for future iterations
- **A `@once <style>` block survives extraction into a partial because
  `@once` keys on the source location, not the file path.** Laravel's
  Blade compiler emits an `@once` block's contents inside a
  `$__env->startComponent('...')->renderComponent()`-style guard that
  hashes the compiled view's path + line number, so moving the same
  block into a partial that's `@include`-d from N call sites still
  produces a single `<style>` emission per page request. This is the
  cleanest pattern for any plugin-internal CSS that's shared across
  multiple Filament RelationManager / custom-view Blade templates —
  drop it into a `partials/{topic}-styles.blade.php` and let every
  consumer `@include` it without worrying about duplicate emission.
- **The AC's "rename `crm-note-*` to `crm-card-*`" should be read
  mechanically.** Even though it produces visually awkward names like
  `crm-card-card-head` (where the second "card" used to be the
  card-shape modifier and the first was the prefix), the alternative —
  collapsing "card-card" → "card" — would diverge from the AC and
  create a one-off rename rule that future stories in the series can't
  predict. The progress entry's "5 new Lead show-page tabs will share
  the partial" promise means the next 5 stories will introduce more
  classes; keeping the rename mechanical (`crm-note-` → `crm-card-`)
  gives them a stable rule to follow.
- **Selectively grep for `class="crm-note-`** when checking
  rename completeness — don't grep for the bare `crm-note-` string.
  The `crm-lead-note-*` test selectors (`data-testid`,
  `id` attributes) overlap textually with `crm-note-*` and would
  produce false positives in a bare-string grep. The narrower
  `class="crm-note-` pattern catches actual class refs without
  flagging the test selectors. Two passes — one with
  `class="crm-note-` and one with the data-testid pattern —
  gives a clean separation of "CSS class references" vs
  "test-only selectors".
- **Always pair an extracted-partial rename with a regression guard.**
  Two new test assertions catch silent regressions:
  (a) `expect($blade)->not->toContain('@once')` — fires if a future
  edit accidentally re-inlines a `<style>` block; and
  (b) `expect($blade)->not->toContain('class="crm-note-')` — fires if
  a future edit accidentally re-introduces an old class name. Both
  are one-line `not->toContain` assertions; cheap insurance against
  the dual failure modes (extraction reversal + naming reversal).


## US-002: Add LeadTasksRelationManager with inline-card Blade view and wire into LeadResource (lead card-styles series)
- New `src/RelationManagers/LeadTasksRelationManager.php` extends

  AND `form(Schema)->statePath('data')` with 5 fields (name + description +
  due_at + user_owner_id Grid'd with user_assigned_id). The form drops the
  parent `completed_at` field — task completion is now a separate workflow.

  the inline-card state. `mount()` calls `parent::mount()` then seeds

- Five lifecycle methods round out the inline CRUD quartet+ for tasks:
  - `createTask()` — validates via `$this->form->getState()`, persists via
    `getOwnerRecord()->tasks()->create([...])` with `user_owner_id` /
    `user_assigned_id` / `user_created_id = auth()->id()` populated
    explicitly. Calls `static::logCrmActivity($owner, $task)` to write the
    Activity timeline row. Re-fills form state and fires a

    logs activity, clears state, fires "Task updated" toast.

### Learnings for future iterations
- **The test schema's `crm_tasks` was missing `user_owner_id` even
  though core's migration declares it.** Symptom: an end-to-end test
  that passes `user_owner_id => $user->id` to `tasks()->create([...])`
  shows the value as null in `$task->getAttributes()` afterward — but
  user_created_id (which IS in the test schema and gets set by the
  observer) reads correctly. Eloquent's mass-assignment silently
  drops keys whose columns don't exist on the table. ALWAYS dump
  `$model->getAttributes()` before assuming a write succeeded — if a
  column is missing entirely from the JSON, that's the test schema
  gap. Same gotcha mentioned in v0.x US-021 (CallKanban) when
  `crm_calls` was missing `name` column — recurring pattern in this
  codebase. Cross-check `TestSchema.php` against
  `vendor/.../database/migrations/create_laravel_crm_*_table.php.stub`
  before assuming a column exists.
- **Sharing a CSS-custom-properties partial across multiple
  wrapper-class scopes is a one-line extension.** The original
  lead-card-styles partial scoped `--crm-card-*` to `.crm-lead-notes`
  only. Extending to also scope to `.crm-lead-tasks` is a comma in
  the selector — `.crm-lead-notes, .crm-lead-tasks { ... }` — plus
  the matching `html.dark` rule. Any future lead show-page tab that
  uses the same card visual treatment can be added the same way
  (one new wrapper class name in the comma-separated selector list).
  Future hygiene option: collapse into a single shared class like
  `.crm-lead-card-area` and have each wrapper apply BOTH the topic
  class AND the shared class, but the comma-list approach is fine
  while the count is small.
- **Subclass-swap stories cascade into the same three classes of
  regression tests as US-006 of the lead notes UI series.** Grep for
  the old class name (`TasksRelationManager` here) across `tests/`
  BEFORE editing — three classes of consumers:
  1. Positional `toBe([...])` ordering assertions (LeadResourceRelationOrderTest).
  2. `toContain($oldClass)` presence assertions (LeadInfolistTest).
  3. Dataset-driven tests where the swap'd resource was lumped with
     peers (RelationManagersTest's contactActivityParents — Lead was
     already split off in US-006 for the Notes swap, so this story
     just had to amend the existing Lead-specific test).
  Skipping any of the three produces a green-then-red regression in
  the next CI run.
- **The TaskObserver mirrors NoteObserver's hook structure.** Both
  observers stamp `user_created_id` on creating, `user_updated_id`
  on updating, `user_deleted_id` on deleting AND cascade-delete the
  linked Activity row on soft-delete. So `$task->delete()` is a
  complete operation from the panel — no manual `user_deleted_id`
  stamp or Activity cleanup needed. Same shape likely applies to
  Call/Meeting/Lunch observers (worth confirming when adding inline
  CRUD for those entities in future stories).
- **The inline-form template now generalises across three entity
  shapes** (Note, Task, and the upcoming Call/Meeting/Lunch).
  Standard pattern: `public ?array $data = []` + `public ?int
  $editingId = null` properties; `mount()` override seeds defaults;
  `form(Schema)->statePath('data')` declares the field schema;
  five lifecycle methods (`create{Entity}`, `edit{Entity}(int)`,
  `cancelEdit`, `update{Entity}`, `delete{Entity}(int)`) operate on
  `$this->data` and persist via `getOwnerRecord()->{relation}()->...`;
  matching Blade view includes the shared partial, renders an add
  card on top, then a `@forelse` of entity cards with three-dot
  dropdowns and inline edit swap. The hot-patch anonymous subclass
  in tests bypasses `$this->form->fill()` / `$this->form->getState()`
  so the round-trip can be exercised headless (same shape as US-008
  of the lead notes UI series). Should be the template for every
  remaining activity tab on the Lead show page.


## US-003: Add LeadCallsRelationManager with inline-card Blade view and wire into LeadResource (lead card-styles series)
- New `src/RelationManagers/LeadCallsRelationManager.php` extends
  `CallsRelationManager`. Overrides `protected string $view =
  'laravel-crm-filament::lead-calls'` AND `form(Schema)->statePath('data')`
  with 6 fields: name (required TextInput, full-span) + description
  (Textarea, full-span) + 2-col Grid containing start_at + finish_at
  DateTimePickers + 2-col Grid containing user_owner_id + user_assigned_id
  Selects. Matches the AC: "name+description+start_at+finish_at+
  user_owner_id+user_assigned_id (excluding guests and reminder_email/sms)"
  — the parent CallsRelationManager doesn't expose guests/reminder fields
  in its form, so the subclass keeps the same shape.
- Public `?array $data = []` and `?int $editingId = null` properties carry
  the inline-card state. `mount()` calls `parent::mount()` then seeds
  `$this->form->fill([...])` with defaults (now() for start_at, null for
  finish_at, auth()->id() for user_owner_id). Same shape as the lead
  notes/tasks pattern from US-001/US-002 of this series.
- Five lifecycle methods round out the inline CRUD quartet+ for calls:
  - `createCall()` — validates via `$this->form->getState()`, persists via
    `getOwnerRecord()->calls()->create([...])` with `user_owner_id` /
    `user_assigned_id` / `user_created_id = auth()->id()` populated
    explicitly. Calls `static::logCrmActivity($owner, $call)` to write the
    Activity timeline row. Re-fills form state and fires a
    `Notification::make()->title('Call added')->success()->send()` toast.
  - `editCall(int $id)` — resolves call via the owner relation
    (`calls()->whereKey($id)->first()`), silently no-ops on cross-lead
    injection, stamps `$editingId`, hydrates form with current values
    (name/description/start_at/finish_at/owner/assigned).
  - `cancelEdit()` — clears `$editingId` and resets form to defaults.
  - `updateCall()` — early-returns when `$editingId === null`, validates,
    re-resolves via owner relation (defensive against stale `editingId`),
    persists via `$call->update([...])` with `user_updated_id = auth()->id()`,
    logs activity, clears state, fires "Call updated" toast.
  - `deleteCall(int $id)` — resolves via owner relation, soft-deletes
    via `$call->delete()`. The core `CallObserver::deleting` stamps
    `user_deleted_id` and cascades into deleting the linked Activity row
    (same shape as NoteObserver/TaskObserver — verified by grep). Clears
    `$editingId` + form when the deleted call was being edited. Fires
    "Call deleted" toast.
- New `resources/views/lead-calls.blade.php` mirrors the lead-tasks
  Blade structurally with the call field set:
  - Wrapper `<div class="crm-lead-calls" data-testid="crm-lead-calls">`
    — new selector class the shared partial now also targets.
  - `@include('laravel-crm-filament::partials.lead-card-styles')` — shared
    from the lead-notes/tasks views. CSS custom properties scoped to
    `.crm-lead-notes`, `.crm-lead-tasks`, AND `.crm-lead-calls` (and
    matching dark-mode selectors).
  - Add-call card with name TextInput + description Textarea + start_at
    DateTimePicker + finish_at DateTimePicker. Section heading uses the
    new `actions.add_call` translation key (added to en/fr/es).
  - `@forelse` loop sorted by `created_at desc` over
    `$this->getOwnerRecord()->calls()`. Each call card renders
    `created_at?->diffForHumans() - createdByUser?->name` header, body
    shows call name as `<strong>` plus optional description, and a
    footer pill showing the start_at..finish_at range:
    `"{start} .. {finish}"` when both are set; single time when only one
    is set; pill hidden entirely when both null.
  - Three-dot dropdown driven by Alpine `x-data="{ open: false }"`
    with Edit and Delete buttons. Delete uses
    `wire:confirm="Delete this call?"`.
  - Inline edit swap: when `$editingId === $call->id`, body is replaced
    with `<form wire:submit="updateCall">` containing the four input
    fields + Save/Cancel.
  - Empty state: `@empty` → "No calls yet."
- The shared `partials/lead-card-styles.blade.php` partial extended to
  scope its CSS custom properties to BOTH the two existing wrapper
  classes AND the new `.crm-lead-calls` (and matching dark-mode rules).
  Third consumer of the partial — the AC's "shared with future tabs"
  promise from US-001 continues to land cleanly.
- `LeadResource::getRelations()` wires the new RM in place of the
  parent `CallsRelationManager::class` at index 3 (between LeadTasks
  and Meetings — order preserved). Import retargeted.
- Translation keys added to en/fr/es: `sections.add_call` ("Add call" /
  "Ajouter un appel" / "Añadir llamada"). All other strings the view
  needs (`fields.name`, `fields.description`, `money.start`,
  `money.finish`, `fields.owner`, `fields.assigned_to`, `actions.save`,
  `actions.cancel`) were already present.
- Three regression-guard test updates following the v0.x US-006 (lead
  notes UI) + US-002 (lead tasks UI) pattern:
  - `LeadResourceRelationOrderTest`: 3 occurrences of
    `CallsRelationManager` retargeted to `LeadCallsRelationManager`,
    including the 7-class `toBe([...])` ordering assertion.
  - `LeadInfolistTest`: 2 occurrences retargeted.
  - `RelationManagersTest`: the Lead-specific test now also asserts
    `LeadCallsRelationManager` present AND `CallsRelationManager` absent
    on Lead. The other 3 contact-activity parents (Deal/Person/
    Organization) continue to use the unmodified `CallsRelationManager`.
- Test schema patch in
  `tests/Database/Migrations/2024_01_01_000002_add_plugin_test_tables.php`:
  added `user_deleted_id unsignedBigInteger nullable` to `crm_calls`.
  The original supplementary migration declared `user_created_id` and
  `user_updated_id` but NOT `user_deleted_id` — without this column the
  `deleteCall()` end-to-end test would error from CallObserver::deleting
  trying to set the missing column via `$call->saveQuietly()`.
- New Pest test `tests/Feature/LeadCallsRelationManagerTest.php`
  (+9 tests / 26 assertions; full plugin suite now **989 passing
  (2809 assertions)**, up from 980 at the post-US-002 lead card-styles
  series baseline). Five AC bullets covered:
  - **(1) Inheritance** — `extends CallsRelationManager` via
    `is_subclass_of`.
  - **(2) $view value** — Reflection on the protected $view confirms it's
    declared locally AND value is `'laravel-crm-filament::lead-calls'`.
  - **(3) form schema** — full field set matches (name TextInput,
    description Textarea, Grid with start_at/finish_at, Grid with
    user_owner_id/user_assigned_id). Also confirms `getStatePath() === 'data'`.
    Walks two nested Grids' `$childComponents` via Reflection to assert
    the inner field names.
  - **(4) CRUD round-trip** — three end-to-end tests using the same
    hot-patch anonymous subclass pattern as
    LeadNotesRelationManagerTest + LeadTasksRelationManagerTest.
    createCall persists with user_owner_id + user_created_id, writes
    activity row, asserts callable morph link to the lead. updateCall
    persists edits with user_updated_id, writes activity. deleteCall
    soft-deletes and respects the SoftDeletes scope.
  - **(5) Blade markers** — source-grep on the new view confirms:
    `wire:submit="createCall"` + `wire:model="data.{name,description,start_at,finish_at}"`,
    `calls()->orderBy('created_at', 'desc')`, three-dot dropdown with
    editCall/deleteCall wire:clicks, inline edit swap, cancelEdit
    button, footer pill with `$call->start_at->format` +
    `$call->finish_at->format` + `..` separator, shared partial
    @include, "No calls yet" empty state. Also confirms the partial
    now declares `.crm-lead-calls` and `html.dark .crm-lead-calls`
    selectors.

### Learnings for future iterations
- **The CallObserver mirrors the NoteObserver + TaskObserver pattern
  exactly.** Stamps `user_created_id` on creating, `user_updated_id`
  on updating, `user_deleted_id` on deleting (via `saveQuietly()`)
  AND cascade-deletes the linked Activity row on soft-delete. So
  `$call->delete()` is a complete operation from the panel — no
  manual `user_deleted_id` stamp or Activity cleanup needed. The
  consistent observer shape across all four activity entities (Note,
  Task, Call, Meeting) confirms the inline-form template will
  continue to generalise cleanly for the remaining Meeting/Lunch
  stories in the lead card-styles series.
- **The test schema's `crm_calls` was missing `user_deleted_id`**
  even though core's migration declares it. Without it, any test
  that exercises `$call->delete()` would error on the CallObserver's
  `saveQuietly()` call because the column doesn't exist. Same gotcha
  shape as v0.x US-002 of the form-parity series (crm_tasks missing
  user_owner_id) and v0.x US-021 (crm_calls missing name column).
  Recurring pattern: ALWAYS cross-check `TestSchema.php` /
  supplementary migration against the upstream
  `vendor/.../database/migrations/create_laravel_crm_*_table.php.stub`
  whenever a new feature exercises a column that wasn't previously
  touched by tests. Best invested up-front check: 30 seconds of grep
  saves a full debug cycle on an opaque SQLite error.
- **The footer pill shape "start..finish" is the cleanest way to
  display a duration range without overflowing the pill width.** The
  AC says "footer pill shows start_at..finish_at" — literal `..`
  (two ASCII periods) is short, unambiguous, and won't collide with
  the `M d, Y` date format. Use this for any future "two-timestamp
  range pill" feature (meeting start/end, lunch start/end, etc.).
  Branch internally on which of the two are set: both → full range;
  one → single time; neither → hide the pill entirely. Avoids
  rendering a pill containing just `..` when both timestamps are
  missing.
- **Third consumer of the shared lead-card-styles partial**
  confirms the comma-list selector approach (`. crm-lead-notes,
  .crm-lead-tasks, .crm-lead-calls`) scales well. Each new lead
  show-page tab in the card-styles series only needs to add ONE
  wrapper class name to two places in the partial (the light-mode
  selector list and the matching `html.dark` block). Future
  refactor option: collapse into a single shared class
  `.crm-lead-card-area` once the count grows past 5; current
  comma-list is fine for 3-4 consumers.
- **Two-grid form schema (5+ fields) needs Reflection on each Grid
  separately in tests.** The previous lead-tasks test only had ONE
  nested Grid (owner + assigned); lead-calls has TWO (start/finish
  + owner/assigned). Reflection walk: `$gridProp =
  new ReflectionProperty(Grid::class, 'childComponents');
  $gridProp->setAccessible(true);` then for each Grid in
  `$components`, read its children via
  `$gridChildren['default'] ?? $gridChildren` and assert the inner
  names. Pair with `expect($components[i])->toBeInstanceOf(Grid::class)`
  to lock the structural ordering at the top level.

### Learnings for future iterations
- **The MeetingObserver mirrors the Note/Task/Call observer pattern
  exactly.** Stamps `user_created_id` on creating, `user_updated_id`
  on updating, `user_deleted_id` on deleting (via `saveQuietly()`)
  AND cascade-deletes the linked Activity row on soft-delete. So
  `$meeting->delete()` is a complete operation from the panel — no
  manual `user_deleted_id` stamp or Activity cleanup needed. The
  consistent observer shape across all four activity entities (Note,
  Task, Call, Meeting) confirms the inline-form template will
  continue to generalise cleanly for the remaining Lunch story in
  the lead card-styles series.
- **The test schema's `crm_meetings` was missing BOTH `user_owner_id`
  AND `user_deleted_id`** even though core's migration declares both.
  This is a double gotcha — every prior US-002/US-003 added one
  column, but Meetings needs both. Without `user_owner_id`, the
  createMeeting end-to-end test silently drops the value at the DB
  layer (no SQL error — Eloquent's mass-assign skips missing columns).
  Without `user_deleted_id`, the deleteMeeting test errors on the
  MeetingObserver's `saveQuietly()` call. Always audit the FULL
  `user_*_id` column set against the supplementary migration
  whenever a new feature exercises any of them — same gotcha shape
  noted across many prior stories in this codebase.
- **The location column lives in the test schema already but not
  in core's migration stub.** Looking at
  `vendor/venturedrake/laravel-crm/database/migrations/create_laravel_crm_meetings_table.php.stub`
  there's no `location` column declared, but the Livewire UI
  (MeetingItem.php / MeetingRelated.php) DOES write to it. This
  suggests there's a follow-up migration in a host's actual install
  that adds the column — but the plugin's own test schema includes
  it pre-emptively (line 142 of the supplementary migration). The
  AC's "location displayed" requirement means hosts who haven't
  migrated this column will see a silent failure when trying to
  write through the panel. Worth flagging in a future migration-
  publishing story but not a US-004 blocker — the panel writes via
  mass-assignment and Eloquent skips missing columns gracefully.
- **Adding TWO translation keys (fields.* + sections.*) in the
  same story** is best done in two separate insertions per locale,
  each anchored to a different stable key. `fields.location` anchors
  off `fields.phone`; `sections.add_meeting` anchors off
  `sections.add_call`. Mixing the two into one regex pass risks
  anchor-key collisions if the same word appears in multiple
  namespaces (the same `'add_call'` gotcha mentioned in earlier
  stories where literal `'products'` appeared in both `money.*` and
  `sections.*`).
- **Four-rich-field form schema (with one full-width field between
  two Grids) needs careful index alignment in tests.** The previous
  lead-calls test asserted `components[2]` is a Grid (start/finish)
  and `components[3]` is a Grid (owner/assigned). For lead-meetings,
  components are `[0]=name, [1]=description, [2]=Grid(start/finish),
  [3]=location, [4]=Grid(owner/assigned)`. The Reflection-walk
  assertions need to be updated to walk `components[2]` AND
  `components[4]` (skipping over the standalone location at [3]).
  Pattern in `it('returns the expected form schema with name,
  description, start/finish times, location, owner, assigned'`
  shows the right shape.


## US-005: Add LeadLunchesRelationManager flipping Lunches from read-only to editable in the Lead context (lead card-styles series)
- New `src/RelationManagers/LeadLunchesRelationManager.php` extends
  `LunchesRelationManager`. Overrides `protected string $view =
  'laravel-crm-filament::lead-lunches'`, overrides `isReadOnly(): bool
  => false` (flipping the parent's read-only contract), and overrides
  `form(Schema)->statePath('data')` with 7 fields: name (required
  TextInput, full-span) + description (Textarea, full-span) + 2-col Grid
  containing start_at + finish_at DateTimePickers + location TextInput
  (full-span) + 2-col Grid containing user_owner_id + user_assigned_id
  Selects. Matches the AC: "Meeting-style form (name+description+start_at
  +finish_at+location+user_owner_id+user_assigned_id)" — including the
  location field (test schema declares it even though core's stub
  doesn't, same as Meetings).
- Adds `use LogsCrmActivity;` trait — the parent `LunchesRelationManager`
  does NOT use the trait (unlike `MeetingsRelationManager` /
  `CallsRelationManager` / `NotesRelationManager` / `TasksRelationManager`)
  because it ships as a read-only standalone view. The Lead subclass
  needs the trait to call `static::logCrmActivity($owner, $lunch)` from
  its lifecycle methods. Differs from US-002/US-003/US-004 of this series
  where the parent already brought the trait via inheritance.
- Public `?array $data = []` and `?int $editingId = null` properties carry
  the inline-card state. `mount()` calls `parent::mount()` then seeds
  `$this->form->fill([...])` with defaults (now() for start_at, null for
  finish_at + location, auth()->id() for user_owner_id). Same shape as
  the lead notes/tasks/calls/meetings pattern.
- Five lifecycle methods round out the inline CRUD quartet+ for lunches:
  - `createLunch()` — validates via `$this->form->getState()`, persists
    via `getOwnerRecord()->lunches()->create([...])` with `location`,
    `user_owner_id`, `user_assigned_id`, `user_created_id = auth()->id()`
    populated explicitly. Calls `static::logCrmActivity($owner, $lunch)`.
    Re-fills form state and fires `Notification::make()->title('Lunch added')
    ->success()->send()` toast.
  - `editLunch(int $id)` — resolves lunch via the owner relation
    (`lunches()->whereKey($id)->first()`), silently no-ops on cross-lead
    injection, stamps `$editingId`, hydrates form with current values
    (name/description/start_at/finish_at/location/owner/assigned).
  - `cancelEdit()` — clears `$editingId` and resets form to defaults.
  - `updateLunch()` — early-returns when `$editingId === null`, validates,
    re-resolves via owner relation (defensive against stale `editingId`),
    persists via `$lunch->update([...])` with `user_updated_id =
    auth()->id()`, logs activity, clears state, fires "Lunch updated"
    toast.
  - `deleteLunch(int $id)` — resolves via owner relation, soft-deletes
    via `$lunch->delete()`. The core `LunchObserver::deleting` stamps
    `user_deleted_id` and cascades into deleting the linked Activity row
    (same shape as NoteObserver/TaskObserver/CallObserver/MeetingObserver
    — verified by grep). Clears `$editingId` + form when the deleted
    lunch was being edited. Fires "Lunch deleted" toast.
- New `resources/views/lead-lunches.blade.php` mirrors lead-meetings.blade.php
  structurally with the lunch field set:
  - Wrapper `<div class="crm-lead-lunches" data-testid="crm-lead-lunches">`
    — new selector class the shared partial now also targets.
  - `@include('laravel-crm-filament::partials.lead-card-styles')` — shared
    from the lead-notes/tasks/calls/meetings views. CSS custom properties

  - Add-lunch card with name TextInput + description Textarea + start_at

  - `@forelse` loop sorted by `created_at desc` over

  - Three-dot dropdown driven by Alpine `x-data="{ open: false }"`

  - Empty state: `@empty` → "No lunches yet."

### Learnings for future iterations
- **The standalone read-only "global view" RM (LunchesRelationManager)
  doesn't use the LogsCrmActivity trait**, unlike NotesRelationManager /
  TasksRelationManager / CallsRelationManager / MeetingsRelationManager
  (all of which use the trait via the inline "after" callbacks they
  expose for the upstream CreateAction). When a Lead* subclass needs
  to log activity from its own lifecycle methods, the trait must be
  applied to the subclass directly (`use LogsCrmActivity;` in the
  class body). Don't assume inheritance — grep the parent first to see
  what traits it brings in.
- **Tests that only surface on the FULL plugin suite — not narrowly-
  scoped targeted filter runs.** Before claiming a swap story is done,
  always run the full suite as the final gate. The
  `LunchesRelationManagerTest::it('is registered on LeadResource...')`
  assertion in US-008 of the lead show-page series was the regression
  that hid from the targeted `--filter` runs in this story (filter
  names that grep the test description don't always catch unrelated
  test files that incidentally assert on the same FQCN). Same gotcha
  shape as US-006 of the lead notes UI series noted in earlier
  progress entries — but with one new failure mode: this test was
  in a file whose NAME (`LunchesRelationManagerTest.php`) didn't
  match my filter pattern, so even running
  `--filter='LeadLunches|LeadInfolist|LeadResourceRelationOrder|RelationManagers'`
  missed it. Always run the FULL pest suite as the final gate before
  declaring complete — same pattern locked in by the v0.x US-009
  story.
- **The LunchObserver mirrors the Note/Task/Call/Meeting observer
  pattern exactly.** Stamps `user_created_id` on creating,
  `user_updated_id` on updating, `user_deleted_id` on deleting (via
  `saveQuietly()`) AND cascade-deletes the linked Activity row on
  soft-delete. So `$lunch->delete()` is a complete operation from
  the panel — no manual `user_deleted_id` stamp or Activity cleanup
  needed. Five-for-five observer consistency across the activity
  family (Note, Task, Call, Meeting, Lunch) confirms the inline-form
  template generalises perfectly — this is the LAST lead show-page
  tab in the card-styles series, completing the parity work
  established by US-001 (extract shared partial).
- **The lead card-styles series is now complete — five consumers of
  the shared partial.** The `partials/lead-card-styles.blade.php`
  comma-list selector now covers all five wrapper classes:
  `.crm-lead-notes, .crm-lead-tasks, .crm-lead-calls, .crm-lead-meetings,
  .crm-lead-lunches` (and matching `html.dark` block). If a future
  story adds a sixth (e.g. files or audits as inline cards), the
  pattern is well-established: one wrapper class in TWO places in
  the partial. Future hygiene option from US-002's progress entry —
  collapse into a single shared class `.crm-lead-card-area` with
  composite `class="crm-lead-card-area crm-lead-lunches"` on the
  wrapper — would now be a cleaner refactor since the count has
  reached the originally-named "past 5" threshold. Worth doing as a
  follow-up hygiene pass.
- **Same dual schema gotcha as Meetings.** `crm_lunches` was missing
  both `user_owner_id` AND `user_deleted_id` in the test schema even
  though core's migration declares both. Recurring pattern across
  US-002 (tasks: user_owner_id), US-003 (calls: user_deleted_id),
  US-004 (meetings: BOTH), and now US-005 (lunches: BOTH). The
  test schema's `user_*_id` declarations are inconsistently incomplete
  across activity tables — future hygiene pass: audit ALL activity
  tables in the supplementary migration against their core migration
  stubs and bring them up to full parity in one go, so subsequent
  stories don't keep tripping on this.


## US-006: Add LeadFilesRelationManager with upload/download/delete inline cards (lead card-styles series)
- New `src/RelationManagers/LeadFilesRelationManager.php` extends
  `FilesRelationManager`. Overrides `protected string $view =
  'laravel-crm-filament::lead-files'` AND `form(Schema)->statePath('data')`
  with TWO fields per AC: FileUpload `file` (full-span, required,
  preserve filenames, stored to `config('laravel-crm.upload_disk',
  'public')`) and TextInput `title` (optional, max 255). NO edit-mode
  field set — the AC explicitly says "no edit mode".
- Public `?array $data = []` property carries the inline-card state.
  `mount()` calls `parent::mount()` then seeds the form with
  `['file' => null, 'title' => null]`. The `editingId` property
  pattern from US-002..US-005 of this series is intentionally absent
  — files don't have an inline-edit flow, only upload/download/delete.
- Three lifecycle methods (AC named: `mount`, `createFile`,
  `downloadFile(int)`, `deleteFile(int)`):
  - `createFile()` — validates via `$this->form->getState()`, computes
    name (basename), filesize, mime, and format from the stored file
    on `Storage::disk($disk)`, persists via
    `getOwnerRecord()->files()->create([...])` with `file`/`name`/`title`/
    `format`/`filesize`/`mime`/`disk`/`user_created_id = auth()->id()`
    populated explicitly. Calls `static::logCrmActivity($owner, $file)`
    to write the Activity timeline row. Re-fills form state and fires
    `Notification::make()->title('File added')->success()->send()`
    toast.
  - `downloadFile(int $id): ?string` — resolves via the owner relation
    (`files()->whereKey($id)->first()`), silently returns null on
    cross-lead injection (the morphMany scopes the lookup). When a
    valid file is found, builds a URL via
    `Storage::disk($file->disk)->temporaryUrl($file->file,
    now()->addMinutes(5))` and falls back to `->url()` if the disk
    doesn't support signed URLs. Public so the Blade view can call
    it inline via `{{ $this->downloadFile($file->id) }}` to render
    `<a href="...">` links.
  - `deleteFile(int $id): void` — resolves via owner relation,
    soft-deletes via `$file->delete()`. The core
    `FileObserver::deleting` stamps `user_deleted_id` (when not
    runningInConsole) and cascades into deleting the linked Activity
    row. Fires "File deleted" toast.
- New `resources/views/lead-files.blade.php` mirrors the lead-notes
  Blade structurally with the file field set:
  - Wrapper `<div class="crm-lead-files" data-testid="crm-lead-files">`
    — new selector class the shared partial now also targets.
  - `@include('laravel-crm-filament::partials.lead-card-styles')` —
    sixth (and likely final) consumer of the shared partial. CSS
    custom properties scoped to `.crm-lead-notes / .crm-lead-tasks /
    .crm-lead-calls / .crm-lead-meetings / .crm-lead-lunches / .crm-lead-files`
    plus matching dark-mode selectors.
  - Upload card (always visible — no `@if ($editingId === null)`
    branch since there's no edit mode). Uses `{{ $this->form }}` to
    render Filament's FileUpload+TextInput schema directly — cleaner
    than hand-rolling a `<input type="file">` because FileUpload's
    drag-drop UI + chunked upload handling are non-trivial. Section
    heading uses the new `sections.add_file` translation key.
  - `@forelse` loop sorted by `created_at desc` over
    `$this->getOwnerRecord()->files()`. Each file card renders
    `created_at?->diffForHumans() - createdByUser?->name` header,
    body shows `$file->name ?? $file->file` as `<strong>` plus
    optional `$file->title`, and a footer pill showing
    `{filesize} bytes · {mime}` (with conditional rendering: shows
    only the populated parts, or nothing if both are null).
  - Three-dot dropdown driven by Alpine `x-data="{ open: false }"`
    with Download (anchor link computed via `$this->downloadFile($file->id)`,
    `target="_blank" rel="noopener"`) AND Delete (button with
    `wire:click="deleteFile({{ $file->id }})"` +
    `wire:confirm="Delete this file?"`). Hidden when download URL
    resolves to null (cross-tenant injection).
  - NO Edit option in the dropdown (AC: "Download + Delete only"). No
    inline edit-form swap. Empty state: `@empty` → "No files yet."
- The shared `partials/lead-card-styles.blade.php` partial extended
  to scope its CSS custom properties to BOTH the five existing
  wrapper classes AND the new `.crm-lead-files` (and matching
  dark-mode rules). Sixth consumer of the partial.
- `LeadResource::getRelations()` swaps `FilesRelationManager::class`
  for `LeadFilesRelationManager::class` at index 6 (last position
  in the array). The import for the parent FQCN was auto-removed by
  pint's `no_unused_imports` rule.
- Translation keys added to en/fr/es:
  - `sections.add_file` ("Add file" / "Ajouter un fichier" /
    "Añadir archivo") — added after `sections.add_lunch`.
  - `fields.file` ("File" / "Fichier" / "Archivo") — added after
    `fields.description`. Distinct from the existing `file.file`
    namespace which is for the standalone FileResource page.
  - `fields.title` ("Title" / "Titre" / "Título") — added after
    the newly inserted `fields.file`.
  `actions.download` was already in place from v0.7 standalone
  resources.
- Test schema **rewritten** in
  `tests/Database/Migrations/2024_01_01_000002_add_plugin_test_tables.php`:
  the `crm_files` table's column shape was completely wrong vs core
  CRM (had `filename`/`original_filename`/`file_type` instead of
  core's `file`/`name`/`format`). Replaced with the core's exact
  shape from `create_laravel_crm_files_table.php.stub`:
  `external_id / team_id / fileable_* / file / name / title / format
  / filesize / mime / disk / user_created_id / user_updated_id /
  user_deleted_id / user_restored_id / timestamps / softDeletes`.
  No prior test wrote File rows directly, so this column rename
  doesn't break anything else.
- Three regression-guard test updates following the prior series
  patterns:
  - `LeadResourceRelationOrderTest`: 3 occurrences of
    `FilesRelationManager` retargeted to `LeadFilesRelationManager`,
    including the 7-class `toBe([...])` ordering assertion. Import
    retargeted.
  - `LeadInfolistTest`: 2 occurrences retargeted. Import retargeted.
  - `StandaloneActivityResourcesTest`: dropped Lead from the
    `filesRelationManagerParents` dataset (used by the
    "attaches FilesRelationManager to every parent resource" loop),

### Learnings for future iterations
- **The test schema's `crm_files` was using completely wrong column
  names compared to core CRM** (`filename` instead of `file`,
  `original_filename` instead of `name`, `file_type` instead of
  `format`, plus missing `user_deleted_id`/`user_restored_id`). The
  table had been there since the v0.7 standalone resources story but
  no test had ever actually written File rows to it — only structural
  presence assertions. The first story to do real File CRUD (this
  one) had to rewrite the entire table definition to align with
  core. Pattern: ANY new feature story that writes to a previously
  untested table needs to compare the test schema column-by-column
  against the core migration stub at
  `vendor/.../database/migrations/create_laravel_crm_*_table.php.stub`
  BEFORE the first write. Cheaper to verify up-front than to debug
  "expected X, got null" failures in test runs.
- **The FileObserver's `user_created_id` stamp is gated by
  `! app()->runningInConsole()`.** In tests, `runningInConsole()`
  returns true, so the observer doesn't write `user_created_id`
  automatically. The same gotcha applies to FileObserver::updating
  AND FileObserver::deleting (which writes `user_deleted_id` via
  `saveQuietly()`). For the Filament inline-card lifecycle methods,
  ALWAYS pass `user_created_id => auth()->id()` explicitly when
  creating — same pattern as the LeadNotes/Tasks/Calls/Meetings/Lunches
  RMs in the prior series. Don't rely on the observer to fill it in
  for you, especially in tests. (The other observers — Note, Task,
  Call, Meeting, Lunch — don't have this gating, hence why the
  prior stories in this series didn't trip on it.)
- **Filament's FileUpload widget can be rendered inline via
  `{{ $this->form }}`** as a single Blade output, even when the
  parent view is a custom RelationManager template. This is
  significantly cleaner than trying to hand-roll a
  `<input type="file" wire:model="data.file">` because FileUpload's
  drag-drop UI, chunked upload handling, and post-upload state
  serialization are all bundled into the Livewire component. Same
  pattern works for any future inline-card view that needs to
  reuse a Filament form component without the full panel CRUD
  modal — drop the schema in via `statePath('data')` and render the
  schema with `{{ $this->form }}`.
- **No edit-mode inline-card pattern.** When the AC says "no edit
  mode", the entire `editingId` property + `editXxx(int)` +
  `cancelEdit()` + `updateXxx()` triad from the prior 5 stories in
  this series should be DROPPED. The Blade view also doesn't need
  the `@if ($editingId === $row->id)` swap — the card always
  renders the read-only display. Files are a natural fit for this
  shape because attachments are immutable in the user's mental
  model (you re-upload to replace, not edit a row's metadata in
  place).
- **`$this->downloadFile($file->id)` from Blade is a legitimate
  pattern for "return a URL string at render time".** Livewire
  invokes the method during view compilation when `{{ ... }}`
  resolves to a method call on `$this`. This is the cleanest way
  to render an anchor link whose URL is computed from server-side
  logic (the temporaryUrl with signed-URL fallback in this case).
  Pair with `wire:click` handlers only when the action mutates
  state — for pure read-side URL generation, the direct method
  call in Blade reads cleaner and produces a working `<a href>`
  link the user can right-click to copy.
- **`Storage::fake('local')` requires setting
  `config(['laravel-crm.upload_disk' => 'local'])` for the
  RelationManager's createFile() path to land on the faked disk.**
  Default config is 'public' which doesn't match the fake. Easy
  miss when writing tests — `Storage::fake('local')` is the most
  common signature but only works if the production code is
  reading 'local' from config. Either fake the right disk name OR
  override the config in the test's `beforeEach`. Same gotcha
  applies to any future test that needs FileUpload integration.
- **Sixth (and likely final) consumer of the shared
  lead-card-styles partial.** With Files now using the partial,
  all six lead show-page tab variants in this series share one
  CSS source. The comma-separated selector list in the partial
  is now 6-deep — at this point the v0.5-noted "future hygiene
  option: collapse into a single shared class
  `.crm-lead-card-area`" is worth considering as a follow-up
  refactor. For now, the comma-list still works cleanly and the
  test assertions on `.crm-lead-files` lock in the contract.

### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`)
- **Added** `tests/Feature/LeadShowPageRelationManagersTest.php`

### Learnings for future iterations
- **A "comprehensive single-file regression gate" test belongs alongside
  the finer-grained per-method tests, not as a replacement.** US-001..US-006
  of the lead card-styles series already shipped per-RM tests that exercise
  CRUD round-trips with hot-patch subclasses (~10 tests per RM, 5 RMs × ~10
  + Files = ~70 tests covering the entity-specific edge cases). This new
  20-test file doesn't duplicate those round-trips — it's the at-a-glance
  "is the FEATURE SURFACE intact" gate that locks the 5 AC bullets in one
  place. Same pattern as v0.x US-008 of the lead notes UI series, which
  added the comprehensive `LeadNotesRelationManagerTest` regression file
  ALONGSIDE the per-method tests rather than replacing them. Two layers of
  coverage: per-method tests catch the nuanced bugs, single-file tests
  catch the structural-surface bugs.
- **Pest dataset functions with shared keys produce one test description per
  dataset entry.** A single `it('AC(b): ...')` definition with `->with([...])`
  produces 6 lines in the test output, one per dataset key. This gives
  granular test names without duplicating the test body — the only cost is
  that the test description is identical across all 6, which Pest renders
  as `it('description') -> ('Notes')`, `it('description') -> ('Tasks')`,
  etc. For a "comprehensive gate" file this is exactly what you want — the
  AC bullet is the same, the dataset key tells you which entity failed if
  the test breaks.
- **Walking up the test file's directory tree to find the project root
  uses `dirname(__DIR__, 2)`.** From `tests/Feature/Foo.php`, `dirname(__DIR__, 2)`
  resolves to the plugin's repo root. Use this for `file_exists()` checks on
  Blade templates or other non-PHP assets that live in `resources/views/`.
  Don't use `base_path('resources/views/...')` from within a testbench-
  hosted test — `base_path()` resolves relative to the testbench's
  `vendor/orchestra/testbench-core/laravel` directory, not the plugin's
  actual root. Same gotcha noted in v0.9a of the v0.x sequence
  (LocalizationTest).
- **Source-grep tests are the cheapest way to lock structural contracts on
  Blade templates.** Filament's Blade rendering pipeline is hard to exercise
  from a pure unit test (it requires a real Livewire mount + a panel
  context + a parent record), so asserting on the Blade source directly
  via `file_get_contents()` + `expect(...)->toContain(...)` is the right
  trade-off for "AC says this marker MUST appear in the view." Catches
  drift cheaply, runs in milliseconds, and the failure message ("expected
  X to contain Y") is immediately actionable. Pair source-grep with
  per-method functional tests (which cover the actual Livewire+DB
  round-trip) for full coverage.
- **Always include the wrapper class assertion in a structural Blade
  test.** The `crm-lead-{notes,tasks,...}` wrapper class is what scopes
  the partial's CSS custom properties — without that class on the outer
  `<div>`, the partial's selectors don't match anything and the dark-mode
  block silently fails. Source-grep for `class="crm-lead-{x}"` to catch
  this. Same trick works for any future "shared CSS partial scoped to N
  wrapper classes" pattern.

### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`)
- **Renamed** 7 RM classes under `src/RelationManagers/`
- **Renamed** 7 tab blade views under `resources/views/`
- **Renamed** 7 partial blade files under `resources/views/partials/`
- **Modified** `src/Resources/Leads/LeadResource.php` (FQCN imports +
  `getRelations()` array swap)
- **Modified** 7 RM class bodies (class declaration + `$view` path)
- **Modified** 7 tab view contents (wrapper class + data-testid + partial @include)
- **Modified** 7 partial contents (CSS selectors + per-card `@include`s)
- **Modified** 17 test files under `tests/Feature/`

### Learnings for future iterations
- **A pure-rename story still produces ~35 file edits + 21 git renames.**
  Don't underestimate the scope just because the AC says "rename only".
  The transformation matrix here was 5 layers deep:
  1. **Class names** (FQCNs in PHP source + tests + production code's
     `getRelations()` array)
  2. **View Blade paths** (`laravel-crm-filament::lead-{x}` string
     literals in PHP `$view` property declarations AND tests)
  3. **Partial Blade paths** (`partials.lead-card-{x}` in `@include`
     directives across the 7 tab views AND tests)
  4. **CSS wrapper class names** (`.crm-lead-{x}` selectors in the
     shared partial AND wrapper `class=`/`data-testid=` attributes in
     the 7 tab views AND source-grep tests)
  5. **Filesystem path strings** (`resources/views/lead-{x}.blade.php`
     in `dirname(__DIR__, 2) . '/...'` test assertions)
  Catch all 5 in ONE refactor script and one targeted second pass —
  trying to do them as 5 separate stories would multiply the work via
  context loss + repeated quality-gate runs.
- **Test failures after a rename surface in three distinct shapes:**
  (a) class-not-found / wrong-FQCN errors — the easiest to catch (the
  bulk content rewrite handles them); (b) "expected X to contain Y"
  failures where Y is a hardcoded string literal in test assertions —
  these need a second pass that handles dataset values, slug strings,
  AND filesystem path strings; (c) "file not found" failures from
  `file_exists()` / `file_get_contents()` calls against the OLD path
  — same fix as (b). When writing the refactor script up-front,
  enumerate all three failure shapes in the replacement map; otherwise
  expect one cycle of "run tests, see hardcoded strings still pointing
  at old names, patch, re-run".
- **`git mv` preserves history through a rename** for git blame /
  log to follow. Always prefer `git mv $from $to` over rm+add+commit
  — the latter loses the file's commit history and shows the rename
  as a fresh add. Pair with content rewrites BEFORE the `git mv` so
  the file's internal references match its new home.
- **The CSS wrapper class rename was *almost* mechanical, but not
  quite.** A naive global substitution of `crm-lead-` → `crm-card-area-`
  would have nuked legitimate `data-testid="crm-lead-note-card"` IDs
  (which use `crm-lead-{singular}-{thing}` shape, not the wrapper
  `crm-lead-{plural}` shape). The safer pattern: enumerate the
  EXACT 7 wrapper class names (`crm-lead-notes`, `crm-lead-tasks`,
  ...) and substitute each as a whole word. The refactor script's
  `$wrapperReplacements` array does exactly this — same trick is
  worth applying to any future "rename `prefix-{slug}` → `newprefix-{slug}`"
  story where the prefix overlaps with other class names.
