### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`)
- **Modified** `src/Resources/Features/FeatureResource.php` (Details
  section closure body rewritten to 6 fields in AC-named order;
  Custom Fields section + ->hidden() gate untouched)
- **Modified** `tests/Feature/FeatureResourceTest.php` (+3 new tests
  after the existing infolist test: AC positional-strpos walk +
  dropped-fields regression guard + Custom Fields byte-for-byte
  literal-source assertion)

### Learnings for future iterations
- **Python's `open(path, 'w')` defaults to text mode with UTF-8
  encoding.** Writing `'\xe2\x80\x94'` as a Python literal produces a
  3-character string `'â\x80\x94'` (U+00E2 + U+0080 + U+0094), which
  then gets UTF-8 encoded to 6 bytes `0xC3 0xA2 0xC2 0x80 0xC2 0x94`
  in the file — a "double-encoded" em-dash that displays as `â` on
  read. Two clean fixes:
  - Use the bare em-dash character `'—'` directly in the Python
    source (Python's source is UTF-8 by default; the encoded bytes
    will round-trip cleanly).
  - OR open the file in binary mode (`open(path, 'wb')`) and write
    raw byte strings `b'\xe2\x80\x94'`.
  ALWAYS verify post-substitution with `od -c | head` to confirm
  the bytes are correct — the visual display alone can mislead. The
  fixup script in this story uses `open(path, 'rb')` +
  `src.replace(bad_bytes, good_bytes)` to repair the encoding in
  place, then re-verifies with `od`. Pattern worth adding to the
  Python-rewrite template for any future story that touches non-
  ASCII content.
- **Scoping a `not->toContain()` regression guard to a STRUCTURAL
  SUB-SECTION of the source file requires extracting a substring.**
  The AC says "Source no longer references `is_public`, `votes_count`,
  `comments_count`, `views_count`, `labels.name`, or `assignedToUser.name`
  inside the Details section closure." A naive
  `expect($wholeSource)->not->toContain("TextEntry::make('is_public')")`
  would pass even if the table()'s `TextColumn::make('is_public')`
  used a similar literal, AND it would fire false negatives if the
  AC ever wanted `is_public` to appear in some other infolist
  section. The right pattern is to extract the Details closure body
  via `strpos` start/end anchors:
  - START: `'->schema(fn (?Feature $record) => array_merge(['`
  - END: `'], $record ? static::crmCustomFieldEntries($record, false)'`
  Then assert against the extracted substring. The anchors are
  unique enough in source to never collide; if Filament's closure
  signature ever changes, the anchor will need an update but the
  pattern stays the same.
- **`composer format-test` may not be the actual script name in
  the consuming repo.** AC's named gate `composer format-test`
  doesn't exist in this plugin — the equivalent is `composer
  test:lint`. Always grep the repo's `composer.json` for the actual
  script names before assuming the AC's prose matches the available
  commands. The functional contract ("pint --test passes on my
  changes") is satisfied via `./vendor/bin/pint --dirty --test`
  regardless of which composer alias wraps it. Document the
  divergence in the progress entry so future stories don't waste
  time hunting for a non-existent script.
- **The Pest output of a story that says "pre-existing tests still
  pass" reads as `git stash`-based round-trip equality**: the same
  failures remain at the same line numbers with the same error
  messages, pre-change vs post-change. The AC's intent is NOT
  "the pre-existing failures must be fixed by this story" — it's
  "this story must not REGRESS anything that was passing before."
  Once you confirm the failure count and identity is byte-identical
  pre/post, the AC's contract is met. Don't over-read the AC's
  prose as requiring you to repair pre-existing baseline failures
  that are out of scope.
- **Anchoring Pest test insertions to a multi-line literal of the
  existing test body** is more robust than line-number-based
  patching. The python script in this story uses the existing
  `it('declares an infolist override...')` test's full source as
  the anchor and appends new tests with a `str.replace()` that
  pastes the new tests right after the closing `});`. Survives
  unrelated indentation/whitespace shifts in the file; fails
  loudly with `SystemExit` if the anchor isn't found. Cleaner
  pattern than `re.sub` with a partial anchor that might match
  unintended locations.


## US-005: Rewrite ViewFeature page with stacked layout, subheading, and Public view action (ViewFeature redesign series)
- Full rewrite of

  - **`getSubheading(): string | Htmlable | null`** — returns an
    `HtmlString` carrying ONE OR TWO inline pills depending on record
    state:
    1. Status pill — colored via `background-color: #{ltrim($hex, '#')}`
       (white text, padding 2px 8px, border-radius 9999px, font-size

    2. Private pill — gray background, white text, same shape as
       the status pill but labelled
       `__('laravel-crm-filament::labels.misc.private')`. Rendered ONLY
       when `! $record->is_public`.

    `$record->is_public` is true (no status to render, nothing to

### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`)
- **Modified** `src/Resources/Features/Pages/ViewFeature.php` (+7
  imports, +`getSubheading(): string | Htmlable | null` method,
  +`publicView` action in `getHeaderActions()`, rewrote
  `content(Schema)` to the 3-row stacked layout, +`getAllRelationManagers()`
  returning `[]`)
- **Modified** `tests/Feature/FeatureResourceTest.php` (replaced 3
  legacy tests with 5 new tests covering subheading + public view
  action + content row layout + Livewire embeds + getAllRelationManagers
  regression guard)

### Learnings for future iterations
- **Overriding `getAllRelationManagers(): array` on a single page
  class is the cleanest way to hide RM tabs on ONE page while
  preserving them on sibling pages.** Filament's `HasRelationManagers`
  trait declares `getAllRelationManagers()` as `protected` with the
  default body
  `return $this->getResource()::getRelations();` (line 27 of
  `vendor/filament/filament/src/Resources/Pages/Concerns/HasRelationManagers.php`).
  Override it on the page to return `[]` (or any subset) and the
  RM tab strip + render block both drop out — the resource's
  `getRelations()` is left untouched, so other pages on the same
  resource (Edit/Create/custom sub-pages) continue to see the full
  list. This is the right shape whenever a story says "show this
  page WITHOUT the usual RM tabs" — much cleaner than overriding
  `getRelations()` on the resource (which would affect every page)
  or hand-rolling visibility on every individual RM class.
- **An inline-style HTML pill in a Filament getSubheading() must
  pass user-supplied values through `e(...)` to prevent style
  attribute injection.** Even though the status color comes from
  a database column, a malicious admin could (in theory) write
  `red; background-image: url(javascript:...)` into the
  `crm_feature_statuses.color` column and have the inline style
  evaluate the script when rendered. The `e()` escape on the
  interpolated `$bg` and `$statusName` defangs this attack vector
  at the rendering edge. Apply to ANY future "inline style
  attribute interpolating model values" rendering.
- **Filament's `Action::visible(Closure)` accepts a typed-param
  closure that's name-injected with the bound `$record`.** The AC
  literally said `->visible(fn (Feature $r) => $r->is_public)` —
  the `$r` parameter is named-injected with the page's bound record
  thanks to Filament's `evaluate()` machinery. NO need for `?Feature
  $r` nullable typing — the closure only fires when the page has
  a record bound (visibility is re-evaluated per-action-mount, and
  ViewRecord always binds the record before evaluating visibility).
  Same name-injection pattern works for `->url(Closure)` — the
  story's URL closure takes `fn (Feature $r)` and gets the same
  bound record.
- **Two-branch `Route::has() ? route() : '#'` is the right pattern
  for "this URL only works when the host has the matching route
  registered".** Hosts that haven't yet migrated to a core CRM
  version with the named portal route (here:
  `laravel-crm.portal.features.show`) silently get a `#` href
  instead of a `RouteNotFoundException`. Pair with `->visible(...)`
  on a separate boolean (here: `is_public`) so the action is also
  hidden in cases where the URL wouldn't make sense — the
  combination gives "always render correctly even when the host
  is on an older core version OR the record state doesn't qualify
  for the action". Two layers of safety; cheap to apply.
- **Replacing N old tests with M new tests via a single
  `str.replace()` in a Python heredoc** is the right shape when
  the new test set has a different structural shape (different
  number of tests, different test bodies, different reflection
  patterns). Anchor on the FULL CONTIGUOUS BLOCK of old tests
  (3 tests = ~30 lines here) as the search target, paste the
  full new block as the replacement. Single edit; preserves the
  unrelated test sections; survives unrelated indentation drift
  in adjacent tests. Same pattern noted by US-004 of this
  ViewFeature redesign series (the anchor-on-existing-test-body
  shape was first locked in there).
- **The `Filament\Resources\Pages\Concerns\HasRelationManagers`
  trait's `renderingHasRelationManagers()` lifecycle method calls
  `getRelationManagers()` -> `getAllRelationManagers()` ->
  `$this->getResource()::getRelations()`.** Returning `[]` from
  `getAllRelationManagers()` short-circuits the trait's tab
  rendering AND the active-tab session restoration at line 76
  of the trait. The page still has access to all the resource's
  RM classes via `static::$resource::getRelations()` if needed
  programmatically (e.g. for a custom-positioned embed like
  this story's row-3 voters), so returning `[]` from
  `getAllRelationManagers()` doesn't lose anything beyond the
  default tab strip rendering.


## US-001: Move 21 Settings cluster resources to top-level Resources namespace
- Moved all 21 resource directories (84 PHP files) under
  `src/Clusters/Settings/Resources/` to `src/Resources/` via `git mv`:
  AddressTypes, ChatWidgets, ContactTypes, EmailTemplates, FeatureStatuses,
  FieldGroups, Fields, Industries, Labels, LeadSources, LeadStatuses,
  OrganizationTypes, PipelineStageProbabilities, PipelineStages, Pipelines,

### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`)
- **Moved + namespace-rewritten** (via `git mv` then script): 84 PHP
  files across 21 resource directories from `src/Clusters/Settings/

- **Modified**: `src/LaravelCrmPlugin.php` (21 import retargets) +
  7 test files (47 import retargets total + 5 cluster assertion flips).

### Learnings for future iterations
- **Bulk-rename refactors with namespace shifts cascade into THREE
  layers of consumer updates**: (1) the moved files' own internal
  references (handled via a single `str_replace` of the old prefix
  with the new prefix across every PHP file in the moved tree), (2)
  external `use` statements in all consuming PHP files (plugin
  registration + test imports), and (3) test ASSERTIONS that
  reference the removed properties (`getCluster() === Settings::class`).
  Each layer needs its own targeted rewrite script. Layer (3) is the
  one most commonly missed by a naive "string replace" approach
  because the test bodies don't reference the FQCN directly — they
  reference the cluster CONSTANT via the resource's static getter.
  Always grep for the constant name (`Settings::class`) and the
  getter name (`getCluster()`) across `tests/` after a move that
  removes a property.
- **Pint's `ordered_imports` fixer recognizes the new namespace
  positions automatically** after a bulk rename. The plugin's
  `LaravelCrmPlugin.php` had 21 imports under
  `Clusters\Settings\Resources` (alphabetically before `Pages\`
  and `Resources\`); after the move, pint re-sorted them
  interleaved with the existing `Resources\` imports. Pint also
  picked up unrelated `unary_operator_spaces` and
  `not_operator_with_successor_space` fixers on the same file —
  pre-existing inconsistencies that get auto-normalised during
  any pint run on the file. Same pattern noted across many prior
  stories.
- **`git mv $src $dst` preserves history through the rename for `git
  blame`** but git's automatic rename detection in `git status` /
  `git diff` depends on content similarity. After the namespace
  rewrite, some moved files' content similarity drops just below
  git's threshold (~50%) — those show as separate D + A pairs rather
  than R-status renames. The history is still preserved (run `git
  log --follow <file>` on a D+A pair to see) — only the visual
  presentation differs. This is normal and not a regression.
- **The cluster's Pages subtree is OUT of scope for "move resources
  out of cluster" stories.** Per the AC's literal scope statement
  ("relocate every resource currently under
  `src/Clusters/Settings/Resources/`"), the Settings cluster's
  PAGES tree (`Reminders`, `Updates`, etc.) stays put. Pages
  continue to declare `$cluster = Settings::class` and live in the
  Settings cluster namespace. This split makes sense semantically
  — Resources are entity CRUD interfaces (better as top-level
  resources for nav-group composition), while Pages are special-
  purpose admin tools that fit the cluster grouping pattern. When
  scoping a similar move story in the future, always read the AC's
  parenthetical scope statement carefully: "Resources" or "Pages"
  or "both" matters.
- **The pre-existing 32-failure baseline pattern continues to
  hold** across yet another resource-restructure story. The
  failures span `RelationManagersTest` (expecting various Crm* RMs
  to be registered on parent resources' getRelations), portal/Xero
  infolist tests, and Quote/Invoice/Order/PO/Delivery parity tests
  that have been on the baseline since US-001 of the parity series.
  None overlap with the Settings cluster resources moved in US-001,
  and stash-based round-trip verification (when needed) consistently
  confirms the 32 failures are pre-existing. Future stories should
  continue to verify "32/32 baseline preserved" via a quick filter
  on the AC's named gates rather than re-investigating each failure.

  - `src/LaravelCrmPlugin.php` (5 new imports + 5 entries appended to
    `$pages` array + `discoverClusters` block removed; pint

    retarget Updates import, flip cluster assertion).

    import, retarget 2 page imports, flip 2 cluster assertions,
    rewrite the file-path discovery test).
  - `tests/Feature/CalendarTaskKanbanRemindersTest.php` (drop
    Settings import, retarget Reminders import, flip cluster
    assertion).
  - `tests/Feature/SettingsClusterTest.php` (drop Settings import,
    replace obsolete "cluster nav icon" assertion with
    "class no longer exists" regression guard).

### Learnings for future iterations
- **The "32-failure baseline preserved" gate has a subtle false-
  negative mode**: a test that ASSERTS on the soon-to-be-deleted
  class (here `Settings::getNavigationIcon()`) will fail AFTER the
  story applies, even though the underlying class deletion is part
  of the story's contract. The initial pest run showed 33/32+1 vs
  the established baseline — the +1 was the `SettingsClusterTest`
  "declares the Settings cluster nav icon" test, which was genuinely
  broken by the deletion. The fix: replace the obsolete test with a
  positive regression guard that asserts the deletion happened
  (`class_exists(...)===false`). Pattern: when deleting a class that
  was named by an existing test's assertion, ALWAYS grep for the
  class name across `tests/` and rewrite the assertion to expect
  the new state — don't just drop the import and hope for the best.
  Same shape as the v0.x US-006 lead-notes "flip not->toContain to
  toContain" cascade, but applied to a class-existence check.
- **`Panel::discoverClusters()` + `$panel->pages([...])` are mutually
  exclusive registration mechanisms with different access patterns.**
  `discoverClusters()` walks a directory and auto-registers any
  `extends Cluster` class + its child Pages (which carry
  `$cluster = SomeCluster::class`). `$panel->pages([...])` explicitly
  enumerates page classes that get registered at the top level
  (independent of any cluster). When promoting pages out of a
  cluster, you MUST switch registration mechanisms: the discover call
  no longer finds anything (the cluster dir is gone), and the pages
  themselves no longer declare a `$cluster` property. Don't try to
  leave the discover call in place "just in case" — if the directory
  doesn't exist, the call would silently do nothing, but if a future
  story adds a fresh cluster, the discover call would resume working
  and might surface stale page registrations. Cleaner to remove it
  and re-add when needed.
- **View path strings inside Filament Page classes survive a
  namespace move untouched.** Reminders + Updates both declared
  `protected string $view = 'laravel-crm-filament::clusters.settings.pages.{name}'`
  — a string-typed reference to a Blade view at
  `resources/views/clusters/settings/pages/{name}.blade.php`. The
  string has no relationship to the PHP class's namespace; views
  are resolved by the Blade compiler against the package's
  registered views directory + the literal namespace prefix
  (`laravel-crm-filament::`) + the dotted path. So even though the
  PHP class moved from `Clusters\Settings\Pages` to `Pages`, the
  view path didn't need updating. Same goes for any future class
  move that involves string-typed view paths, route names, config
  keys, etc. The AC's scope ("rewrite the namespace, drop the
  cluster import, remove the cluster property") was intentionally
  narrow on this point. Don't reflexively rename Blade views just
  because their containing class moved.
- **Filament v5's `Cluster` discovery uses BOTH the `$cluster`
  property on the page AND the directory layout.** Even if you
  remove the `$cluster` property from a page but leave the page
  file in the cluster directory, `discoverClusters()` will still
  pick it up and try to register it under the cluster — but the
  cluster lookup will fail because the page doesn't claim
  membership. The right cleanup order is:
  1. Add the page to `$panel->pages([...])` (so it's registered
     before discover would have).
  2. Remove the `$cluster` property + drop the
     `use ...Clusters\Settings;` import.
  3. Move the file out of the cluster directory.
  4. Drop the `discoverClusters` call AND delete the cluster
     directory.
  Skipping any step risks an in-between state where the panel
  silently fails to register a page OR registers it twice. This
  story did all four in lockstep via a single commit.

### Learnings for future iterations
- **A bulk-rename refactor's COMMIT can be incomplete even when the
  files appear at the new path.** The prior US-002 commit `dbb6c9f`
  did `git mv` of the 5 files to `src/Pages/` but failed to apply
  the in-file namespace rewrite + cluster property removal. The
  story prompt was re-issued (autopilot saw the work as incomplete)
  AND the actual code state matched the re-issuance — the in-file
  edits were missing despite a commit with the correct message
  having landed. Verify-before-noop discipline noted across many
  prior stories applies HERE too: when a story prompt is re-issued
  and a matching commit exists in git log, CONFIRM the file
  contents actually satisfy the AC before declaring noop. The git
  log message alone is insufficient; read the file.
- **The right response to "story prompt re-issued + work appears
  incomplete in current files" is to complete the missing work
  with a NEW commit using the same AC message.** Don't try to
  amend the prior commit (it's now in the upstream's history).
  Don't write a "fixup" or "[US-002 partial]" message either — the
  AC contract is what matters, and a new commit with the canonical
  message keeps the story discoverable in `git log --oneline`
  searches. This produces TWO commits with the same message, which
  reads cleanly as "first attempt did the file move, second commit
  finished the inner work" — same shape as the v0.x US-006 of the
  prices RM series where the user surfaced a production bug after
  the structural test gates passed, and the fix landed as a
  follow-on commit.
- **Pint's `--dirty --test` mode happily passes a file with an
  unused `use` statement** because the import isn't "wrong" in any
  formatting sense — it's just dead code that PHP's static analyzer
  would flag if enabled. The 2 stale `use Clusters\Settings;`
  imports in the FeatureStatus and UserResourcePromotion test
  files survived the prior US-001 cluster-evacuation cleanup
  silently. Worth proposing as a future hygiene story: run
  `pint --rules=no_unused_imports` across the test suite to surface
  every remaining dead import in one sweep.
- **Pest output in background mode is buffered until process exit
  on some terminals.** Setting `run_in_background: true` on a pest
  invocation that writes to its own stdout file produced a 0-byte
  output file for the entire ~3.5 minute run, with the full output
  appearing in one batch at exit. This is a known characteristic
  of process-spawning interactions: pest's TTY-detection sees no
  terminal and buffers heavily. Workaround: use Monitor with an
  `until` loop that polls a marker (here:
  `grep -qE "Tests:|FAIL|ERROR" $output_file`) so the loop fires
  the moment the output finally arrives. For interactive runs
  during development, the targeted-filter approach (`pest --filter`)
  runs fast enough to show output in <5s and is the right scope
  for confirming a specific gate.


## US-003: Add navigation group and sort properties to all 26 promoted classes
- Wrote a single one-shot PHP script (`/tmp/us003_nav.php`) that walks
  a 26-entry `[relative-path => sort-int]` map and applies two
  transformations per file, idempotently:
  1. **navigationGroup** — replace any existing
     `protected static ... $navigationGroup = ...;` declaration with
     the canonical full-union form
     `protected static string | \UnitEnum | null $navigationGroup =
     'Settings';`. When no declaration exists, insert one immediately
     after the existing `navigationIcon` line (every promoted file has
     one). The regex `/^\s*protected\s+static\s+(?:[^\$;]+)\$navigationGroup\s*=\s*[^;]+;\s*$/m`
     matches ANY existing type signature so a future refactor that
     uses `?string` (or any other variant) gets normalised back to the
     union form automatically.
  2. **navigationSort** — replace any existing
     `protected static ?int $navigationSort = N;` declaration with the
     schema-mandated value. When no declaration exists, insert one
     immediately after the navigationGroup line we just normalised.
- 21 Resources picked up BOTH new properties (none had either before).
  5 Pages had pre-existing `navigationSort` values that got rewritten:
  - GeneralSettings: -10 → 10
  - Integrations: -5 → 20
  - ClickSendIntegration: -4 → 30
  - Reminders: 80 → 240
  - Updates: 100 → 250
- All 5 pages picked up a brand-new navigationGroup line — none of
  them declared one before (they used to be cluster pages that
  inherited their cluster's navigation context).
- Pint auto-fixed the inserted properties' spacing via the
  `class_attributes_separation` fixer — pint inserts a blank line
  between adjacent property declarations as required by PSR-12.
  Several files also picked up unrelated `unary_operator_spaces`,
  `not_operator_with_successor_space`, and `ordered_imports` fixes —
  pre-existing inconsistencies pint normalises whenever it touches a
  file. All 26 files staged with their pint-normalised state.
- **AC's two named gates**:
  - `php -l` on every modified file → "No syntax errors detected" on
    all 26 files. Verified via a loop that catches any failure and
    prints the offending file path + error output.
  - `composer dump-autoload` → completed successfully with no
    class-not-found warnings (the 8-package dependency tree resolved
    cleanly).
- **Additional gates**:
  - `./vendor/bin/pint --dirty --test` → `{"tool":"pint","result":"passed"}`.
  - Targeted pest filter on tests that touch the promoted resources
    or navigation properties

### Learnings for future iterations
- **`protected static ?string $navigationGroup = 'X';` fatal-errors
  at autoload time on every Filament Resource because the parent
  `Filament\Resources\Resource` declares the property with the union
  type `string | UnitEnum | null`.** PHP's strict property type
  matching on overrides forbids the narrower `?string` form. The
  full union form `string | \UnitEnum | null` is required — same
  rule applies to ANY property override that narrows a parent's
  declared type. Same gotcha called out by v0.x US-004 of the parity
  series continuation for UserResource. Lock the contract for every
  resource that participates in nav-group rendering: ALWAYS use the
  union form on property overrides; ALWAYS grep the parent class's
  declaration BEFORE writing an override.
- **A single regex-driven "replace-or-insert" script handles both
  upgrade and fresh-insertion cases idempotently.** The pattern
  shape for "normalise to a canonical form":
  ```php
  // Match ANY existing declaration of the target property.
  $regex = '/^\s*protected\s+static\s+(?:[^\$;]+)\$target\s*=\s*[^;]+;\s*$/m';
  if (preg_match($regex, $src)) {
      // Replace with the canonical form.
      $src = preg_replace($regex, $canonicalLine, $src, 1);
  } else {
      // Insert after a stable anchor (the line that's known to exist
      // in every target file).
      $src = preg_replace($anchorRegex, "$1\n\n" . $canonicalLine, $src, 1);
  }
  ```
  The non-greedy `(?:[^\$;]+)` matches any type signature (`?string`,
  `string`, `string | UnitEnum | null`, `string|null`, etc.) before
  the property name, so the script auto-normalises ANY variant to
  the canonical form. Idempotent on re-runs because the canonical
  form matches the regex AND the replacement produces the same
  string. Apply this pattern to any future "every file in the family
  needs property X with canonical type" story.
- **Pint's `class_attributes_separation` fixer enforces a blank line
  between consecutive property declarations** — but it does NOT
  enforce a blank line between a property and an existing method
  body that follows. So when a script inserts a new property
  immediately above a method, pint won't add a blank line on its
  own. The right pattern: AFTER the bulk insertion, ALWAYS run
  `./vendor/bin/pint --dirty` (without `--test`) so the formatter
  fixes any tightly-packed lines, THEN run `./vendor/bin/pint
  --dirty --test` as the final gate. Two-pass pint is cheaper than
  trying to enumerate every PSR-12 rule in the insertion script.
- **`composer dump-autoload` is the right named gate for "did the
  class signatures land cleanly?"** — it walks every PHP class
  reachable from the autoload manifest and triggers PHP's
  property-type checking on every class load. If any file had a
  property type that violated the parent's declaration, dump-autoload
  would print the offending FQCN + error. A clean exit (no warnings,
  no errors) is strong evidence the union-type contract is satisfied
  across the whole package. Pair with `php -l` per file (catches
  syntax errors that dump-autoload's lazy loading might miss) for
  belt-and-braces coverage.
- **The 5 Pages had pre-existing negative `navigationSort` values
  (-10, -5, -4) intended to position them ABOVE the rest of the
  Settings cluster's nav items.** The new schema uses positive
  values starting at 10 — same relative ordering (GeneralSettings
  first, then Integrations, then ClickSendIntegration) but a clean
  positive-integer schema that interleaves with the 21 promoted
  resources. The 26 sort values land in the range [10, 250] with
  AddressTypeResource at 135 (the only non-multiple-of-10 — the AC
  intentionally wedges it between ContactTypes=130 and
  OrganizationTypes=140). Don't try to "regularise" 135 to 145 or
  similar; the AC's sort schema is the contract.

### Learnings for future iterations
- **A multi-bullet AC can be already mostly-satisfied by prior stories
  in the same series.** US-004's AC named 4 changes, but 3 had already
  landed in US-001 and US-002 of the Settings cluster evacuation series.
  Discipline check at session start: read the file as it stands NOW and
  diff against EACH AC bullet, not against the AC's prose-as-narrative.
  When most-of-it is done, the right response is to surgically add the
  remaining contract AND pile a comprehensive regression-guard test on
  top of all 4 bullets (so a future commit can't accidentally regress
  any of the previously-completed changes). Same shape applies to any
  future story whose work is partially landed across a multi-story
  evacuation/refactor series.
- **`Panel::navigationGroups(array | string $groups): static`** is a
  simple flat-array setter — pass a list of group-name strings to pin
  visible order. Filament's NavigationManager merges the listed groups
  with any others discovered from resources/pages: listed groups render
  in the prescribed order; unlisted groups follow in the order they were
  discovered. AC's "renders other groups after the listed pair via
  default trailing behavior" is the correct expected behavior. No need
  to declare NavigationGroup wrapper objects when only the ordering
  matters.
- **`Panel::getNavigationGroups(): array` is the public read-side**
  for the protected `$navigationGroups` storage. Same shape as the
  many other "set X / get X" pairs across the Panel concerns. Useful
  for structural tests that need to confirm "this exact sequence was
  pinned" without rendering the navigation menu — single getter call,
  positional `array_values()` comparison.
- **Regression-guard tests for "dropped" features** (here:
  `discoverClusters` call, `Clusters\\Settings\\` imports) should be
  written as `expect(...)->not->toContain(...)` source-grep assertions.
  When a future story might inadvertently re-introduce the removed
  feature, this catches it immediately and produces a precise failure
  message. Pair with the positive-presence assertion for the new
  feature (`->toContain("\$panel->navigationGroups(['Contacts',
  'Settings'])")`) so the test file documents both halves of the
  contract: "this stays present" AND "this stays absent".

### Learnings for future iterations
- **The AC's literal prose for "swap X for Y" assumes the original
  state of the file, NOT the current state shaped by prior stories
  in the same series.** US-005's AC says "swap
  `expect($resource::getCluster())->toBe(Settings::class);` for the
  reflection-based form" — but the current file (after US-001 of the
  Settings cluster evacuation series) already had
  `expect($resource::getCluster())->toBeNull();`. The semantically
  correct interpretation: any cluster-membership assertion in the
  file (regardless of which form it takes) should be replaced with
  the AC's reflection-based form. Cross-check the file's current
  state against the AC's prose; if the prose names a form that no
  longer exists, treat the prose as describing the conceptual
  contract (cluster check) and apply the swap to whatever form the
  file currently carries. Same pattern noted by v0.x US-004 of the
  Settings cluster evacuation series where 3 of 4 AC bullets had
  already landed in prior series stories.
- **`ReflectionClass::getStaticPropertyValue('name')` can read
  protected static properties on PHP 8.0+.** Quick verification one-
  liner before committing to the approach:
  ```bash
  php -r "require 'vendor/autoload.php';
  \$ref = new ReflectionClass('FQCN');
  var_dump(\$ref->getStaticPropertyValue('navigationGroup'));"
  ```
  Confirms the reflection bypass works without needing
  `setAccessible(true)` on a `ReflectionProperty`. Same shape works
  for any future "read a parent-class-declared property's value on
  a subclass" assertion. PHP 8.0 removed the
  `ReflectionException: Property is protected` failure mode that
  pre-8.0 versions would throw here.
- **File renames cascade into `file_get_contents()` references in
  other test files.** The AC's "rename" directive named only the
  primary file, but `UserResourcePromotionTest.php` was reading the
  old file's source via `file_get_contents(dirname(__DIR__)
  . '/Feature/SettingsClusterTest.php')` as a regression guard. The
  rename broke that path with `Failed to open stream: No such file
  or directory`. Always grep `tests/` for the OLD filename (here:
  `SettingsClusterTest`) immediately after a rename — there can be
  three classes of consumers:
  1. PHP `use` imports (handled by the rename script if the file
     declares a class — but Pest test files don't declare classes).
  2. Test method bodies that read the file via `file_get_contents`
     or `file_exists` (this story's case).
  3. Test description strings that mention the old filename
     (cosmetic but worth updating for consistency).
  Layer (2) is the one that produces a runtime failure; layers (1)
  and (3) are silent. Pattern: every rename of a test file needs a
  `grep -rn "OldName" tests/` pass before declaring done.
- **The "32-failure pre-existing baseline preserved" gate has a
  subtle false-negative mode that's already been documented in
  prior progress entries (US-002 re-run): a test that ASSERTS on
  a soon-to-be-renamed file path will fail AFTER the rename even
  though the path change is part of the story's contract.** This
  story hit the exact same shape on the first pest run (33 failed
  / 1427 passed instead of the expected 32 / 1428). The recurring
  fix pattern: grep for the OLD file path in `tests/` BEFORE the
  rename, prepare a parallel patch for any consumer test files,
  apply both edits in lockstep, then re-run the full suite to
  confirm the baseline is restored. Save 1 pest cycle (~4 minutes
  per cycle on this codebase).

- **Modified** `tests/Feature/NavigationGroupOrderTest.php` (drop the
  `not->toContain('Clusters\\Settings\\')` regression guard test)

### Learnings for future iterations
- **A cluster-evacuation series with an explicit "no remaining
  cluster references" AC needs to drop regression guards alongside
  active uses.** The intuition is to "keep regression guards that
  assert absence" but the AC's literal contract ("No file in `tests/`
  references X, Y, or Z anymore") doesn't distinguish active use
  from regression-guard reference. The right pragmatic interpretation:
  drop ALL references (including regression guards) and rely on
  `composer dump-autoload` + pint as the post-deletion safety net.
  Same precedent locked in by US-005 of the Settings cluster
  evacuation series ("Dropped the 'Settings cluster class no longer
  exists' regression guard"). When a future story has the same
  AC shape, cascade the cleanup across ALL cluster-referencing files
  in one pass rather than leaving regression guards behind.
- **AC's "intact" instruction is narrowly scoped.** US-006's AC says
  "Leave the existing 'lives under the top-level Resources\\Teams
  namespace' assertions for CrmTeamResource intact — those are
  already top-level." This refers SPECIFICALLY to the
  `toStartWith('VentureDrake\\LaravelCrmFilament\\Resources\\Teams\\')`
  assertion — NOT to the companion `class_exists('...Clusters\\Settings\\...')->toBeFalse()`
  regression guard inside the same test block. Read AC's "intact"
  literally: the named assertion stays; everything else around it
  is in-scope for cleanup. When the AC names a specific assertion,
  treat it as scoped to that one literal — not as "preserve the
  entire surrounding test block".
- **Pest top-level helper functions and dataset names referenced
  across multiple test files survive a related test's cleanup
  cleanly.** UserResourcePromotionTest still reads
  `SettingsNavGroupTest.php`'s source via `file_get_contents()` to
  assert UserResource is NOT in the `settingsNavGroupResources`
  dataset. This regression guard is fine — it doesn't reference the
  deleted Cluster, it references the canonical test file's source.
  Always check sibling tests for cross-file source-grep references
  AFTER a rename or content change in a primary test, not before.
- **A `null` warning from `shell_exec` + `trim` in a Bash heredoc
  verification step is harmless but noisy.** `shell_exec` returns
  null when the command exits with a non-empty exit code AND has no
  output (the "no matches found" case for grep). PHP's `trim(null)`
  triggers a deprecation warning in PHP 8.1+ but doesn't break the
  script. Suppress with `(string) shell_exec(...)` if you want a
  clean verification log — or just `if ($out === null || trim($out)
  === '')` for the same intent. Cosmetic; the verification still
  works correctly.

reading `$navigationGroup`, `$navigationSort`, `$slug`, and `$cluster`

### What still needs the literal browser click-through
The autopilot has proven every wiring contract via source-grep,
property-reflection audit, and pest's structural + integration test
coverage. What the user still needs to confirm in a real browser at
`/Users/andrewdrake/Sites/laravel-13-crm-v2`:

  (each entry's sort value is correct; the rendering layer's behavior
  with duplicate values would matter — but the AC's schema has no
  duplicates, so this is theoretical).

  Blade view AND mounts the Livewire component without runtime
  errors. Structural tests verify the class structure but not the

manual walkthrough at the host caught a real production bug
(`->defaultSort('default', 'desc')` against a non-existent column
in production schema) that the structural tests couldn't surface

walkthrough step even when the structural tests are green** —
some bugs only surface against the real production schema or the
real browser rendering layer.

### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/.polyscope/clones/66571e70/humble-koi`)
- **Modified** `.context/progress.md` (this entry only — verification
  story carries no code change in either repo)

### Learnings for future iterations
- **A clean "all-green at all gates" verification story is still
  worth doing comprehensively**, not just `git log`-and-noop. The
  audit script's per-entry sort + nav-group + slug + cluster check
  is a structural integrity check that catches any drift since the
  AC's named schema was locked in. Re-runs in 100ms; surfaces issues
  immediately. Pattern: any "verify the X is in place" story should
  produce a deterministic audit script as a side-effect, even when
  the result is "all green". The script lives at `/tmp/` and can
  be re-run by future stories that want to confirm the same contract
  still holds (e.g. after a refactor that re-touches any of the 26
  files).
- **Structural-proxy mapping per AC bullet is the right shape for
  manual-verification stories.** When the AC has N walkthrough
  bullets, the progress entry should enumerate each bullet AND
  name the structural test (or audit) that covers it AND state
  which test name to grep if the wiring ever regresses. This makes
  the verification story's value persistent: a future incident
  ("the Settings nav-group order regressed!") can grep the progress
  log for "NavigationGroupOrderTest" and immediately find the
  authoritative test name. Don't just say "wiring confirmed";
  name the tests by hand for the index they create.
- **The "32-failure pre-existing baseline preserved" gate has now
  been re-confirmed across 35+ consecutive stories with byte-exact
  count parity.** This is a strong signal that the codebase's
  failure pattern is genuinely stable. Future stories should
  CONTINUE to verify the baseline (cheap insurance) but can
  confidently expect 32/7 at every full-suite run. Any deviation
  is a regression to investigate, not a baseline shift.
- **Browser-bound manual walkthrough remains the LAST QA layer.**
  This is the third manual-verification story in the autopilot
  flow (v0.x US-007 of the recalc series, v0.x US-006 of the
  prices RM series, now US-007 of the Settings cluster evacuation
  series). Each one has had a slightly different posture:
  - v0.x US-007 (recalc): pure handoff, no proxy gates needed,
    the recalc body was already structurally trivial.
  - v0.x US-006 (prices RM): proxy gates passed, but the user's
    walkthrough caught a real production bug (default-sort column
    that didn't exist in production schema).
  - US-007 (Settings nav-group): proxy gates pass, audit script
    confirms wiring, handoff is comprehensive.
  Pattern: ALWAYS run the proxy gates (pint + targeted pest + full
  pest), ALWAYS write a comprehensive audit script when the AC
  names a numeric schema, ALWAYS map each AC bullet to its
  structural coverage, AND clearly state what the user still needs
  to literally click. The user's walkthrough then has a tight
  scope (5 specific things to verify) rather than an open-ended
  "go check everything" task.

### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`)
- **Modified** `src/Pages/GeneralSettings.php` (rewrite KEYS map +
  form() schema + helper option methods; lifecycle preserved)
- **Modified** `resources/lang/en/labels.php` (+3 keys:
  `sections.localisation`, `sections.document_defaults`,
  `sections.behaviour`)
- **Modified** `resources/lang/fr/labels.php` (same 3 keys)
- **Modified** `resources/lang/es/labels.php` (same 3 keys)
- **Added** `tests/Feature/GeneralSettingsKeysAndSectionsTest.php`

### Learnings for future iterations
- **AC math inconsistency between story heading and explicit
  enumeration is a recurring footgun.** US-001's heading says "9
  → 25 entries" but the comma list enumerates 26 keys grouped
  into 6 sections that sum to 3+6+7+6+2+2=26. Same pattern noted
  in v0.x US-005 of the lead-notes UI series (label count
  discrepancy in the AC prose). When the AC's count and explicit
  enumeration diverge, the explicit enumeration is authoritative —
  deliver every named key AND document the typo in the progress
  entry so future stories don't try to "fix" the count by dropping
  an arbitrary key.
- **Filament v5's `Filament\Schemas\Components\Section` class does
  NOT expose a public `getName()` getter.** Section::make's first
  positional arg becomes the section identifier internally but is
  not introspectable via a public getter. Calling
  `$section->getName()` throws `BadMethodCallException: Method
  Filament\Schemas\Components\Section::getName does not exist.`
  from `vendor/filament/support/src/Concerns/Macroable.php`.
  Workarounds for "assert section ordering" tests:
  - **Source-grep with cursor walk** (what this story used): walk
    the literal `Section::make('X')` strings via `strpos($src,
    $needle, $cursor)` advancing the cursor by `strlen($needle)`.
    Catches both "section missing" AND "section out of order" with
    a single assertion per needle. Reusable template for any future
    "assert ordered structural elements in source" check.
  - Reflection on the protected `$name`/`$id` property — works but
    fragile across Filament version bumps.
  - `getHeading()` — returns the rendered heading string (typically
    the localized text), not the section identifier. Useful when the
    headings themselves are the contract but not for identifier-based
    ordering.
  Same gotcha as the `TextColumn::getStateUsing()` pattern noted
  across multiple prior stories — the public-getter vs setter
  asymmetry recurs across Filament's fluent API.
- **`function_exists(...)` guards around namespaced helper-function
  calls are the right defensive pattern when the helper file is
  loaded via Composer's `files` autoload.** The
  `vendor/venturedrake/laravel-crm/src/Http/Helpers/SelectOptions.php`
  file declares free-floating functions in the
  `VentureDrake\LaravelCrm\Http\Helpers\SelectOptions` namespace.
  Composer's `files` autoload registers them at app boot — but if a
  consumer panel mounts before that boot step (uncommon but
  possible), the function calls would fatal. Wrapping each helper
  call with `if (function_exists('VentureDrake\\LaravelCrm\\Http\\Helpers\\SelectOptions\\countries')) { ... }`
  gracefully degrades to an empty options array instead of crashing
  the page. Cheap insurance; applies to any future helper sourced
  from a vendored Composer package.
- **AC's "Source Select options for X from
  vendor/venturedrake/laravel-crm/src/Http/Helpers/SelectOptions/*.php"
  wildcard path is misleading.** The actual file is a single
  `SelectOptions.php` (no directory). The intent is clearly "use the
  helper functions declared in that file" — read past the
  pseudo-glob syntax to the underlying intent. Always grep the
  vendor directory for the literal file path before assuming an
  AC's pattern matches.


## US-002: Add nested phones/emails/addresses Repeaters to GeneralSettings (GeneralSettings scalar parity series)
- Rewrote `src/Pages/GeneralSettings.php` to grow 3 new Sections (phones,
  emails, addresses) each wrapping a `Filament\Forms\Components\Repeater`,
  bringing the page from 6 top-level Sections (post-US-001) to 9. Each
  Repeater binds polymorphic morphMany rows on the
  `Setting{name='team'}` anchor — same shape as core CRM's Livewire
  `SettingEdit::save()` reference.
- **Migration cross-check (per the Codebase Patterns warning) revealed
  the AC's "type_id (Select from PhoneType/EmailType)" naming is
  unfulfillable**:
  - `crm_phones`: `type` is an ENUM string (work/home/mobile/fax/other),
    NOT `type_id`. NO PhoneType model ships in core CRM.
  - `crm_emails`: `type` is an ENUM string (work/home/other), NOT
    `type_id`. NO EmailType model.
  - `crm_addresses`: `address_type_id` IS a real FK to
    `crm_address_types`, AND AddressType model exists.
  Pragmatic resolution: use the actual schema. Phones/Emails Select
  binds to the enum options (sourced via `SelectOptions\phoneTypes()` /
  `\emailTypes()` helpers with a hardcoded fallback for hosts without
  the helpers autoloaded); Addresses Select binds to
  `AddressType::query()->orderBy('name')->pluck('name','id')`.
- **Repeater shapes per AC**:
  - phones: `Hidden id` + `Select type` + `TextInput number` (required,
    tel, max 50)
  - emails: `Hidden id` + `Select type` + `TextInput address` (required,
    email, max 255)
  - addresses: `Hidden id` + `Select address_type_id` + 7 TextInputs for
    line1/line2/line3/city/state/code/country. NB: AC names "suburb"
    and "postcode" but the schema uses `city` and `code` (cross-checked
    against `vendor/.../database/migrations/create_laravel_crm_tables.php.stub`
    lines 102-125); used the actual column names.
- **Lifecycle** (mirrors core's SettingEdit reference):
  - `mount()` calls `resolveAnchor()` which does
    `Setting::firstOrCreate(['name' => 'team'], ['value' => 'related'])`
    + `->load(['phones', 'emails', 'addresses'])` — single eager-load
    batch. The firstOrCreate guard is necessary because core's Settings
    middleware seeds this row on every request, but the Filament page
    may be exercised before that middleware runs (e.g. in tests).
  - `mount()` then maps each morphMany collection to the flat
    `[id, type, number/address/...]` row shape the Repeater expects
    and merges into `$this->data` before `form->fill($this->data)`.
  - `save()` extends the existing scalar-key loop with three new diff
    helpers — `syncPhones(Setting $anchor, array $rows)`,
    `syncEmails(...)`, `syncAddresses(...)`. Each helper:
    1. Iterates submitted rows; if `id` is set AND the row exists,
       `update($attrs)`; else if the row has meaningful content
       (e.g. number for phones, address for emails, any non-null
       address column for addresses), creates a new row via
       `$anchor->{relation}()->create([...]; ['external_id' =>
       Uuid::uuid4()->toString()])`.
    2. Collects kept ids; deletes any pre-existing row whose id
       isn't in the kept set.
  - Single success Notification fires after the diff.
- **Test updates**:
  - `GeneralSettingsKeysAndSectionsTest::it('renders 6 top-level
    Sections ...')` → bumped to "renders 9 top-level Sections including
    the phones/emails/addresses repeaters" with the cursor-walk
    extended to assert the 3 new section names in order. Used the
    Python-style heredoc + `str_replace`-with-old-block-anchor
    pattern for surgical replacement.
  - New `tests/Feature/GeneralSettingsRepeatersTest.php` (+8 tests /
    27 assertions; full plugin suite now **1460 passed / 32 failed /
    7 skipped (4807 assertions)** — net +8 passing tests matching
    the new file's 8 cases. Zero net new failures vs the post-US-001
    baseline of 1452/32/7). Tests cover:
    - 3 Repeaters declared in source (`Repeater::make('phones')`
      etc.).
    - Phones repeater block contains Hidden id + Select type +
      TextInput number + `phoneTypeOptions()` source reference
      (block extracted via `strpos` start/end anchors so the
      assertion is scoped to the right Repeater).
    - Same shape for emails (Hidden id + Select type +
      TextInput address + `emailTypeOptions()`).
    - Addresses block: Hidden id + Select address_type_id +
      `AddressType::query()` source reference + 7 TextInputs
      (line1/line2/line3/city/state/code/country).
    - mount() end-to-end: seeds a Setting{name='team'} anchor +
      one phone + one email + one address, invokes the data-loading
      half of mount() via Reflection on the protected
      `resolveAnchor()` method, asserts the loaded collections
      come back with the right shape.
    - save() diff end-to-end: seeds 2 phones on the anchor, calls
      `syncPhones` via Reflection with [keep+update, new], asserts
      the kept row was updated, a new row was inserted, AND the
      dropped row was deleted from the DB.

- **Modified** `src/Pages/GeneralSettings.php` (+17 imports,

### Learnings for future iterations
- **The "Codebase Patterns" warning about TestSchema.php divergence
  from production migrations now applies BOTH WAYS: an AC can name
  columns/models that ALSO don't exist in production.** US-002's AC
  literally said "type_id (Select from PhoneType)" and "type_id
  (Select from EmailType)" — neither model ships in core CRM, and
  the actual column is the `type` enum string. The right read of
  the AC's own "Verify exact column names against
  vendor/.../create_laravel_crm_{phones,emails,addresses}_table.php.stub
  before assuming any field names (per the Codebase Patterns warning)"
  is to PREFER the migration-verified shape over the AC's prose names.
  Same shape applies to the AC's "suburb" / "postcode" naming for
  addresses — actual columns are `city` and `code`. When the AC's
  prose disagrees with the migration, the migration wins; document
  the divergence in the progress entry.
- **Filament v5 Repeater's diff-and-persist with a hidden `id`
  field is the cleanest shape for "Livewire-backed singleton page
  edits a polymorphic collection".** Each row carries a
  `Hidden::make('id')` field that's null for new rows AND set to
  the database row id for existing rows. The `save()` diff
  partitions submitted rows into update/create branches based on
  the presence of `id`, then deletes any pre-existing row whose
  id wasn't kept. Pattern reusable for any future "page edits a
  polymorphic morphMany without an Eloquent record" scenario
  (single-record edit pages like GeneralSettings, profile pages,
  etc.).
- **`Setting::firstOrCreate(['name' => 'team'], ['value' =>
  'related'])` in the page's `resolveAnchor()` method is the right
  defensive pattern.** Core CRM's `Http\Middleware\Settings.php`
  seeds this row on every request via the same firstOrCreate call,
  but in test environments (and any edge case where the middleware
  hasn't run) the page would otherwise see a null anchor and
  crash. Mirroring the same firstOrCreate in the page itself makes
  the page self-sufficient. Apply this whenever a Filament page
  reads a singleton record that's normally seeded elsewhere.
- **A "block-scoped source-grep" via `strpos` start/end anchors**
  is the right pattern for asserting "field X is present inside
  the Repeater for Y" when multiple Repeaters in the same source
  share field names. The Hidden id appears 3 times (one per
  Repeater); the Select type appears 2 times (phones + emails) —
  a bare `toContain("Hidden::make('id')")` wouldn't distinguish
  which Repeater. Extract the block via `$start = strpos($src,
  "Repeater::make('phones')"); $end = strpos($src,
  "Section::make('emails')", $start); $block = substr($src,
  $start, $end - $start);` then assert against the substring.
  Same pattern as v0.x US-004 ViewFeature redesign series
  (Details section closure body extraction).
- **`Setting::create(['name' => 'team', 'value' => 'related'])`
  in a test seeds the anchor cleanly because the test schema's
  `crm_settings` table allows `name` to be non-unique** (no
  unique index on the `name` column in the test schema). Multiple
  Setting rows with name='team' could exist; the production
  firstOrCreate pattern just returns the first match. Worth
  flagging — if a future hygiene story adds a unique index on
  `name`, the page's firstOrCreate would still work but tests
  that create multiple anchors would error. For now, single-anchor
  tests are the right shape.


## US-003: Add GeneralSettings parity test (GeneralSettings scalar parity series)
- New `tests/Feature/GeneralSettingsPageParityTest.php` (+5 tests / 112
  assertions; full plugin suite now **1465 passed / 32 failed / 7 skipped
  (4919 assertions)**, up from 1460/32/7 at the post-US-002 baseline of
  this series — exactly +5 passing tests matching the new file, +112
  assertions, zero new failures). The 32 failures are the IDENTICAL
  pre-existing baseline noted across the prior 38+ stories
  (Quote/Invoice/Order/PurchaseOrder/Delivery parity tests +
  Audits/Portal/Pipeline tests + RelationManagersTest expecting various
  Crm* RMs to be registered).
- Consolidates the GeneralSettings expansion contract into a single
  regression-gate file. Three AC contracts covered:
  - **(a) Reflection-based KEYS map assertion** — asserts
    `array_keys(GeneralSettings::KEYS)` equals the explicit 26-element
    list in expected order (`organization_name` → `dynamic_products`)
    AND `count() === 26`. Companion test loops every KEYS entry and
    asserts the label is a non-empty string (required because
    `SettingService::set($key, $value, $label)` uses the label for the
    "friendly name" column).
  - **(b) Schema introspection of section ordering** — single test mounts
    the page via `(new ReflectionClass(GeneralSettings::class))->newInstanceWithoutConstructor()`,
    builds a `Schema::make($page)`, invokes `$page->form($schema)`, and
    filters to top-level Section components. Asserts `count(>= 6)` AND
    `array_slice($sections, 0, 6)` mapped through `getHeading()` equals
    the 6 AC-named section translation strings in order
    (branding/localisation/prefixes/document_defaults/tax/behaviour).
    The 3 additional repeater Sections (phones/emails/addresses) are
    intentionally allowed to follow — the AC's "6 section headings" is
    the scalar-only surface. Companion source-grep test cursor-walks the
    literal `Section::make('X')` identifiers + the
    `->heading(__('...sections.X'))` chain for each of the 6 scalar
    sections (Filament v5's Section class has no public `getName()`
    accessor, so the identifier check needs source-grep).
  - **(c) Round-trip test** — uses the hot-patch anonymous-subclass
    pattern (established across many prior stories incl.
    ClickSendIntegrationPageTest, LeadNotesRelationManagerTest) to
    bypass `$this->form->getState()` (which requires a real Livewire
    mount). The subclass's `save()` body reads `$this->data` directly,
    iterates `static::KEYS` writing every scalar via
    `$settings->set($key, $value, $label)`, then calls the existing
    `resolveAnchor()` + `syncPhones()` + `syncEmails()` +
    `syncAddresses()` helpers. The test seeds:
    - A fresh `AddressType` via `AddressType::create(['name' =>
      'Headquarters'])` (the address row needs this FK).
    - A full scalar payload (all 26 KEYS entries with sensible values
      mirroring real-host settings — VAT prefix strings, organisation
      name, 6 Document-defaults bodies, 6 localisation Select values,
      etc.).
    - One phone row (`type=work`, `number='+1-555-9000'`).
    - One email row (`type=work`, `address='team@acme.test'`).
    - One address row (`address_type_id=$type->id`,
      `line1='1 Wharf St'`, `city='New York'`, etc.).
    After `$page->save()`, asserts:
    - Every scalar key is retrievable via
      `app('laravel-crm.settings')->get($key)` AND the value matches
      the seeded data (with bool→string normalisation for the two
      Toggle keys).
    - The `Setting{name='team'}` anchor exists after the call.
    - The phone row landed on `crm_phones` with `phoneable_type ===
      $anchor->getMorphClass()` AND `phoneable_id === $anchor->id`.
    - Same shape for the email row (`emailable_type/_id`) and the
      address row (`addressable_type/_id` AND the `address_type_id`
      FK preserved).
- Quality gates green:
  - `./vendor/bin/pint --dirty --test` reports `passed` (after
    auto-fix of `class_definition`, `braces_position`, and
    `self_static_accessor` on the new file).
  - Targeted filter `--filter='GeneralSettingsPageParityTest'` → 5
    passed (112 assertions) in 1.12s.
  - Targeted filter `--filter='GeneralSettings|Localization'` → 46
    passed (248 assertions) in 2.33s.

    (4919 assertions) in 219.72s.

### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`)
- **Added** `tests/Feature/GeneralSettingsPageParityTest.php`

### Learnings for future iterations
- **The AC math discrepancy (25 vs 26 keys) recurs and is documented
  cleanly across multiple progress entries now.** US-003's AC says
  "exactly 25 entries" but the implementation has 26 keys (locked-in
  by US-001 of this series, also documented in US-002). The test
  asserts the actual 26-key contract because:
  1. Asserting "exactly 25" would fail against the implementation.
  2. The existing `GeneralSettingsKeysAndSectionsTest` from US-001
     already locks the 26-key shape — divergent assertions across
     test files would be a maintenance footgun.
  3. The progress notes for US-001 explicitly acknowledge the typo
     and treat the explicit enumeration as authoritative.
  Pattern: when the AC's count doesn't match the explicit
  enumeration AND the implementation, treat the explicit enumeration
  as authoritative and document the divergence in the progress entry.
  Same pattern noted by v0.x US-005 of the lead-notes UI series
  (label count discrepancy in the AC prose).
- **The AC's "6 section headings render in order" is the SCALAR
  surface, not the total Section count.** The page has 9 top-level
  Sections (6 scalar + 3 contact-detail repeaters), but the AC's
  parity claim is specifically about the scalar grouping established
  by US-001. The right interpretation: assert the first 6 Sections
  in their AC-named order via `array_slice($sections, 0, 6)`. Allow
  any additional Sections to follow without constraining the test
  to "exactly 6 sections" (which would conflict with the
  GeneralSettingsKeysAndSectionsTest from US-001 that asserts 9).
  Two complementary tests cover two complementary contracts:
  GeneralSettingsKeysAndSectionsTest locks "9 total sections in
  this order"; GeneralSettingsPageParityTest locks "first 6
  sections are the scalar group in this order". Different scoping,
  same shape, no conflict.
- **`Section::getHeading()` returns the RESOLVED translation string,
  NOT the translation key.** When the AC says "Section headings
  via the labels namespace", the test can pair (a) `getHeading()`
  matching `__('...labels.sections.X')` (locks the rendered visible
  text matches the i18n resolution) with (b) source-grep for
  `->heading(__('...labels.sections.X'))` (locks that the source
  actually uses the i18n key rather than a hardcoded string).
  Two-sided coverage. Same pattern noted by US-005 of the product
  list series for `TextColumn::getPlaceholder()`.
- **`SettingService::set($key, $value, $label)` writes the value via
  `Setting::updateOrCreate(['name' => $key], ['value' => $value,
  'label' => $label])`** — so boolean `true` round-trips through the
  `value` string column as `'1'` (PHP's default scalar coercion for
  bool→string). The retrieval via `SettingService::get($key)`
  returns the literal string. Tests need to normalise both sides:
  `is_bool($expected) ? ($expected ? '1' : '0') : (string) $expected`
  is the right pattern. Worth noting for any future "round-trip
  test for a settings page with boolean Toggle fields" story.
- **The hot-patch anonymous-subclass pattern for bypassing
  `$this->form->getState()` is the established way to exercise a
  Filament page's `save()` body without a real Livewire mount.**
  Locked-in across many prior stories (ClickSendIntegrationPageTest,
  LeadNotesRelationManagerTest, LeadTasksRelationManagerTest, etc.).
  The subclass overrides `save()` to read `$this->data` directly,
  then calls all the other private/protected helpers via inheritance
  — no Reflection needed for the helpers. The cost is reimplementing
  the save body shape in the test; the benefit is fast, deterministic
  tests that don't require a panel mount + auth + Livewire request
  pipeline. Pair with source-grep assertions against the REAL `save()`
  body to confirm the production code path matches the test
  subclass's shape (the existing `GeneralSettingsKeysAndSectionsTest`
  already does this for the `$settings->set(...)` + Notification
  call sites — no need to duplicate here).

### Learnings for future iterations
- **`RelationManager::getTitle(Model, string): string` is a STATIC
  method on Filament v5's RelationManager base class.** Overriding
  it as a regular (non-static) instance method triggers a hard
  `Fatal error: Cannot make static method
  Filament\Resources\RelationManagers\RelationManager::getTitle()
  non static in class X`. This kills pest with exit 2 + ZERO
  visible output (the harness silently swallows the fatal error
  unless you re-run with `php -d display_errors=stderr -d
  log_errors=on` and capture stderr separately to a file). Cross-
  reference: every other RM in this codebase that overrides
  `getTitle()` (AuditsRelationManager, CrmActivitiesRelationManager)
  uses `public static function getTitle(Model $ownerRecord, string
  $pageClass): string` — same shape. ALWAYS grep an existing
  sibling RM for the `getTitle` signature before declaring an
  override, AND when pest exits with code 2 + no output, the FIRST
  diagnostic step is the stderr-redirect rerun. Saves at least one
  full debug cycle.
- **The "pest exit 2 + no output" diagnostic shape is now a
  documented recurring pattern** (this story + US-004 of the
  parity series continuation noting UnitEnum union types).
  Always re-run as `php -d display_errors=stderr -d log_errors=on
  ./vendor/bin/pest ... 2>/tmp/err.log >/tmp/out.log` to surface
  the PHP fatal that the test harness silently swallows. Look for
  Fatal errors involving inheritance constraints (non-covariant
  property types, static-vs-instance method overrides) — these are
  the most common shapes that pass syntax checks but blow up at
  autoload time.
- **The labels-insertion + test schema-patching scripts continue to
  work verbatim across stories.** The recurring two-script
  pattern (labels.php anchor-based insert + supplementary migration
  `Schema::table` with `Schema::hasColumn` guards) has now been
  applied in 22+ consecutive stories. Worth elevating to a
  standalone Codebase Patterns entry when the count crosses some
  threshold — the templates themselves are stable enough that a
  future story can copy-paste the heredoc body and just swap the
  per-story values (anchor key, new key/value triple, namespace
  name, target columns).

### Learnings for future iterations
- **Anonymous-class Livewire components implementing `HasTable` are
  too noisy to set up in tests.** Filament's HasTable contract has
  multiple abstract methods (including
  `makeFilamentTranslatableContentDriver`), and an anonymous class
  needs to implement every one of them — or fatal with
  "contains 1 abstract method and must therefore be declared
  abstract or implement the remaining methods". The reliable pattern
  is `livewire(ListXxx::class)->instance()->getTable()` — the
  ListRecords page already implements HasTable correctly. Pair with
  the standard `RoleSeeder::seed()` + `actingAs($user)` beforeEach
  scaffold so the table render passes the policy gate. Locked in by
  PersonListColumnsTest / OrganizationListColumnsTest /
  ProductListColumnsTest of the parity series continuation.
- **RoleSeeder's `ENTITIES` array is the authoritative seed list
  for `{create,view,edit,delete} crm {entity}` permissions across
  the whole test suite.** Any policy gate that reads a permission
  string not in the ENTITIES list (e.g. `view crm tax rates`,
  `view crm roles`) will throw `PermissionDoesNotExist` from a
  Livewire-mounted test page. Always grep
  `vendor/.../laravel-crm/src/Policies/*Policy.php` for the
  `hasPermissionTo('foo')` string a new test will exercise, and
  cross-check against the ENTITIES list. Add to the list if missing
  — same pattern as v0.x US-007 of the parity series continuation
  for `'teams'`.
- **`TernaryFilter::make('column_name')`** without further
  customisation produces an "All / Yes / No" three-state filter
  that queries `WHERE column_name = true|false|<unfiltered>`. The
  column name must match the actual DB column — `crm_role` maps
  cleanly to the boolean column added by core's
  `add_fields_to_roles_permissions_tables.php.stub` migration. No
  need for an explicit `query()` closure; Filament's default
  behaviour handles boolean columns automatically.
- **A 4-step rename/edit script with anchor-based `str_replace`** is
  the established pattern for "make N targeted code changes to
  multiple files in a single shot from outside the clone". The
  script uses `str_contains($src, $needle)` for idempotency
  (re-running is a no-op) and `exit(1)` for missing anchors (fails
  loudly when the source has drifted). Reusable verbatim across
  any future story whose code changes are small + targeted +
  anchor-able.

- **AC baseline numeric predictions can lag the actual baseline by
  several stories.** US-007's AC names "1426 passed" but the actual
  baseline at session start was 1481 — the cumulative work from
  US-001 through US-006 added +55 tests that the AC writer didn't
  account for. This is the third occurrence of "AC's stated baseline
  is stale" in the conversation flow (also noted by v0.x US-006 of
  the prices RM series and US-007 of the Settings cluster evacuation
  series). The right read of any "baseline preserved" AC contract:
  treat the FAILURE COUNT (and SKIPPED COUNT) as the authoritative
  byte-identical part of the contract, and treat the PASSING COUNT
  as a floor (must be ≥ predicted; exceeding is fine and expected
  when prior stories in the same series have added tests). Always
  diff against the most recent recorded baseline in the progress
  log, not against the AC's prose.
- **Verification stories are the right place to recap a multi-story
  series.** US-007 wraps a 6-story Settings parity sweep — the
  progress entry's recap section (US-001 → US-006 implementation
  contracts) becomes a quick-reference index for future stories
  that need to reference what landed in this sweep. Without this
  recap, finding "which story added the singleton-page-Repeater
  pattern" would require reading 6 separate entries. Future
  multi-story-series verification stories should consider adding
  the same recap shape — cheap to write, valuable for context
  recovery later.
- **The singleton-page-Repeater pattern is the headline new pattern
  from this sweep.** Worth elevating to the top-level Codebase
  Patterns section in a future hygiene story. The pattern is
  distinct from:
  - RelationManager (always has a bound parent Eloquent record).
  - Form Repeater inside a resource's Create/Edit page (has a
    record-to-be-created or existing record bound).
  - LiveQuoteItems-style repeater (Livewire 3 component without
    Filament).
  The new pattern: a Filament Page with `public array $data = []`,
  a singleton anchor resolved via `firstOrCreate(...)`, eager-loads
  morphMany collections into `$this->data` for Repeater binding,
  and persists via per-relation diff helpers driven by Hidden-id
  row identity. Reusable for any "singleton page edits a polymorphic
  collection" UI.

  been re-confirmed across 41+ consecutive stories with byte-exact
  parity.** Pattern is extremely stable. Any future deviation from
  32/7 is a regression to investigate, not a baseline shift.

### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`)
- **Added** `src/Pages/ActivityFeed.php`
- **Modified** `src/LaravelCrmPlugin.php` (+1 import + 1 entry in
  the `$pages` array before CalendarPage)
- **Added** `tests/Feature/ActivityFeedPageSkeletonTest.php`

### Learnings for future iterations
- **`LaravelCrmPlugin::get()` requires the plugin to be attached to
  the CURRENT panel via `$panel->plugin($plugin)`, NOT just
  `$plugin->register($panel)`.** The static `get()` calls
  `filament(app(static::class)->getId())` which reads
  `$panel->getPlugin($id)` from the current panel's plugin registry.
  A bare `->register($panel)` populates resources/pages/widgets but
  does NOT add the plugin instance to the panel's `$plugins` map —
  that's done by the separate `$panel->plugin($plugin)` call
  (Filament v5's `Panel::plugin()` at `HasPlugins.php:15`). For any
  test that calls `LaravelCrmPlugin::get()` (directly or indirectly
  via `getNavigationGroup()` etc.), the setup shape must be:
  ```php
  $panel = Panel::make()->id('my-panel')->default();
  $plugin = LaravelCrmPlugin::make();
  $panel->plugin($plugin);       // register in panel's plugin map
  $plugin->register($panel);     // populate resources/pages/widgets
  Filament::setCurrentPanel($panel);
  ```
  Without the `$panel->plugin($plugin)` line, the test fails with
  `LogicException: Plugin [laravel-crm] is not registered for panel
  [my-panel]`. Same shape gotcha called out in v0.x US-011 progress
  ("LaravelCrmPlugin::get() is fragile in tests"). The v0.x note
  suggested "make module-gating helpers fall back to the panel's
  getResources() list" — for a fresh page in the activity feed
  series, the workaround is simpler: just attach the plugin in the
  test scaffold.
- **`ReflectionProperty::getDefaultValue(): mixed`** (PHP 8.0+) is
  the right way to read a class property's declared default without
  instantiating the class. Returns the literal declared default
  (`'heroicon-o-bolt'` here, or `null` for `?string $x = null` shape).
  Works for public/protected/private uniformly. Same shape used
  across many prior progress entries for reflection-based structural
  tests.
- **`Filament\Pages\Page`'s `$title` and `$navigationIcon`
  properties are BOTH `protected static`** (declared on the parent
  `Filament\Support\Concerns\HasNavigationLabel` +
  `HasNavigationIcon` traits). Reading them via
  `new ReflectionProperty(ChildClass::class, 'name')` works
  because ReflectionProperty crawls the inheritance chain to
  find the property. The child class's declared default overrides
  the parent's default via PHP's static property initialization
  order — same pattern as US-006 of the Settings cluster
  evacuation series noted for `$navigationGroup` overrides.
- **The `Livewire\Attributes\Url` attribute** on a public property
  makes it query-string-syncable across page navigations and
  refreshes. Filament's Page class inherits Livewire component
  behavior, so any public property annotated with `#[Url]` is
  automatically wired to Livewire's URL binding mechanism.
  `ReflectionProperty::getAttributes(Url::class)` returns a
  non-empty array when the attribute is present — the standard
  reflection-based structural test shape.
- **The AC's "stub setScope/setTab methods that assign the property"
  is a minimum-viable body pattern.** No validation, no side effects,
  no notification firing. Just `$this->scope = $scope;`. The
  autopilot's "build now, wire later" pattern (established across
  many prior series) means the wiring/UX polish comes in follow-up
  stories; US-002's job is the skeleton class + panel registration
  + reflection-testable shape.

### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`)
- **Modified** `src/Pages/ActivityFeed.php` (+7 imports +
  `getActivities(): LengthAwarePaginator` public method +
  `recordableTypeMap(): array` private helper)
- **Added** `tests/Feature/ActivityFeedGetActivitiesTest.php` (9 tests
  covering AC bullets a–f + composition)

### Learnings for future iterations
- **Testing paginator behavior via a bare `new ActivityFeed;` works
  fine.** No need for `newInstanceWithoutConstructor()` when the page's
  public properties are directly settable. Filament's Page base class
  has no constructor-invoked side effects that would break a bare `new`;
  the Livewire mount lifecycle is a separate concern that isn't
  exercised by calling `getActivities()` directly. This is a lighter-
  weight test pattern than the hot-patch anonymous-subclass approach
  used elsewhere (e.g. ClickSendIntegrationPageTest) — it works when the
  method under test doesn't call `$this->form->getState()` or other
  Livewire-mount-dependent helpers.
- **The recordable type map deliberately mirrors LogsCrmActivity's
  contract**, not a Filament resource's slug scheme. The trait at
  `src/Concerns/LogsCrmActivity.php:16-35` writes activity rows with
  `recordable_type => $child->getMorphClass()` where `$child` is a Note
  / Task / Call / Meeting / Lunch / File model. Core CRM doesn't call
  `Relation::enforceMorphMap()`, so the morph_type column stores the
  raw FQCN. The map's values must be the exact FQCNs
  (`Note::class` etc.) — matching against a bare short name or a
  Filament slug would silently return zero rows. Always cross-reference
  the trait's write path when building a query that filters on a
  polymorphic `_type` column.
- **`ActivityFeed::getActivities()` uses `$this->tab`/`$this->scope`
  directly rather than reading `$data`** as some earlier Filament pages
  do. The two properties are Livewire `#[Url]`-attributed (from US-002
  of this series), so their state is automatically hydrated from the
  query string on mount and re-synchronised on `wire:model.live`
  updates. No `getState()` call is needed — the property IS the source
  of truth. Simpler than the form-based state pattern used by
  GeneralSettings / Reminders / ClickSendIntegration (which need
  `$this->form->getState()` to read multi-field forms), but only works
  when the state surface is small (2 scalars here).
- **Seeding activity fixtures via `Activity::create([...])` in tests
  bypasses the `LogsCrmActivity` trait's semantics** — the trait's job
  is to write activity rows on child creates via a RelationManager's
  `->after()` callback, but tests can insert rows directly. Just
  provide the required morph columns (`causeable_type/id`,
  `recordable_type/id`, and optionally `timelineable_type/id`) plus the
  minimum non-null columns (`external_id`, `log_name`, `event`).
  Faster than exercising the full trait path and independent of any
  parent Eloquent record.

### Files changed (in `/Users/andrewdrake/Packages/laravel-crm-filament`)
- **Added** `resources/views/activity-feed.blade.php`
- **Modified** `resources/views/crm-activity.blade.php` (dual-mode:
  single-item render when `isset($activity)`, legacy iteration mode
  when called without variables — preserves all 6 per-type partial
  includes verbatim)
- **Added** `tests/Feature/ActivityFeedBladeViewTest.php`

### Learnings for future iterations
- **The AC's "reuse the `crm-activity` wrapper" combined with
  "@include crm-activity with per-row variables" implies modifying
  the existing view to support dual-mode operation, NOT creating a
  new sibling partial.** The current codebase had `crm-activity`
  designed as a full iteration container bound to a
  `RelationManager` (calling `$this->getOwnerRecord()
  ->timelineActivities()`). Making it work with per-row includes
  requires either (a) a new single-item partial (AC forbids) OR
  (b) making the existing view branch on `isset($activity)`.
  Option (b) is the right read of the AC's intent. The branch
  cost is minimal (a top-level `@if / @else`) and both callers
  (the new page + existing RMs) work correctly. Apply this pattern
  whenever an AC says "reuse existing partial but add new variables"
  — dual-mode via `isset()` is the cheapest defensible shape.
- **`ucfirst($t)` as a tab label fallback** is appropriate when
  the AC names tab identifiers (like `'notes'`, `'tasks'`) that
  don't have dedicated translation keys. The alternative would be
  to add 7 more translation keys (`labels.misc.all`, `.notes`,
  etc.) — but the AC didn't call this out, and `ucfirst` produces
  readable English titles ("All", "Notes", "Tasks", etc.) that
  match visitor expectations. Worth flagging as a future
  translation follow-up story if any host wants the tab labels
  in French/Spanish; for now, `ucfirst` is defensible.
- **A `toContain($needle, $message)` call in Pest v3+ treats the
  second argument as ANOTHER needle**, not as a description
  message.** Same gotcha noted many times across the codebase
  (v0.x US-001 of the parity-series-continuation for
  `LeadResourceRouteBindingTest`). The right Pest v3 shape for a
  descriptive assertion is a bare `expect(...)->toContain($needle)`
  — descriptive context lives in the `it('describes what')` string
  wrapping the assertion. Cost me one debug cycle before I noticed
  the failure output was echoing the second needle back at me.
- **A blade view's `@include` variables aren't inherited from the
  parent scope automatically** — in Blade, the `@include` directive
  creates a new scope and only the explicit `['x' => $y, ...]`
  array is passed through. The existing `crm-activity` view had
  `$activity` as a `@forelse` loop variable, but the new dual-mode
  branch reads `$activity` as a passed-in variable. Both work
  because `@include(..., ['activity' => $activity, 'last' => $loop->last])`
  populates the child scope's `$activity` even when the parent
  has its own `$activity` at that point. Verified via the
  regression test on legacy RelationManager consumers (all
  50 tests green post-refactor).

  `canCreate(): bool` override so the two "sidebar suppression" declarations

- `getPages()` entries preserved verbatim on every resource: `view`
  routes stay registered for RelationManagers' open-parent deep-links
  (via `Concerns\StandaloneActivityResource::openParentAction()`) AND
  FileResource's temporaryUrl download closure. CallResource's `kanban`
  route continues to register alongside `index` + `view` — confirmed

  file paths, checks each for existing `shouldRegisterNavigation`
  (idempotency), locates the `canCreate` anchor block, and inserts the
